You spend a day copying the couriers' schedule into your travel book. The record is yours now, though it cost you a day of the road.
ev.ev_cambaluc_entry.choice_1_result: The clerks of the shìbó sī write your cargo into the great register and hand you the tally. As you turn from the table, a clerk of the relay stations rises to ask a word with you.
ev.ev_cambaluc_entry.choice_2_result: The men of Cambaluc answer you freely, for the city is proud of its size and its roads. Their answers are many and different, and one of them follows you out of the gate to give you the truer account.
ev.ev_cambaluc_entry.choice_3_result: You spend a day walking the great market of Cambaluc and carry away a load of goods. The market of the Great Kaan's city is now written in your book.
ev.ev_cambaluc_mentor_followup.body: The chronologer of the Astronomical Bureau does not let you leave with only his lessons. He draws the yarrow-stalks once more, this time for the road ahead of you, and reads what season it will be open and where a man must stand when he chooses it. Then he sets the reading down between you and leaves the rest to your choosing.
ev.ev_cambaluc_mentor_followup.choice_1: Take his parting notes on reading a road by time and position
ev.ev_cambaluc_mentor_followup.choice_1_: The notes are plain and exact, like the man himself. What you learned at the Bureau is now written where you can consult it on the road.
ev.ev_cambaluc_mentor_followup.choice_2: Ask which road the hexagrams show to be open in the season ahead
ev.ev_cambaluc_mentor_followup.choice_2_: The chronologer reads the hexagrams and names the road south, the road by which the Kaan's envoys ride to Kinsay. The way is now clear in your mind, and you know the season in which to take it.
ev.ev_cambaluc_mentor_followup.choice_3: Linger a day at the Bureau to learn the reading of the seasons
ev.ev_cambaluc_mentor_followup.choice_3_: You spend a day among the Bureau's instruments, learning how the year is read and the roads ordered. It costs you time, but the hexagrams now have a reader who knows where he stands.
ev.ev_cambaluc_mentor_followup.title: Cambaluc: The Chronologer's Parting Hexagram
ev.ev_cambaluc_mentor_iching.choice_1_re: The chronologer of the Astronomical Bureau takes your fee and opens his hand. The fourteen days' teaching begins with the first cast, and before you leave he has a parting hexagram to lay before you.
ev.ev_cambaluc_mentor_iching.choice_2_re: The chronologer shows how each hexagram names a turn in the road. The six-and-forty signs are now written in your book, though their reading stays with him.
ev.ev_campichu_a.choice_1_result: You watch the governor's clerks at their tally. It costs you 1 day on the road. The account is written down before the hour turns. The road to Caracoron opens on your map.
ev.ev_campichu_a.choice_2_result: You bargain with desert caravans for tea. You pay 6000 coins. You add 1 item to your stores. You set what you saw into your travel book.
ev.ev_campichu_a.choice_3_result: You pass through the government quarter without delay. The road to Etzina opens on your map. Fortune bends a little your way.
ev.ev_campichu_a_followup.body: In the capital of Tangut a clerk of the governor's court who has sealed caravan papers for twenty years draws you from the market into a side room. He says Caracoron and Etzina are not merely names on a map — they are the measure of how far a Tangut passport will carry you before the desert takes over.
ev.ev_campichu_a_followup.choice_1: Ask him to seal a note naming the road to Caracoron
ev.ev_campichu_a_followup.choice_1_resul: Caracoron is marked on your map with the clerk's seal beside it. The northern road is no longer a rumour.
ev.ev_campichu_a_followup.choice_2: Buy a chest of tea at the court caravan price
ev.ev_campichu_a_followup.choice_2_resul: You leave with tea at a price the desert caravans accept. The chest is sealed for the next march.
ev.ev_campichu_a_followup.choice_3: Wait a day for the passport office to open again
ev.ev_campichu_a_followup.choice_3_resul: You wait a day for the office. The waiting costs time, but Etzina is named before you go.
ev.ev_campichu_a_followup.title: Campichu: The Tangut Seat's Second Counsel
ev.ev_campichu_b.choice_1_result: You enter one of the three Christian churches. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again. You set what you saw into your travel book. Your name carries a little more weight here now.
ev.ev_campichu_b.choice_2_result: You walk the idol abbeys and note their gilded figures. The account is written down before the hour turns. The road to Egrigaia opens on your map. Fortune bends a little your way.
ev.ev_campichu_b.choice_3_result: You leave a small offering at an abbey gate. You pay 500 coins. Your name carries a little more weight here now. You set what you saw into your travel book.
ev.ev_campichu_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through the gate without delay. The road to Campichu opens on your map.
ev.ev_campichu_entry.choice_2_result: You walk through the market. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again. You set what you saw into your travel book. You set the way to Campichu on your map.
ev.ev_campichu_entry.choice_3_result: You enter the sì and bow before the painted scrolls. The monks remember your courtesy, and the scent of incense lingers in your sleeves. You set the road to Campichu on your map.
ev.ev_camul_a.choice_1_result: You walk the gardens with Nuri’s brother. By evening both families have agreed on a shorter turn and he moves the gate as promised. You write down how the channels are shared and spend the day in Hami.
ev.ev_camul_a.choice_2_result: You pay 0.6 silver for a slice, eat it beside the baskets, and feel refreshed. Nuri wraps the remaining pieces for the children while the two families settle their water turn.
ev.ev_camul_a.choice_3_result: The drivers point out the roads toward Lop and Suzhou, then show where each party usually fills its water skins. You mark the two places on your map.
ev.ev_camul_a_followup.body:
At Nuri’s stall, she and her brother are tying a full merchant load of melons for the next caravan. The neighbours have finished their water turn, and the child who carried the cut melon is drawing small marks on each basket so her mother can identify her family’s share. Nuri checks each knot before the driver loads it.

‘You used to mix these baskets up,’ Nuri tells the child. ‘I can read the marks now,’ the girl replies. You ask where the caravan will go. The driver names Lop and Suzhou and shows a worn list of wells; another party is waiting for news from Etzina. Nuri says the full load is available for 108 silver. The driver warns that this is trade cargo, not a snack for the road.

The child hands her mother’s basket over first. You can buy Nuri’s merchant lot, ask her and the driver to go through the wells with you, or stay a day for the eastbound party to arrive and ask them about Etzina.
ev.ev_camul_a_followup.choice_1: Buy the full merchant load for 108 silver
ev.ev_camul_a_followup.choice_1_result: You pay 108 silver for the full load. Nuri’s brother counts the baskets with you and the driver makes room for them. You write down the water turns and packing method you learned, ready for the next desert stretch.
ev.ev_camul_a_followup.choice_2: Ask them to name the wells toward Lop and Suzhou
ev.ev_camul_a_followup.choice_2_result: Nuri holds the paper while the driver names the usable wells toward Lop and Suzhou. You mark both destinations and record where a party can refill before crossing the dry ground.
ev.ev_camul_a_followup.choice_3: Wait a day for the eastbound party
ev.ev_camul_a_followup.choice_3_result: You wait through the next day. The arriving driver tells you what he saw toward Etzina, and Nuri shares tea while you draw that place on your map. The girl asks him whether he noticed her basket marks on the road.
ev.ev_camul_a_followup.title: Nuri’s Packed Melons
ev.ev_camul_b.choice_1_result: You stay through the day. The keeper explains where he learned the old story and how his family looks after travellers now. His nephew finishes mending the mat and invites you to sit; you record their account.
ev.ev_camul_b.choice_2_result: You watch the gathering without interrupting. The woman brings her father another cup of tea and thanks you for moving his stool; the keepers remember your courtesy. You note what you saw in the courtyard.
ev.ev_camul_b.choice_3_result: The keeper spends the day asking a returning driver about water and shelter toward Etzina. He then tells you what the driver knows, and you mark Etzina on your map.
ev.ev_camul_entry.choice_1_result: The girl shows you the newly marked water skin before you leave. You mark Hami on your map and continue with your own water checked.
ev.ev_camul_entry.choice_2_result: You spend a day at the market. The seller tells you how water reaches the gardens; drivers tell you where they stop between the oasis and the desert. You record what you learn and mark Hami on your map.
ev.ev_camul_entry.choice_3_result: You visit the place of worship and speak with the people who sweep its courtyard. One of them guides you back to the main lane; you mark Hami on your map, and the family remembers that you came respectfully.
ev.ev_caracoron_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through without stopping. The road to Caracoron opens on your map.
ev.ev_caracoron_entry.choice_2_result: You rest and ask what men say of this place. You set the way to Caracoron on your map. You set what you saw into your travel book. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again.
ev.ev_caracoron_site_gap.choice_1_result: The groom points south across the grassland. “This road leads to Camul, but it is a long way. Go with a pack train that knows where to find water and pasture.”
ev.ev_caracoron_site_gap.choice_2_result: He gives you a few strands. “Twist them one way, then lay the two strands together in the opposite direction. That keeps the cord from unravelling. A little water on your palms helps.”
ev.ev_cascar_a.choice_1_result: You pay 0.5 silver for the melon. Rima’s daughter wraps it with leaves so it will not bruise, then asks her mother to check the channel one last time. You carry the fruit as a small provision.
ev.ev_cascar_a.choice_2_result: You spend the day watching the water pass from the neighbour’s branch to Rima’s younger vines. Her daughter marks the hour with a shadow on the wall. You record what the family showed you; Rima asks you to return when the next parcel of seeds is ready.
ev.ev_cascar_a.choice_3_result: You pay 1 silver for the dried grapes. The daughter checks that the cloth parcel is tied tightly, then gives you the small provision. Rima reminds her to put the next basket back in the shade.
ev.ev_cascar_a_followup.body:
Rima calls you back to the orchard when her daughter is sorting melon seeds for the next planting. The girl has mixed two dried batches in one bowl. ‘I marked the cloths, not the seeds,’ she admits. Rima asks her to look at their size before giving up. The neighbour who shares the water channel brings a handful from his own crop so they have something to compare.

You ask whether the varieties come from the same valley. Rima says one was brought by a driver from farther west, though she knows it now by the taste of its fruit. The neighbour talks about the mountain road to Badakhshan where his brother once carried grafts. The daughter asks him which trees survived the trip. ‘The ones he wrapped well,’ he says, showing her a folded leaf.

Rima cuts a melon she had saved for the family and offers you a piece. Her daughter spreads the seeds in two lines on clean cloth, ready to hear your guess before she checks the old labels.
ev.ev_cascar_a_followup.choice_1: Accept the melon and hear how Rima kept its seed
ev.ev_cascar_a_followup.choice_1_result: Rima gives you a generous piece of melon, and her daughter compares its fresh seeds with the two dried lines. She can now separate the batches by herself. You carry away a small fruit provision and note the family’s method.
ev.ev_cascar_a_followup.choice_2: Ask the neighbour about the Badakhshan road
ev.ev_cascar_a_followup.choice_2_result: The neighbour names the places where his brother watered the grafts on the road toward Badakhshan. Rima’s daughter writes them on the old seed label so the story stays with the batch. You mark Badakhshan on your map.
ev.ev_cascar_a_followup.choice_3: Help the daughter sort seed for the neighbours
ev.ev_cascar_a_followup.choice_3_result: You help divide the seeds into labelled cloth packets. The neighbour takes his share, and Rima’s daughter keeps the remaining two rows apart this time. The family thanks you for staying until the work is done.
ev.ev_cascar_a_followup.title: Rima’s Seed Packet
ev.ev_cascar_b.choice_1_result: You pay 116 silver for Saliha’s finished carpet. Her brother rolls it carefully, making sure the narrow corner faces out so she can check it once more. The full trading carpet joins your cargo.
ev.ev_cascar_b.choice_2_result: You spend the day at Saliha’s bench. She has you try the corner on a scrap while her brother counts the turns aloud. By evening you know why their family keeps that small change in the border, and you put the lesson in your notes.
ev.ev_cascar_b.choice_3_result: You pay 1.5 silver for the packet of dye samples. The aunt labels each small portion before handing it over, and Saliha warns you to keep the indigo wrapped separately. You leave with a portable sample of the family’s work.
ev.ev_cascar_b_followup.body:
Saliha’s aunt invites you into the dye yard, where her nephew is holding three sample threads against the light. He says the blue has dried darker than he expected. His aunt asks whether he compared it before or after washing. ‘Before,’ he says. She hands him a clean bowl and tells him to wet the thread, then wait. Saliha calls from the loom that a buyer wants another finished carpet, and the aunt has one prepared for 116 silver.

You ask how they decide which colour belongs in the narrow border. The aunt says Saliha decides after seeing the whole field of the carpet. A trader from Yarcan has brought a mineral pigment she wants to examine, though he cannot stay past tomorrow. The nephew asks whether he may try it on a scrap. His aunt agrees if he marks the source first, so nobody later mistakes it for their usual dye.

Saliha brings the carpet into the courtyard. The wet blue sample dries beside the new mineral colour, and her aunt asks what difference you see.
ev.ev_cascar_b_followup.choice_1: Buy the finished carpet for 116 silver
ev.ev_cascar_b_followup.choice_1_result: You pay 116 silver for the other finished carpet. Saliha rolls the full trading piece and ties on a tag naming the colours she used. Her brother carries it to your load while the aunt checks the next dye bath.
ev.ev_cascar_b_followup.choice_2: Ask the pigment trader about Yarcan
ev.ev_cascar_b_followup.choice_2_result: The pigment trader describes Yarcan, its market, and the road on which he brought the mineral. The nephew writes the place on his sample cloth; you mark Yarcan in your map. Saliha asks him to keep the wet and dry tests side by side until morning.
ev.ev_cascar_b_followup.choice_3: Spend a day testing the border colours
ev.ev_cascar_b_followup.choice_3_result: You spend the day at the dye yard. The aunt has you compare each thread after washing and drying; Saliha chooses the colour once the whole border is in view. You record the lesson, and the nephew keeps his labelled sample for the next order.
ev.ev_cascar_b_followup.title: The Aunt’s Dye Samples
ev.ev_cascar_c.choice_1_result: You sit with the neighbour while he tells the story he learned at home. Mariam’s son asks which names belong to which telling, and the neighbour patiently repeats them. The people at the cave remember that you listened with respect.
ev.ev_cascar_c.choice_2_result: The traveller tells you the version her father passed on, including the old coin carried to a baker after the long sleep. Mariam’s son wants to know what the coin looked like; the traveller says her father never told her. She thanks you for asking and hopes you will carry the account onward.
ev.ev_cascar_c.choice_3_result: You stay a full night by the cave and help Mariam sweep in the morning. The two visitors talk until their lamps burn low, and her son finally falls asleep against the wall. At dawn he asks you which part you remember best; you answer while he gathers the last wicks.
ev.ev_cascar_c_followup.body:
The morning after your night at the cave, Mariam’s son has two scraps of paper on his knee. The Muslim neighbour wrote one set of names, and the Christian traveller wrote another. ‘Which one should go on the wall?’ the boy asks. Mariam tells him to ask whether either guest wants their paper displayed. Both would rather keep the sheets for visitors to read at the table, where they can answer questions.

You ask the traveller where she learned the story. Her father heard it on the eastward road, she says, and she can name the oasis of Khotan where they once stopped. The neighbour asks whether that was before or after a hard winter; the traveller cannot remember, but she recalls his hands around a warm cup as he told it. Mariam puts the papers in a small box so the lamps cannot singe them.

The boy wants to copy both lists neatly. The traveller also offers to show you the road she knows. Mariam says anyone who stays another day can help make a safe shelf for the box.
ev.ev_cascar_c_followup.choice_1: Help the boy copy both lists
ev.ev_cascar_c_followup.choice_1_result: You help the boy copy both lists. He puts the names on separate sheets and leaves space below each for the visitors’ own explanations. Mariam places them in the box, and you note how the two accounts were told.
ev.ev_cascar_c_followup.choice_2_result: The traveller tells you about Khotan and the resting places her family used on that road. The boy adds the city’s name to the back of her paper, and you mark Khotan on your map. Mariam closes the box before the first visitors arrive.
ev.ev_cascar_c_followup.choice_3: Stay a day and make a shelf for the papers
ev.ev_cascar_c_followup.choice_3_result: You stay a day helping Mariam fix a shelf away from the lamps. Her son tests it with the box before putting both stories inside. The two visitors thank you, and the cave’s papers will be easier for others to read safely.
ev.ev_cascar_c_followup.title: Names Told at the Cave
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_a.body:
Tariq catches up with you after your days at the relay. He has tied a fresh cord for a driver who has never taken the northern stage. ‘The last knot is where his cousin will meet him,’ he says, ‘but I only heard the place from my father.’ The driver asks whether that is enough to trust. Tariq says it is enough to ask another person, and takes the cord back rather than send him out with a guess.

You ask who keeps the next station. The yard clerk comes over with a name and shows the driver a mark that the keeper uses on receipts. Tariq repeats it aloud. A fruit seller nearby says she saw the cousin last month, repairing a harness by the water trough. The driver wants to write a short note so the cousin knows when to expect him.

Tariq asks whether you will carry a copy of the cord’s marks. The clerk puts paper on the table; she can help check every knot against the names before anyone leaves.
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_a.choice_1: Take a checked copy of the relay cord
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_a.choice_1_resu: You take a copy of the knots and ask Tariq who will recognise each mark. He and the clerk name the station keepers in order. The driver writes his note to the cousin, and Tariq says he will come back when the names are set out clearly.
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_a.choice_2: Leave the cord with Tariq and the driver
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_a.choice_2_resu: You thank Tariq and let him finish the cord with the driver. The clerk checks the last mark before they tie it off. When you leave, the driver is already repeating his cousin’s name without looking at the paper.
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_a.title: Tariq’s Last Knot
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_a_resolution.bo:
Tariq returns with the checked cord and a narrow strip of paper. His father has written the station names beside each knot. ‘He corrected my count,’ Tariq admits, showing you where one short stage was missing. The driver asked him not to erase the old mark; it will remind them both why the route had to be checked.

You ask whether the cord will survive rain. Tariq dips one end in a bowl, then lays it in the sun. The knots stay firm, while his paper curls. The clerk says to keep the names inside a dry book and use the cord outside. The driver sends word that his cousin will indeed be at the last station.

Tariq offers you the spare copy. If you leave soon, he can pass your name ahead. If you have a day, he will teach you to make the same knots and write the station names in your own hand.
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_a_resolution.ch: Let Tariq send your name ahead
Tariq hands the checked cord to the outgoing rider with your name attached. The clerk reads it once more before the rider leaves. Your introduction now travels ahead to the next relay.
Stay a day and copy the station names

You spend the day making knots and writing the station names. Tariq checks the short stage that he once missed; you have it in the right place. The clerk gives you a dry sleeve for the paper when the lesson is done.
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_b.body:
After your day in Tariq’s garden, a dyer named Amina comes looking for you. She heard that his father blamed a late water turn for a pale patch on the vines. ‘My sister says the channel was clear that day,’ Amina tells you. ‘If the water arrived late, the gate farther up must have been held closed.’ She asks Tariq to bring his father’s note so they can put the days in order.

You ask why the timing matters to her dye work. Amina uses the same channel for rinsing wool after the orchards have taken their share. If the turn changes, she must keep the wet bundles another night. Tariq arrives with his father’s note: he had mixed the day of the pale patch with the day the neighbour repaired the stone. Amina laughs at herself for nearly doing the same.

She sketches the water turns on a piece of cloth and asks whether you want to carry the corrected account. Her sister can still add the precise hour when she returns from the washing yard.
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_b.choice_1: Wait for Amina’s sister and take the corrected account
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_b.choice_1_resu: You ask Amina to wait for her sister’s account. The sister returns with the hour she marked on a jar, and the two women correct the cloth drawing together. Amina promises to give you a clean copy after the wool is rinsed.
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_b.choice_2: Leave the water-turn account with the dyers
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_b.choice_2_resu: You tell Amina the account will be most useful beside her washing yard. She agrees and pins the cloth where her sister can see it. Tariq takes the corrected date back to his father before the next water turn begins.
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_b.title: The Dyer’s Question
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_b_resolution.bo:
Amina brings you a clean list after the wool has dried. Her sister has checked the hours against the jar marks, and Tariq’s father has added the orchard’s next turn. ‘I used to keep all this in my head,’ Amina says. ‘Then my nephew began helping at the dye vats, and I had to explain it so he would know when to draw water.’ The nephew is behind her, reading the list aloud to prove he understands.

You ask whether the water schedule changes in winter. It does, she says, and she has left a blank line for that. Tariq’s father will write again when the season turns. Her nephew points out a smudge on the lower edge; Amina dries it with a cloth rather than rub it away.

She slides a copy toward you. Her nephew keeps his finger on the first line and asks whether he should read it aloud once more.

The sister arrives with a rinsed bundle under one arm and checks the copied hour against the mark on her jar. She points out one line where the nephew has written the time too small; he makes the letters larger before handing you the page.
ev.ev_cascar_consequence_b_resolution.ch: Carry the corrected water list to other travellers
You take Amina’s clean copy. Her nephew reads the first line once more, and she lets him write the family name beneath it. The corrected schedule is now in your care for the road.
Spend a day checking the channel turns

You spend the day following the channel between orchard and washing yard. Amina’s nephew marks each turn as it arrives; by evening he can tell his aunt when the next rinse will begin. You copy the list into your travel book.
ev.ev_cascar_entry.choice_1_result: You spend two days comparing cords and pack marks with the clerk. Tariq finds the slipped knot and keeps his father’s cloth out of the animal tally. You add Kashgar to your notes and map. He comes to find you again when the next relay hands in its cord.
ev.ev_cascar_entry.choice_2_result: Tariq takes you into his family’s garden for the day. His father explains which water turn keeps the vines alive, and Tariq shows you how they mark the baskets for market. You record the visit; by evening a dyer from the weaving quarter asks whether you heard the same story she did.
ev.ev_cascar_entry.choice_3_result: You inspect the merchant’s sealed jade lot and pay 135 silver. He waits a day to have the transfer entered properly, then loads the goods with yours. Tariq moves the melon crate aside so your pack animal can pass.
ev.ev_cascar_mentor_followup.body:
On your return, Habib has spread his cloth map across the bench. The young carrier has come back from the first station and says the repaired trough held water. ‘Did you drink there?’ Habib asks. ‘We filled the skins and let the animals rest,’ the carrier replies. Tariq marks the report on his cord, careful to distinguish what the carrier saw from what another driver told him.

You ask about the western road to Samarkand. Habib traces it with a finger, stopping where several wells are close together. He says caravan leaders sometimes argue over which one to use, but the decision depends on the season and the loads. The carrier admits he would have chosen the nearest without looking at the animals.

Habib takes a spare knotted cord from the bench. Tariq brings a clean cup and moves it away from the map before the tea is poured.
ev.ev_cascar_mentor_followup.choice_1_re: Habib ties the spare cord to your wrist and has you name the first two stations. The young carrier supplies the third from his new memory. You carry their introduction to the relay with you.
ev.ev_cascar_mentor_followup.choice_2: Ask Habib to trace the Samarkand road
ev.ev_cascar_mentor_followup.choice_2_re: Habib traces the westward road toward Samarkand, marking the wells he has checked this season. Tariq copies the names onto your paper. You add Samarkand to your map, and the carrier asks for a copy as well.
ev.ev_cascar_mentor_followup.choice_3: Stay a day comparing the drivers’ reports
ev.ev_cascar_mentor_followup.choice_3_re: You spend a day sorting reports by who saw each stop and when. Habib has you ask the carrier again about the repaired trough, and his answer stays the same. Tariq marks the account cleanly; you leave with a clearer way to compare road news.
ev.ev_cascar_mentor_followup.title: Habib’s Cloth Map
ev.ev_chamba_a.choice_1_result: You hear the full tale of how the elephant tribute was settled. The account is written down before the hour turns. The road to Zayton opens on your map. Fortune bends a little your way.
ev.ev_chamba_a.choice_2_result: You watch a day upon the harbour while tribute goods are tallied. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again. You set the way to Pentam on your map. You set what you saw into your travel book.
ev.ev_chamba_a.choice_3_result: You buy sandalwood from the tribute quarter. You pay 900 coins. You add 1 item to your stores. The tribute clerks set your name beside the ledger of gifts.
ev.ev_chamba_a_followup.body: When the clerks have finished counting the elephant tribute, a harbour pilot who has sailed the tribute ships to Zayton draws you onto the mole. He says Chamba's wealth is not only ivory — it is the sea road west-south-west of Zayton, and the names of Pentam and Fuju if you mean to follow the Kaan's ships home.
ev.ev_chamba_a_followup.choice_1: Buy sandalwood at the tribute harbour price
ev.ev_chamba_a_followup.choice_1_result: He sells you sandalwood sealed for the next monsoon. The scent stays in the hold.
ev.ev_chamba_a_followup.choice_2: Ask him to mark the sea road toward Zayton
ev.ev_chamba_a_followup.choice_2_result: Zayton is marked on your map with the monsoon days between. The tribute road is clear.
ev.ev_chamba_a_followup.choice_3: Watch the tribute harbour a day and hear the pilots' talk
ev.ev_chamba_a_followup.choice_3_result: You spend a day on the mole. Pentam is named in the talk, and fortune bends a little your way.
ev.ev_chamba_a_followup.title: Chamba: After the Elephant Tribute
ev.ev_chamba_b.choice_1_result: You wait two days upon the harbour to hear word of the King's court. You spend 2 days before the way is clear again. You set what you saw into your travel book. Your name carries a little more weight here now.
ev.ev_chamba_b.choice_2_result: You buy pepper from the spice merchants. You pay 8000 coins. You add 1 item to your stores. The account is written down before the hour turns.
ev.ev_chamba_b.choice_3_result: You ask the mariners how many days' sail lie to Zayton and Fuzhou. You set the way to Zayton on your map. You set the way to Fuju on your map. You set what you saw into your travel book.
ev.ev_chamba_b_followup.body: At the court in Chamba, a pepper broker leads you from the audience into the shade of the quay sheds. “Elephants go to the Great Khan as tribute,” he says, “but pepper goes to the passing ships.” He opens his monsoon book and points to a ship leaving soon for Fuju. If you mean to send goods with it, he advises you to decide before it sails.
ev.ev_chamba_b_followup.choice_1: Buy pepper at the court broker's price
ev.ev_chamba_b_followup.choice_1_result: He sells you pepper sealed for the monsoon. The price is the court's own list.
ev.ev_chamba_b_followup.choice_2: Ask which sea road leads toward Fuju
ev.ev_chamba_b_followup.choice_2_result: Fuju is marked on your map. The sea road north is clear.
ev.ev_chamba_b_followup.choice_3: Visit the court a day and hear the king's sea talk
ev.ev_chamba_b_followup.choice_3_result: You spend a day at court. The king's talk names the islands, and fortune bends a little your way.
ev.ev_chamba_b_followup.title: Chamba: The Idolater Court and the Pepper Quay
ev.ev_chamba_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through the gate without delay. The road to Chamba opens on your map.
ev.ev_chamba_entry.choice_2_result: You walk through the harbour market. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again. You set what you saw into your travel book. You set the way to Chamba on your map.
ev.ev_chamba_entry.choice_3_result: You climb to the masjid above the roofs. The elders take your greeting and give their names in turn, and their blessing rides down the hill with you. The road to Chamba is now drawn on your map.
ev.ev_chandu_a.choice_1_result: The guards take your silver and look the other way, and you step inside the gilded cane palace. The light is all gold and green, and the walls give gently as you pass, as if the building itself were breathing.
ev.ev_chandu_a.choice_2_result: You stand in the meadow outside the palace and admire its gilded roof against the sky. The Kaan's pleasure palace is now marked in your book.
ev.ev_chandu_a.choice_3_result: You spend a day sketching the palace in detail. The lines of the roof and the garden are now set down in your book, as no other traveller has them.
ev.ev_chandu_a_followup.body: You stand at last inside the gilded cane palace of the Great Kaan, and the keeper of the building, a man of the household, comes to your side. The whole palace, he tells you, is held together by silk alone — every column and roof-beam lashed with cords dyed in the Kaan's colours. You ask why a sovereign who commands marble from half Asia should raise his summer seat of hollow cane. The keeper answers that the astrologers of the court read the sky when the palace was first planned, and they declared that the trees of the park would die within the Kaan's own lifetime, and that no fixed palace could stand long among dead groves. So the Kaan commanded a house that could be unbound and carried wherever he chose to hold his court; when he travels, the silk cords are loosed, the gilded columns laid down, and the whole palace moves with him on the backs of camels, to be re-lashed at the next camp. He shows you the lacquered dragon columns, the gilded roof, the marble floors that reflect the ceiling, and he says that the palace is never empty long, for the Kaan returns with the summer. You look at the silk bindings with new eyes: a building that is not nailed together is a building that is never abandoned.
ev.ev_chandu_a_followup.choice_1: Ask the keeper why the palace is built to move
ev.ev_chandu_a_followup.choice_1_result: The keeper explains that the astrologers of the court read the sky when the palace was planned, and declared that no fixed house could stand among trees that were doomed to die. The silk cords and gilded columns are the Kaan's answer: a palace that can move is a palace that cannot be left in a dead grove.
ev.ev_chandu_a_followup.choice_2: Ask where the cane and the silk come from by road
ev.ev_chandu_a_followup.choice_2_result: The keeper names the road south, through the cane country of Manzi, by which the gilded bamboo and the silk come up to Chandu. The road to Cacanfu is now on your map, and you know where the lightest palace in the world is born.
ev.ev_chandu_a_followup.choice_3: Stay a day to watch the palace re-bound for the Kaan's travel
ev.ev_chandu_a_followup.choice_3_result: You stay a day in the palace while the cords are loosed and the columns laid down, as though the whole gilded house were a tent. The keeper lets you watch the binding, and you carry away a knowledge of how the Kaan's palace travels that no book would have given you.
ev.ev_chandu_a_followup.title: Chandu: The Palace That Moves
ev.ev_chandu_b.choice_1_result: You spend much of the day walking along the park's sixteen-mile wall. Deer, peacocks and hunting dogs have their own enclosures. A keeper guides you and warns, “Stay on the path; do not startle the hawks.”
ev.ev_chandu_b.choice_2_result: You find a gap in the wall and watch the sacred white mares, whose milk only the Kaan and his kin may drink. The sight is now marked in your book.
ev.ev_chandu_b.choice_3_result: You hire a falconer who keeps the Kaan's own birds, and you ride out with the hooded gerfalcon on his fist. The master of the mews has chosen his bird and his ground with care, and he means to show you why.
ev.ev_chandu_b_followup.body: You find the falconers' mews along the inner face of the sixteen-mile wall, where the Kaan keeps his hunting birds. There are more than two hundred gerfalcons alone, without reckoning the other hawks, each sitting hooded on its perch; the keepers feed them on the flesh of the game that the Kaan takes in the park. The head falconer, seeing that you are a stranger, sets a hooded gerfalcon on his wrist and speaks of the Kaan's hunts: how he rides the park with a leopard on the croup of his horse, and when he sees an animal that takes his fancy, he slips the leopard at it, and the quarry when taken is made over to feed the hawks in mew. The falconer tells you the art of the hood and the lure, and how a bird is entered to the lure before it is ever flown at game. He speaks also of the road that runs east to the great city of Cambaluc, where the Kaan winters when the grass of the meadow is gone, and he draws in the air the shape of the way — the park wall, the river, the plain. You listen, and the park that seemed only a pleasure-ground begins to look like the frame of a whole empire.
ev.ev_chandu_b_followup.choice_1: Ask the falconer how the Kaan hunts with the leopard
ev.ev_chandu_b_followup.choice_1_result: The falconer tells you how the Kaan slips the leopard from the croup of his horse when a beast takes his fancy, and how the quarry is made over to feed the birds in mew. You understand now why the park is stocked so richly — every hare and stag is meat for the Kaan's hawks.
ev.ev_chandu_b_followup.choice_2: Ask the way the road runs east to Cambaluc
ev.ev_chandu_b_followup.choice_2_result: The falconer draws the road east in the air: past the park wall, over the river, across the plain to the great city of Cambaluc. The way is now clear on your map, and you know the Kaan rides it when the meadow's grass is spent.
ev.ev_chandu_b_followup.choice_3: Stay a day to watch the gerfalcons fed in mew
ev.ev_chandu_b_followup.choice_3_result: You spend a day at the mews while the keepers feed the gerfalcons the flesh of the morning's hunt. You see a hooded bird bated to the lure, and the day costs you something — but you have watched the Kaan's own falconers at their trade.
ev.ev_chandu_b_followup.title: Chandu: The Mews of the Falconers
ev.ev_chandu_c.choice_1_result: You watch the monks milk the white mares at dawn and spill the milk on the ground, as the rite demands. The sacrifice to the sky is now written in your book.
ev.ev_chandu_c.choice_2_result: You pour an offering of wine to the Eternal Blue Sky. The shaman's eyes follow you, and a small favour settles on you like a falling feather.
ev.ev_chandu_c.choice_3_result: You ask a monk what the ceremony means, and he pauses at the brim of the golden vessel. The question is one the monks are used to answering, but he chooses his words as though for the first time.
ev.ev_chandu_c_followup.body: A monk in the meadow says, “Each year the palace offers milk to Eternal Heaven, praying for good pasture and healthy animals. I do not enter the palace every year; this is what the people there have told me.” You may ask what the rite means, hear a story of Chinggis Khan, or remain to watch the morning milking.
ev.ev_chandu_c_followup.choice_1: Ask the monk to tell of Chinghiz Kaan's rise
ev.ev_chandu_c_followup.choice_1_result: The monk tells the tale of Chinghiz Kaan, the herdsman who bound all nations under one sky, and of the oath he swore on the steppe to the spirits of sky and earth. The tale of the first Kaan now goes with you out of the meadow.
ev.ev_chandu_c_followup.choice_2: Ask what the rite asks of the sky and the earth
ev.ev_chandu_c_followup.choice_2_result: The monk explains that the rite of the poured milk asks the sky to keep the grass green and the earth to keep the waters sweet, and that the Kaan pours it in the name of his ancestors. Some of that understanding you take with you, and it will shape the roads you choose.
ev.ev_chandu_c_followup.choice_3: Stay until dawn to watch the mares milked in the first light
ev.ev_chandu_c_followup.choice_3_result: You stay until dawn to watch the white mares milked in the first light, the golden vessels borne to the Kaan's table. It costs you a day of the road, but you have seen the rite that no foreigner was ever permitted to witness.
ev.ev_chandu_c_followup.title: Chandu: The Rite of the White Mares
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_a.body: A groom in the meadow stops you. The court horse trainer is willing to choose a mount for your journey, but first asks how far you will travel and how much baggage you carry. He does not wish to give a good horse to the wrong traveller.
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_a.choice_1: Take the name and ask the stable-hand who can vouch for it
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_a.choice_1_resu: You take the name the stable-hand offers and ask who can vouch for it. He names two grooms of the meadow, and the matter opens again.
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_a.choice_2: Thank the stable-hand and keep your own counsel
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_a.choice_2_resu: You thank the stable-hand and keep your own counsel. The matter closes at the meadow, and nothing more is asked of you in Chandu.
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_a.title: Chandu: The Mark at the Gate
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_a_resolution.bo: You have agreed to carry the horse-master's word with you — a promise, the stable-hand says, that will be honoured on the northern meadow. It will not decide the whole journey, but on the meadow road his word may gain you a mount.
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_a_resolution.ch: You give your word before nightfall. The horse-master's promise now travels with your name, and the meadow folk have a reason to receive you.
Keep the horse-master's promise in your travel book
You keep the horse-master's promise in your travel book and spend a day setting it down plainly. The record is made; the favour waits for a road that may never call on it.
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_b.body: The answer sends a rumour along the road. Before the day is out, a falconer of the court finds you at the meadow with a second account of the summer palace and the meadow — where the mares graze, and which gate the Kaan truly uses. It is less grand than a traveller's tale, and more useful.
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_b.choice_1_resu: You follow the falconer's practical advice and ask him to set it down. He writes the account out for you, and the meadow's true measures come into your hand.
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_b.choice_2: Leave the account with the falconer
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_b.choice_2_resu: You thank the falconer but decline the paper. He folds it into his sleeve and reminds you not to speak of the white-horse meadow near the palace gate.
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_b.title: Chandu: The Road Behind the Answer
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_b_resolution.bo: You have chosen to carry the falconer's account with you — where the mares graze, and which gate the Kaan truly uses. It will not decide the whole journey, but it names the road that will not waste your day.
ev.ev_chandu_consequence_b_resolution.ch: Warn the next rider before nightfall
You warn the next rider before nightfall. The meadow's measures now travel ahead of you, and where they land, your name follows.
Keep the meadow-notes in your travel book
You spend a day copying the meadow-notes into your travel book. The record is yours now, though it cost you a day of the road.
ev.ev_chandu_entry.choice_1_result: The darughachi reads your declaration over twice, then stamps it and waves you toward the meadow gate. As you pass, a stable-hand of the Kaan's meadow detaches himself from the postern to walk with you.
ev.ev_chandu_entry.choice_2_result: The men of Chandu answer your questions with their eyes on the palace roof. Their answers are careful and short, but one of them adds that a truer telling will find you before you leave the meadow.
ev.ev_chandu_entry.choice_3_result: You spend a day in the market of Chandu and carry away a load of goods. The summer capital's trade is now written in your book.
ev.ev_chandu_mentor_followup.body: The trainer takes stable notes and an old relay map from his saddlebag. “The notes show what to look for in a horse's ears, hooves and breathing. The map marks changes of horse on the southern road to Changlu. If you wish to choose a mount yourself, stay with me for a day. Which first?”
ev.ev_chandu_mentor_followup.choice_1: Take the horse-master's notes on the imperial stud
ev.ev_chandu_mentor_followup.choice_1_re: You take the horse-master's notes on the imperial stud, written in a close, plain hand. What you have learned of the white mares and of the reading of horses is now yours to consult on the road.
ev.ev_chandu_mentor_followup.choice_2: Ask which road the couriers ride south to Chinangli
ev.ev_chandu_mentor_followup.choice_2_re: The horse-master traces the courier road south to Chinangli, where the posts change horses at every stage. The road is now drawn on your map, and you know the way the Kaan's own messengers ride.
ev.ev_chandu_mentor_followup.choice_3: Linger a day to learn the horse-master's art
ev.ev_chandu_mentor_followup.choice_3_re: You linger a day at the horse-master's side, learning how a mount is chosen and how a rider's weight is carried. It costs you time, but the art of reading a horse is now partly your own.
ev.ev_chandu_mentor_followup.title: Chandu: The Horse-Master's Parting Gift
ev.ev_charchan_entry.choice_1_result: The boy waves a clean stone as you leave. His aunt reminds you to ask before filling your water skin at the next well. You mark Charchan on your map.
ev.ev_charchan_entry.choice_2_result: You stay a day, watch the aunt sort the stones, and learn which nearby wells carry sweet water. The boy eventually finds one uncracked piece; you write down what they taught you and mark Charchan on your map.
ev.ev_charchan_site_gap.choice_1_result: Aysa names the road to Pein and the wells she trusts along it. You mark both the route and Pein on your map while her brother fills the waiting woman’s jar.
ev.ev_charchan_site_gap.choice_2_result: You try the knot while Aysa holds the bucket. Her brother checks it against the rim; it passes without catching. You record what you learned about the well and its ropes.
ev.ev_chinangli_a.choice_1_result: You walk the quay and count the upstream boats. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again. You set what you saw into your travel book. You set the way to Cambaluc on your map.
ev.ev_chinangli_a.choice_2_result: You buy a bolt of river-traded silk. You pay 10000 coins. You add 1 item to your stores. The road to Cacanfu opens on your map.
ev.ev_chinangli_a.choice_3_result: You ask which spices the downstream boats carry. You set what you saw into your travel book. A small turn of fortune favours you. You set the way to Chandu on your map.
ev.ev_chinangli_a_followup.body: On the quay of the great river a broker who prices silk and spice for boats bound to Cambaluc opens his ledger beside the water. He says the river is a road that remembers every toll — and that a traveller who buys silk without hearing the days to Cacanfu and Chandu rides half-blind upstream.
ev.ev_chinangli_a_followup.choice_1: Buy a bolt of silk at the river ledger price
ev.ev_chinangli_a_followup.choice_1_resu: He sells you silk at a price the upstream markets will recognize. The bolt is sealed for the boat.
ev.ev_chinangli_a_followup.choice_2: Ask him to name the water road toward Cambaluc
ev.ev_chinangli_a_followup.choice_2_resu: Cambaluc and Cacanfu are marked on your map. The river road north is clear.
ev.ev_chinangli_a_followup.choice_3: Spend a day counting spice chests with the clerks
ev.ev_chinangli_a_followup.choice_3_resu: You spend a day among the chests. Chandu is named in the talk, and a small turn of fortune favours you.
ev.ev_chinangli_a_followup.title: Chinangli: The River Brokers' Ledger
ev.ev_chinangli_b.choice_1_result: You watch the paper-money exchange at a stall. It costs you 1 day on the road. The account is written down before the hour turns. The clerk gives you one sample paper note as a record of what you saw.
ev.ev_chinangli_b.choice_2_result: You buy a small porcelain bowl with paper-money. You pay 4000 coins. You add 1 item to your stores. Your name carries a little more weight here now.
ev.ev_chinangli_b.choice_3_result: You ask the exchange clerks how the notes are renewed. The account is written down before the hour turns. Fortune bends a little your way.

ev.ev_chinangli_entry.choice_2_result: You walk through the market. It costs you 1 day on the road. The account is written down before the hour turns. The road to Chinangli opens on your map.
ev.ev_chinangli_entry.choice_3_result: You visit the sì (Buddhist monastery). Your name carries a little more weight here now. You carry away a small sign of the place. You set the way to Chinangli on your map.

ev.ev_cobinan_entry.choice_1_result: The apprentice points out the street beyond the smiths. You mark Cobinan on your map and continue.
ev.ev_cobinan_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day among the workshops, writing down what the metalworkers tell you. Before leaving, you mark Cobinan on your map.

ev.ev_coilum_entry.choice_2_result: You rest and ask what men say of this place. The road to Coilum opens on your map. The account is written down before the hour turns. It costs you 1 day on the road.
ev.ev_coilum_site_gap.choice_1_result: “Follow this coastal road southeast to Maabar,” the weighman says. “Avoid loading at midday; the beach is busiest then.”
ev.ev_coilum_site_gap.choice_2_result: You steady the beam while he resets the weights. Some pepper has clumped at the damp bottom of the sack. He removes it: spices must be kept off the floor on boards, and the warehouse shut at night.
ev.ev_constantinopolis_entry.choice_1_re: Anna calls out the turn toward the market before hurrying after her brother. You mark Constantinople on your map and continue.
ev.ev_constantinopolis_entry.choice_2_re: You spend the day along the harbour and the lodging streets. Anna introduces you to a cloth merchant who crosses into Anatolia and takes the overland road toward Smyrna. You mark Constantinople, Smyrna, and that road on your map.
ev.ev_cotan_a.choice_1_result: You pay 135 silver for the sealed trading lot. Amina wraps its corners again and Yusuf signs the ownership mark before the merchant steps aside. The jade cargo goes with you; the cracked pebble stays on the tray as a lesson for his daughter.
ev.ev_cotan_a.choice_2_result: You spend the day walking the safe shallows with Yusuf and Amina. They show you how a change in current alters the gravel bed; Amina finds the cracked pebble’s matching mark on another stone. You record the river work in your travel book before your feet finally warm.
ev.ev_cotan_a.choice_3_result: The older washer sits beside you and turns each sample toward the light. He does not offer a price until Yusuf has signed off the lot; instead he tells you what he looks for at this river bend. A little later he asks you to come back and help him check a different tray.
ev.ev_cotan_a_followup.body:
The older washer calls you back to the river when Amina brings a second tray of stones. She has marked where each came from with a little strip of reed. Her father Yusuf says the reeds will dry and curl, so she should copy the places before the marks fall off. ‘I can remember them,’ she says. Then she pauses over one pale stone and admits she is no longer sure which bend it came from. The older washer gives her a clean board to write on.

You ask what happens after they sort the river haul. Yusuf says a merchant checks the stone and buys a sealed trading lot if the quality agrees with his order. Another river worker carries goods west toward Yarcan and can tell you where the loads change hands. Amina asks him whether his cart has room for a note to her aunt; he says there is, if she writes the address clearly.

The older washer sits with you while Amina copies her reed marks. He is willing to spend a day showing you the shallows after the next water change, and the carrier waits to explain his westward road.
ev.ev_cotan_a_followup.choice_1: Buy the other sealed jade lot for 135 silver
ev.ev_cotan_a_followup.choice_1_result: The merchant opens a second sealed lot while Amina reads the reed marks on its tag. You inspect the jade and pay 135 silver for the whole trading pack. Yusuf signs the transfer, and the carrier helps you stow it before he takes Amina’s letter west.
ev.ev_cotan_a_followup.choice_2: Ask the carrier about the road to Yarcan
ev.ev_cotan_a_followup.choice_2_result: The carrier names the stops where the river goods change hands on the way to Yarcan. Amina adds her aunt’s address to his letter bundle and checks it with Yusuf. You mark Yarcan on your map before the cart leaves.
ev.ev_cotan_a_followup.choice_3: Stay a day learning how the washers mark the shallows
ev.ev_cotan_a_followup.choice_3_result: You spend the day with the older washer and Amina, comparing her reed marks with the changing riverbank. She corrects the one pale stone’s place on her board. Yusuf thanks you for staying, and the family remembers you at the water’s edge.
ev.ev_cotan_a_followup.title: Amina’s Second Tray
ev.ev_cotan_b.choice_1_result: You pay 100 silver for the completed silk bolt. The aunt checks the roll and ties on a label with your name. Farah keeps working on the unfinished edge while Zuleika helps load the purchased cloth with your goods.
ev.ev_cotan_b.choice_2_result: You spend a day beside the sisters. Farah shows you the edge pattern; Zuleika has you count the shuttle’s passes aloud until you can see where the blue belongs. Their aunt says she will show you the dye yard if you return.
ev.ev_cotan_b.choice_3_result: You pay 1.2 silver for the small labelled samples. The aunt wraps the indigo separately and makes you read the names back before she hands them over. Farah laughs that she wishes her own bobbins were labelled as carefully.
ev.ev_cotan_b_followup.body:
Farah and Zuleika’s aunt invites you back when the first blue edge has come off the loom. She has placed four dyed scraps on a shelf. Zuleika says the safflower red looks faint beside the indigo. Her aunt asks her to move it away from the window and look again. ‘Better?’ she asks. Zuleika admits the sun was passing through the thin cloth and changing what she saw. Farah, still at the loom, calls that she will wait for the new comparison before choosing the next thread.

You ask how dyes reach the workshop. A trader from Kashgar has delivered walnut hulls and will return north after collecting his payment. He tells Farah that her last cloth survived the journey well, though the outer wrapping came loose. Her aunt says she will use a wider knot this time. She has a small labelled dye sample for you if you want to try the colours on your own cloth.

Zuleika asks you to hold the four scraps together while she writes the trader’s name on the wrapping. Farah is ready to teach the rhythm of this edge if you can stay another day.
ev.ev_cotan_b_followup.choice_1_result: The aunt gives you the small dye packet, with indigo wrapped apart from the others. Zuleika reads each label aloud before it goes into your bag. Farah asks her to write the same clear names on the workshop shelf.
ev.ev_cotan_b_followup.choice_2_result: The trader describes the road north to Kashgar and where his last bundle was rewrapped. Farah writes down the place so she can secure the next shipment. You mark Kashgar on your map while Zuleika finishes the new tag.
ev.ev_cotan_b_followup.choice_3: Stay a day and practise the loom rhythm
ev.ev_cotan_b_followup.choice_3_result: You spend the day at the loom. Farah counts the edge pattern slowly and has you repeat it while Zuleika works the shuttle. The aunt checks the finished blue against her scraps; you leave with the sisters’ method in your notes.
ev.ev_cotan_b_followup.title: Auntie’s Colour Shelf
ev.ev_cotan_c.choice_1_result: You spend three days helping Rahman set supports beside the old brick. His mother keeps the children from stepping on the fresh channel edge. When water finally runs safely past, you record the family’s field and the exposed wall in your travel book.
ev.ev_cotan_c.choice_2_result: Rahman’s mother gives you a small painted fragment from her own basket after the children have made a drawing of it. She says its curve may be a hand, or part of a leaf. You wrap it carefully and leave the sound bricks in the wall.
ev.ev_cotan_c.choice_3_result: Rahman’s mother tells you how the old wall has appeared and disappeared under sand during her life. Her youngest child brings a second piece for her to compare. You write down what she knows, and she offers to walk with you along the higher terrace another day.
ev.ev_cotan_c_followup.body:
Rahman’s mother takes you along the upper terrace she mentioned. A wall end appears through the sand beside the path. Her grandson runs ahead with a painted shard and says he found it after yesterday’s wind. She asks him to set it on her palm before he trips over the irrigation ridge. The child asks whether its painted curve matches the one at home. ‘Close enough that we should draw both,’ she says.

You ask where the old path led. She remembers her father describing travellers toward Charchan, though the field walls have shifted since his time. Rahman has brought a spade to clear sand from a blocked channel and says he can show which terrace still carries water. He does not want anyone digging at the exposed wall while the ground beneath it is wet. His mother agrees and moves the children back to a dry place.

She has a loose painted fragment from her own basket to give you after the family records it. Rahman offers to explain the eastern road, or you can stay a day to hear how the terrace changed in his mother’s lifetime.
ev.ev_cotan_c_followup.choice_1: Accept the family’s recorded painted fragment
ev.ev_cotan_c_followup.choice_1_result: The children draw the painted curve before Rahman’s mother gives you the loose fragment. She puts their drawing beside the first one at home. You wrap the piece carefully and leave the sound wall stones in place.
ev.ev_cotan_c_followup.choice_2: Ask Rahman about the road to Charchan
ev.ev_cotan_c_followup.choice_2_result: Rahman tells you where his family has heard travellers bound for Charchan turn east. His mother adds which old field path has disappeared under new channels. You mark Charchan on your map, then help the child step safely over the ridge.
ev.ev_cotan_c_followup.choice_3: Stay a day with the family on the upper terrace
ev.ev_cotan_c_followup.choice_3_result: You stay a day while Rahman clears the channel and his mother tells you how the terrace has changed. The children compare both drawings beside her. When water finally runs through, you record the family’s account in your travel book.
ev.ev_cotan_c_followup.title: Rahman’s Upper Terrace
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_a.body:
The river washer from the entry yard calls you back after a day at Samira’s register. He is Yusuf’s cousin Harun, and he has found that two loads carried the same chalk mark after the rain. ‘One was ours to carry,’ he says. ‘The other belongs to a family across the channel. If a chest goes missing, I do not want them looking in the wrong house.’

You ask whether the family can tell the loads apart. Harun brings out a narrow strip of cloth tied to one handle. Samira’s brother says he saw that strip when the cart first arrived. The other family’s daughter comes over with their own receipt and points to a small tear in the paper. Harun remembers that the cart wheel brushed it against the wall. Their stories fit, but Samira asks them to keep both receipts until the next station has the correct names.

Harun offers to write an introduction to the river carriers who will receive the goods ahead. The daughter asks whether you can help spell her mother’s name on the outside.
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_a.choice_1: Take Harun’s note after checking the names
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_a.choice_1_resul: You check the cloth strip against both receipts and ask Harun who will take the note at the next river yard. He names two carriers; the daughter writes her mother’s name beside theirs. Samira says she will bring the final copy before you leave.
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_a.choice_2_resul: You leave the correction with Samira. Harun and the daughter wait while she copies the two marks into separate lines. Once the ink dries, each family takes back its own receipt, and you continue on your way.
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_a.title: The Washer’s Carrying Mark
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_a_resolution.bod:
Samira brings the finished note to the water yard. Harun has signed beneath his carrying mark, and the daughter has added her mother’s full name. ‘I nearly wrote the short name everyone calls her,’ the girl says. Samira answers, ‘The next station may know a different woman by that name.’ Her brother reads the outside aloud and catches one letter hidden by the fold. Harun unfolds it and writes the letter again.

You ask whether the next carriers will have a way to check the boxes themselves. Harun has put the cloth strip back on the correct handle and copied the tear in the other family’s receipt. The daughter agrees that anyone can now match both loads without guessing. Her mother arrives to see the names and thanks the group for stopping the mistake early.

Samira offers you the note to carry ahead. If you want a day to copy the marks into your own book first, her brother has set out a dry table.
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_a_resolution.cho: You take the corrected note. Harun shows you where the cloth strip is tied; the daughter points to the receipt’s tear once more. You can now hand both names to the next carriers without confusing their loads.
Spend a day copying both cargo marks

You spend the day copying the two receipts and the names on the note. Samira’s brother checks your letters against the originals, and Harun returns the cloth strip to its proper handle. Your book now holds the corrected record.
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_b.body:
After your visit to Samira’s family, a weaver named Farah asks whether you saw the channel by their house. Her aunt has heard that a shallow patch may leave grit in the water used for rinsing silk. ‘The river washer says it looked clear yesterday,’ Farah says, ‘but our new white cloth has a faint line.’ She holds up the edge so you can see it. Her sister Zuleika thinks the line may be from the old dye tub instead.

You ask whether they can test the water before washing another length. Farah fills one jar at the channel and another at the yard well. Zuleika puts a plain thread in each. Samira comes to check the jar labels; she once confused two cargo marks and does not want this family to mix their samples. The sisters wait while the threads dry. Their aunt asks them to write the time beside each jar, so they can check the water again tomorrow.

Farah asks if you want a copy of their test. Zuleika suggests writing down the time and which jar came from where, so the next weaver can compare it later.
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_b.choice_1: Take a checked copy of the sisters’ water test
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_b.choice_1_resul: You ask the sisters to label both jars before copying the test. Farah writes the channel time, Zuleika writes the well time, and Samira checks the names. Their aunt says she will send you the final result when the threads are dry.
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_b.choice_2: Leave the test with Farah’s workshop
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_b.choice_2_resul: You leave the notes with Farah. Her aunt hangs the two threads beside their labelled jars, where the sisters can check them in tomorrow’s light. Samira goes back to her register, satisfied that no one will mistake the water sources.
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_b.title: A Weaver Asks About the Channel
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_b_resolution.bod:
Farah’s aunt brings you the two dried threads. The line appears on the one rinsed in the old dye tub. The thread washed in channel water has dried clean. Zuleika grins because her guess was right; Farah asks her to help clean the tub before she celebrates. Samira reads the jar labels aloud, and the sisters mark the result in their workshop book.

You ask whether they will throw away the lined silk. The aunt says the length is sound and can be used for a hidden lining; she has another clean bolt for the customer. Farah says she will tell the buyer what happened rather than quietly swap the order. Zuleika carries the old tub outside to scrub it.

The aunt offers a copy of the test for your notes. Zuleika sets a clean thread beside the old one and asks Farah whether they should test the washed tub again before the customer arrives.

Farah holds the second length against the light and asks Zuleika to bring the clean jar, not the old one. Their aunt nods; the lesson has already changed how the sisters work.
ev.ev_cotan_consequence_b_resolution.cho: Carry the sisters’ test to other makers

You take the labelled copy. Farah writes the workshop’s name at the bottom so anyone with a question can find her. Zuleika holds up the clean thread while you fold the paper; their tested method goes with you.
Spend a day checking a second length of silk

You spend the day with the sisters as they rinse and dry another length. The cleaned tub leaves no line this time. Zuleika records the result, and Farah shows the customer both pieces before the order is settled.
ev.ev_cotan_entry.choice_1_result: You spend two days checking pack names with Samira. Her brother learns to keep the washer’s carrying mark separate from the merchant’s ownership mark. You record Khotan on your map and in your travel book. The river washer later comes to ask you about another mark.
ev.ev_cotan_entry.choice_2_result: Samira’s brother takes you to his mother’s shelf of river stones. She remembers who brought each piece and lets you compare the smooth sides with the rough ones. You spend the day hearing the family’s account, note Khotan, and later receive a question from a weaver who knows the same channel.
ev.ev_cotan_entry.choice_3_result: You inspect the sealed lot, pay 135 silver, and spend the day arranging carriage for it. Samira enters the merchant’s name and yours on separate lines before the package joins your cargo. The washer keeps his carrying mark in the register as well.
ev.ev_cotan_mentor_followup.body:
You return to Mahmud’s well before the first caravan arrives. His daughter has lowered a small weight on a cord to check the water level. It touches the surface sooner than yesterday. ‘Is that rain upstream?’ she asks. Mahmud says it might be, but he wants another morning’s reading before he tells people to expect more. The river washer arrives and says a channel higher up was cleared late yesterday; that may have changed the flow.

You ask whether they record both reports. Mahmud’s daughter writes the measured level first, then the washer’s observation beneath it. Her father says the two lines can be compared after the next rain. The washer sets down a smooth river pebble, which she uses to hold the page flat in the breeze.

Mahmud offers you his extra marked stone, or a careful account of the road east toward Pein. If you stay through the day, his daughter will show you how the well changes between morning and evening.
ev.ev_cotan_mentor_followup.choice_1_res: Mahmud gives you the spare marked pebble after his daughter copies its sign into her book. It is a reminder of the well where the family measured before making a promise about tomorrow’s water.
ev.ev_cotan_mentor_followup.choice_2: Ask Mahmud about the road to Pein
ev.ev_cotan_mentor_followup.choice_2_res: Mahmud explains the road toward Pein and where travellers can refill before leaving the river valley. His daughter adds the names to the edge of the well record. You mark Pein on your map while the washer checks his empty jar.
ev.ev_cotan_mentor_followup.choice_3: Stay a day and compare the water levels
ev.ev_cotan_mentor_followup.choice_3_res: You stay through the day and take the evening reading with Mahmud’s daughter. The level has changed only a little; she writes the number beside the morning mark. Her father thanks you for checking it together before the next caravan asks.
ev.ev_cotan_mentor_followup.title: The Morning Well Mark
ev.ev_ctesiphon_entry.choice_1_result: The girl points out the path around the fallen wall. You mark Ctesiphon on your map and continue.
ev.ev_ctesiphon_entry.choice_2_result: Her father gives you room beneath the cloth. After a day’s rest you feel stronger, and the girl helps you mark Ctesiphon beside the river on your map.
ev.ev_damascus_entry.choice_1_result: You ask Nura the way out of the city. She points to the gate beyond the market and tells her nephew to take the bottle first. “Walk, please. You've got glass in your hands.” You pass through with the other travellers and mark Damascus on your map.
ev.ev_damascus_entry.choice_2_result:
You help Nura wrap the bottle again, then accompany her nephew to his home. His mother opens the door in her cooking apron, smells the rosewater, and laughs that Nura has been sparing with it once more.

You stay in Damascus another day. That evening his mother tells you where the caravan for Tripoli meets and draws the road it takes out of town. You add it to your map.
ev.ev_delli_battuta_a.choice_1_result: You stay until evening, matching the wooden tallies against the register. Rahim had received one measure; Shirin adds the missing one to his sack when he comes by. Safiya carries the now-dry page inside. The families in the courtyard thank you for staying with the work.
ev.ev_delli_battuta_a.choice_2_result: The trader waits while his animals are fed, then spends the day showing you the westward road toward Cambay. He names the watering places and draws a bend around a stretch that floods in heavy rain. You add the Delhi–Cambay route to your map; before leaving, you help Safiya keep the wet register away from the sacks.
ev.ev_delli_battuta_a.choice_3_result: After the clerk confirms the tallies, you help Shirin call each family forward and explain the corrected measures. One neighbour grumbles until Safiya shows her his old mark on the wood. By the end of the day everyone has collected their grain, and Shirin asks you to come by if you need a place to sit in the shade.
ev.ev_delli_battuta_b.choice_1_result: You stay through the next day, helping Hina give each family a dry place to sleep. Her nephew finishes sorting the letters while you carry bedding upstairs. When the last guest has a room, Hina thanks you in front of the neighbours and keeps a seat for you at supper.
ev.ev_delli_battuta_b.choice_2_result: The westward driver spends the day checking addresses with you and naming the stages toward Cambay. He points out the stop near his sister’s home, then draws the road onward. You add the Delhi–Cambay route to your map before he takes the bundle.
ev.ev_delli_battuta_b.choice_3_result: You spend the day sorting the eastern letters by their next carrier and copying the long road list toward Khotan. Hina pays you 0.8 silver for the work. Her nephew reads the addressees aloud once more before the bundles leave; you mark the Delhi–Khotan route on your map.
ev.ev_delli_entry.choice_1_result: The sister returns with both jars at their proper doors. You mark Delhi on your map and continue while the water carrier fills the caravan’s last skin.
ev.ev_delli_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day with the scribe, checking his list of intermediate stops before the distant road reaches Khotan. The water carrier’s sister reads the place names aloud while the drivers pack. You mark Delhi, Khotan, and the long route between them on your map.
ev.ev_dongola_entry.choice_1_result: You ride on without delay. The road to Dongola opens on your map.
ev.ev_dongola_entry.choice_2_result: You rest half a day by the road. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again. You set the way to Dongola on your map.
ev.ev_dongola_site_gap.choice_1_result: He points along the southern riverbank. “Follow this route south to Mecha. When the water is high, wait until the ferry is secure before boarding. Keep clear of the fast current.”
ev.ev_dongola_site_gap.choice_2_result: You hold one end while he feels each section and turns a worn patch away from the strain. Reed rope softens in water and tightens as it dries, he says, so never tie it in a knot that cannot give.
ev.ev_dufar_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through without stopping. The road to Dufar opens on your map.
ev.ev_dufar_entry.choice_2_result: You rest and ask what men say of this place. You set the way to Dufar on your map. You set what you saw into your travel book. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again.
ev.ev_dufar_site_gap.choice_1_result: “Go northwest from here by this road to Esher,” the seller says. “Caravans often leave at dawn, before the heat builds on the dry ground.”
ev.ev_dufar_site_gap.choice_2_result: You break one open, revealing a pale vein. Very dark grains may contain earth, the seller says. Break the resin into small pieces before burning it, so the smoke rises evenly without scorching.
ev.ev_edessa_entry.choice_1_result: You fill your bag, thank Miran, and move on. Derya calls after you that a stone is still waiting for the place you visit next. You mark Edessa and the water stop on your map.
ev.ev_edessa_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day with Miran's family. Derya takes you along the water street and introduces you to everyone who knows the story of her uncle's return. In the evening the family shares a meal and gives you a place to sleep. You leave the next morning with renewed strength, and mark Edessa and its water stop on your map.
ev.ev_egrigaia_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through without stopping. You set the way to Egrigaia on your map.
ev.ev_egrigaia_entry.choice_2_result: You rest and ask what men say of this place. The road to Egrigaia opens on your map. The account is written down before the hour turns. It costs you 1 day on the road.
ev.ev_egrigaia_site_gap.choice_1_result: “Take this road south to the Tenduc camp,” he says. “You can recognise the path the herds take. At a fork, ask the herders instead of chasing stray wagon ruts.”
ev.ev_egrigaia_site_gap.choice_2_result: You hold the roof cord while he lets it out a little at a time. Too wide, and the warmth escapes; too narrow, and the smoke stings your eyes. Watch the fire and the wind together.
ev.ev_ephesus_entry.choice_1_result: You thank Leyla and continue past the old stones. Nisa holds up the marble to show you the carved edge she found. You mark Ephesus and the path up the hill on your map.
ev.ev_ephesus_entry.choice_2_result: You stay with Leyla's family for the day. Nisa's grandfather washes the marble and shows her the tool marks along one edge. After supper he tells you both about the older streets below the hill, and Leyla gives you a place to sleep. You leave the next morning stronger and mark Ephesus on your map.
ev.ev_esher_a.choice_1_result: You walk the haven and note how the Soldan's customs are kept. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again. You set the way to Aden on your map. You set what you saw into your travel book.
ev.ev_esher_a.choice_2_result: You stand upon the mole and watch the Indian ships unload. The road to Dufar opens on your map. The account is written down before the hour turns. Fortune bends a little your way.
ev.ev_esher_a.choice_3_result: You buy an Arabian horse from the export pens. You pay 16000 coins. You add 1 item to your stores. You set what you saw into your travel book.
ev.ev_esher_a_followup.body: In the haven four hundred miles from Aden a frankincense merchant who farms the Soldan's white incense draws you from the mole into his storehouse. He says Esher's revenue is smoke and gum — and that Aden, Dufar, and Axuma are written in his coast book if you mean to sail or ride with more than a glance at the harbour.
ev.ev_esher_a_followup.choice_1: Buy frankincense at the Soldan's coast price
ev.ev_esher_a_followup.choice_1_result: He sells you frankincense sealed for the next monsoon. The gum is white and the price is the coast's own.
ev.ev_esher_a_followup.choice_2: Ask which sea road leads toward Aden and Dufar
ev.ev_esher_a_followup.choice_2_result: Aden and Dufar are marked on your map. The frankincense coast is clear.
ev.ev_esher_a_followup.choice_3: Watch the ships a day and hear Axuma named
ev.ev_esher_a_followup.choice_3_result: You spend a day on the mole. Axuma is named in the talk, and fortune bends a little your way.
ev.ev_esher_a_followup.title: Esher: The Soldan's Haven, a Second Page
ev.ev_esher_b.choice_1_result: You buy frankincense at the Prince's price in the harbour market. You pay 2400 coins. You add 1 item to your stores. The account is written down before the hour turns.
ev.ev_esher_b.choice_2_result: You buy dates from the coastal orchards. You pay 150 coins. You add 1 item to your stores. Your name carries a little more weight here now.
ev.ev_esher_b.choice_3_result: You ask the Saracen merchants where the coast trade runs southward. The road to Axuma opens on your map. The road to Aden opens on your map. The account is written down before the hour turns.
ev.ev_esher_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through the darvāzā without delay. You set the way to Esher on your map.
ev.ev_esher_entry.choice_2_result: You walk through the bāzār. It costs you 1 day on the road. The account is written down before the hour turns. The road to Esher opens on your map.
ev.ev_esher_entry.choice_3_result: You visit the mandir (temple). Your name carries a little more weight here now. You carry away a small sign of the place. You set the way to Esher on your map.
ev.ev_etzina_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through without stopping. You set the way to Etzina on your map.
ev.ev_etzina_entry.choice_2_result: You rest and ask what men say of this place. The road to Etzina opens on your map. The account is written down before the hour turns. It costs you 1 day on the road.
ev.ev_fuju_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through without stopping. The road to Fuju opens on your map.
ev.ev_fuju_entry.choice_2_result: You rest and ask what men say of this place. You set the way to Fuju on your map. You set what you saw into your travel book. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again.
ev.ev_gap_cacanfu.body: At the river wharf of Cacanfu, a merchant disputes the weight of a sack of beans. The weighman asks whether to weigh the sack with the beans or subtract the weight of the empty bag. Each batch of sacks differs, he says; weighing one first will settle the argument before the boat leaves.
ev.ev_gap_cacanfu.choice.route_result: “Go southeast from here and follow the river to Linju.”
ev.ev_gap_cacanfu.choice.scene_result: You and the weighman weigh the empty sack separately. The merchant nods. “Next time I will put the bag’s weight on the manifest first.”
ev.ev_gap_cacanfu.title: The Scale Beside the Canal
ev.ev_gap_cachanfu.body: Two wooden boards hang at the riverside ferry: one records the depth, the other the wind. Having replaced a rope, the ferryman wants to recut the old marks. Which should he record first? A mistaken reading when the water rises could be dangerous. He hangs the boards high enough to see from the bank during a flood.
ev.ev_gap_cachanfu.choice.route_result: “Take the main road southwest to Kenjanfu.”
ev.ev_gap_cachanfu.choice.scene_result: He points to a muddy mark on the bank. “When the water falls to that line, the shoal emerges. Stay on the bank instead of cutting across.”
ev.ev_gap_cachanfu.title: Two Boards at the Ferry
ev.ev_gap_caiju.body: A vegetable seller sets down two bamboo baskets. Leaves go in one and roots in the other; stacked together, the leaves would wilt. If you are going to Chinghianfu, she says, separate them for the jolting road. She hands you thin cord and tells you to tie leafy greens loosely so air can pass through.
ev.ev_gap_caiju.choice.route_result: “Go south from here along the official road to Chinghianfu.”
ev.ev_gap_caiju.choice.scene_result: You separate the wet leaves from the dry roots. “Leaves on top,” she says. “At market this saves much of what would otherwise be thrown away.”
ev.ev_gap_caiju.title: Bamboo Baskets by the Bridge
ev.ev_gap_chinghianfu.body: Stone steps lead down to the water in Chinghianfu. A water carrier sets down his buckets to catch his breath. The lowest steps grow slick with moss.
