ev.ev_saianfu_a.choice_2_result: You buy fine silken stuff from a weaver's stall. You pay 9000 coins. You add 1 item to your stores. The road to Cachanfu opens on your map.
ev.ev_saianfu_a.choice_3_result: You ask the magistrates which towns owe tribute. You set what you saw into your travel book. A small turn of fortune favours you.
ev.ev_saianfu_a_followup.body: In the noble city that rules twelve others a clerk who keeps the tribute lists of the subordinate towns draws you into the magistrate's outer court. He says Saianfu's silk and ginger roads are the same roads that feed those twelve — and that a traveller who buys without hearing the list rides half-blind toward Sinjumatu and Cachanfu.
ev.ev_saianfu_a_followup.choice_1: Buy silk at the magistrate's measured price
ev.ev_saianfu_a_followup.choice_1_result: You leave with silk sealed for the circuit road. The price is fair, and Saianfu's name goes with the bolt.
ev.ev_saianfu_a_followup.choice_2: Ask which of the twelve roads leads toward Sinjumatu
ev.ev_saianfu_a_followup.choice_2_result: Sinjumatu and Cachanfu are marked on your map. The rich circuit is no longer a blank.
ev.ev_saianfu_a_followup.choice_3: Spend a day with the weavers and hear the circuit names
ev.ev_saianfu_a_followup.choice_3_result: You spend a day among the looms. Kenjanfu is named in the talk, and fortune bends a little your way.
ev.ev_saianfu_a_followup.title: Saianfu: The Twelve Cities' Clerk
ev.ev_saianfu_b.choice_1_result: You walk the hunters' market beside the workshops. It costs you 1 day on the road. The account is written down before the hour turns. The road to Kenjanfu opens on your map.
ev.ev_saianfu_b.choice_2_result: You buy ginger from a victualler's stall. You pay 2000 coins. You add 1 item to your stores. Your name carries a little more weight here now.
ev.ev_saianfu_b.choice_3_result: You walk the northern approach where the host once lay siege. The account is written down before the hour turns. Fortune bends a little your way.
ev.ev_saianfu_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through the gate without delay. You set the way to Saianfu on your map.
ev.ev_saianfu_entry.choice_2_result: You walk through the market. It costs you 1 day on the road. The account is written down before the hour turns. The road to Saianfu opens on your map.
ev.ev_saianfu_entry.choice_3_result: You visit the sì (Buddhist monastery). Your name carries a little more weight here now. You carry away a small sign of the place. You set the way to Saianfu on your map.
ev.ev_samara_entry.choice_1_result: You ride on without delay. You set the way to Samara on your map.
ev.ev_samara_entry.choice_2_result: You rest half a day by the road. It costs you 1 day on the road. The road to Samara opens on your map.
ev.ev_samara_site_gap.choice_1_result: “Take this sea route east to Mien,” he says. “Ask when a ship is due to leave. If the monsoon is unfavourable, a captain may wait several days.”
ev.ev_samara_site_gap.choice_2_result: As you roll the cloth, he points to worn stitching. A repair should follow the old needle holes. Let the sail dry before folding it; saltwater left in the cloth weakens the thread.
ev.ev_samarcanda_a.choice_1_result: You walk the Registan between its three great madrasas, and a thin man in a dusty robe detaches himself from the portico to walk beside you. He has been waiting, he says, for someone to ask the right question.
ev.ev_samarcanda_a.choice_2_result: You stand beneath the turquoise dome and look up until the blue fills your sight. The mausoleum and its glazed tiles are now marked in your book.
ev.ev_samarcanda_a.choice_3_result: You walk the canal-lined streets and return the greetings of the scholars. In Samarcanda, where every third man is a teacher, your name is now spoken with approval.
ev.ev_samarcanda_a_followup.body: On a madrasa terrace in Samarcand, an astrolabe lies beside a table of stars. The scholar points to several marks: caravan travellers use these stars to find their way at night. He asks whether you would rather learn to read the instrument, copy a star table, or stay to hear the rest of the lesson.
ev.ev_samarcanda_a_followup.choice_1: Take the lesson and study the star tables
ev.ev_samarcanda_a_followup.choice_1_res: You sit until the lamps are lit, copying what you can of the tables into your own book. The skill stays with you, and the patience of the Registan goes with it.
ev.ev_samarcanda_a_followup.choice_2: Ask which road the scholars say leads to the sky of Cascar
ev.ev_samarcanda_a_followup.choice_2_res: The astronomer draws the road east along the river valleys to Cascar, where he says the sky is even clearer and the scholars even keener. The road to Cascar is now on your map.
ev.ev_samarcanda_a_followup.choice_3: Offer your own account of the road in exchange
ev.ev_samarcanda_a_followup.choice_3_res: You trade your account of the road for the astronomer's account of the sky. The scholars of the Registan remember your name, and your word carries weight in the blue city.
ev.ev_samarcanda_a_followup.title: Samarcanda: The Astronomer of the Registan
ev.ev_samarcanda_b.choice_1_result: You buy a sheaf of Samarcand paper, fine enough to take ink without blotting. It rolls into your cargo, and the paper-makers' skill rides with you.
ev.ev_samarcanda_b.choice_2_result: You watch the paper-makers beat the linen rags and polish the sheets to a shine like watered silk. The master of the shop watches you watching, and at last draws out a sheet that did not come from his vat.
ev.ev_samarcanda_b.choice_3_result: You pay a thousand pieces for an illuminated manuscript from a calligrapher's hand. Gold leaf and ink, bound between boards, now travel in your pack.
ev.ev_samarcanda_b_followup.body: The paper-master who let you watch the vats keeps one secret for those who ask twice. He leads you past the drying yard to a low room where the finished sheets lie in stacks, and there he shows you the polishing stone — a great smooth block, worn hollow in the middle by generations of hands. The beaten sheet is laid on it and rubbed, again and again, with a smaller stone that fits the palm, until the surface shines like watered silk. He says the sheen is not for beauty; it is what keeps the ink from bleeding, and a sheet polished this way will carry a book for three hundred years. Then he dips a pen and writes on a sheet before you, and the ink stands on the surface like a thing alive, never sinking into the fibre.
ev.ev_samarcanda_b_followup.choice_1: Buy a sheaf of the master's polished paper
ev.ev_samarcanda_b_followup.choice_1_res: You pay the master his price and take a sheaf of paper polished until it shines. No ink will bleed on it for three hundred years, and the people of the quarter remember your purchase.
ev.ev_samarcanda_b_followup.choice_2: Ask to learn the polish yourself
ev.ev_samarcanda_b_followup.choice_2_res: You spend a day at the polishing stone, learning how a sheet must be rubbed until it shines. The craft of the quarter is now a little your own.
ev.ev_samarcanda_b_followup.choice_3: Ask where the whitest linen rags come from
ev.ev_samarcanda_b_followup.choice_3_res: The master tells you the whitest rags come up the west road from Bochara, where the flax is long and clean. The road to Bochara is now on your map.
ev.ev_samarcanda_b_followup.title: Samarcanda: The Paper-Master's Secret
ev.ev_samarcanda_c.choice_1_result: You press your forehead to the stone that weeps and feel its cold against your skin. The shrine accepts your devotion, and the favour sits light on you.
ev.ev_samarcanda_c.choice_2_result: You pray in the great mosque for the road ahead. The silence of the courtyard answers you, and the shrine's favour walks out with you into the sun.
ev.ev_samarcanda_c.choice_3_result: You ask the mullahs when the black stone last wept. The youngest answers you, and the oldest silences him; but the question has been asked, and there is a man here who has kept the count.
ev.ev_samarcanda_c_followup.body: The mullah who keeps the mosque chronicle in Samarcand shows you the years when the stone gathered water. “These entries coincide with troubled years,” he says, “but some believe it weeps for people who leave home.” He asks which reading you find persuasive.
ev.ev_samarcanda_c_followup.choice_1: Press your forehead to the stone and wait for a sign
ev.ev_samarcanda_c_followup.choice_1_res: You press your forehead to the black basalt and feel the cool of it against your skin. Whatever the stone means, you have met it face to face, and the sign is now yours to carry.
ev.ev_samarcanda_c_followup.choice_2: Ask the mullah to read you the whole chronicle
ev.ev_samarcanda_c_followup.choice_2_res: You sit among the lamps while the mullah reads the whole chronicle, every weeping and every year. The pattern of the stone's tears is now written in your understanding of the city.
ev.ev_samarcanda_c_followup.choice_3: Ask the pilgrims where they come from
ev.ev_samarcanda_c_followup.choice_3_res: The pilgrims tell you they have come up from Sapurgan, through the passes, to touch the stone and pray. You ask them where the road runs, and the road to Sapurgan is now on your map.
ev.ev_samarcanda_c_followup.title: Samarcanda: The Chronicler of the Stone
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_a.body: The first answer does not end at the gate. A student of the blue-tiled college draws you aside and asks what you intend to carry away from Samarcanda. Beyond the question lies the colleges and the caravans; he offers to set a name to your name, the name of a scholar who receives travellers. Choose what you will make of the sign.
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_a.choice_1: Take the name and ask the student who can vouch for it
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_a.choice_1_: You take the name the student offers and ask who can vouch for it. He names two masters of the college, and the matter opens again.
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_a.choice_2: Thank the student and keep your own counsel
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_a.choice_2_: You thank the student and keep your own counsel. The matter closes at the college gate, and nothing more is asked of you in Samarcanda.
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_a.title: Samarcanda: The Mark at the Gate
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_a_resolutio: You have agreed to carry the student's mark with you — a book no copyist has yet made, promised to a scholar on the road. It will not decide the whole journey, but the scholar's house may open to you when no other door will.
Carry the book to its scholar before nightfall
You carry the book to its scholar before nightfall. The student's word now travels with your name, and the college folk have a reason to receive you.
Keep the scholar's promise in your travel book
You keep the scholar's promise in your travel book and spend a day setting it down plainly. The record is made; the favour waits for a road that may never call on it.
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_b.body: The answer sends a rumour along the road. Before the day is out, a paper-maker finds you at the college with a second account of the colleges and the caravans — which caravan pays in good coin, and which teaches a useful lesson. It is less grand than a traveller's tale, and more useful.
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_b.choice_1_: You follow the paper-maker's practical advice and ask him to set it down. He writes the account out for you, and the road's true measures come into your hand.
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_b.choice_2: Leave the account with the paper-maker
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_b.choice_2_: You leave the account with the paper-maker and keep your own counsel. It goes back to the paper shop, and Samarcanda asks nothing more of you.
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_b.title: Samarcanda: The Road Behind the Answer
ev.ev_samarcanda_consequence_b_resolutio: You have chosen to carry the paper-maker's account with you — which caravan pays in good coin, and which teaches. It will not decide the whole journey, but it will steady you when the road offers a bad bargain.
Tell the next student before nightfall
You tell the next student before nightfall. The road's measures now travel ahead of you, and where they land, your name follows.
Keep the caravan-notes in your travel book
You spend a day copying the caravan-notes into your travel book. The record is yours now, though it cost you a day of the road.
ev.ev_samarcanda_entry.choice_1_result: You declare your goods at the toll-house of Samarcanda, and the clerk notes the blue tiles of the colleges on your route. As he stamps the page, a student of the college leans in to speak.
ev.ev_samarcanda_entry.choice_2_result: The answers you gather speak of the colleges and the caravans with pride, but each man tells it differently. The tale passes from mouth to mouth, and by evening it has found its way back to you, fuller than before.
ev.ev_samarcanda_entry.choice_3_result: You spend a day in the bāzār of Samarcanda and carry away a load of goods. The city's paper, dyes, and trade are now written in your book.
ev.ev_samarcanda_mentor_followup.body: The old student of the blue-tiled college does not let you leave with only his account. He reaches into his satchel and lays out what remains of his student's life: a sheet of Samarcand paper with a map drawn on it in his own hand, a worn copy of a star table, a day's patience. He tells you to choose what will serve you best, because a traveller is only as good as what he carries, and the colleges of Samarcand have nothing else to give.
ev.ev_samarcanda_mentor_followup.choice_: Take the student's notes on the road ahead
The notes are plain and exact, like the man himself. What you learned in the blue-tiled college is now written where you can consult it on the road.
Ask how the blue of the domes is made
The student tells you the blue of the domes comes from lapis ground down from the mountains of Badashan, fired into the glaze. The road to Badashan is now on your map.
Linger a day to copy the student's book
You spend a day at the student's bench, learning his hand and his book. It costs you time, but the book is now partly yours.
ev.ev_samarcanda_mentor_followup.title: Samarcanda: The Student's Parting Gift
ev.ev_sapurgan_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through without stopping. You set the way to Sapurgan on your map.
ev.ev_sapurgan_entry.choice_2_result: You rest and ask what men say of this place. The road to Sapurgan opens on your map. The account is written down before the hour turns. It costs you 1 day on the road.
ev.ev_sapurgan_site_gap.choice_1_result: “Go east on this mountain road to Taykan. Villages along the way can tell you about pack trains. Wrap copper goods well so they do not knock against one another.”

ev.ev_tauris_consequence_a.body: The first answer does not end at the gate. A broker who holds a bench in the Great Bazaar draws you aside and asks what you intend to carry away from Tauris. ev.ev_tauris_consequence_a.choice_2_resu: You thank the broker and keep your own counsel. The matter closes at the bazaar bench, and nothing more is asked of you in Tauris.
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_a.title: Tauris: The Mark at the Gate
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_a_resolution.bo: You have agreed to carry the broker's letter with you — a letter that will outrun any caravan. It will not decide the whole journey, but at the next bazaar his letter may open the credit house.
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_a_resolution.ch: You send the letter before nightfall. The broker's word now travels with your name, and the bazaar folk have a reason to receive you.

ev.ev_tauris_consequence_b.body: The answer sends a rumour along the road. Before the day is out, a qanat-waterman finds you in the bazaar with a second account of the bazaar and the snow-fed qanats — which water lasts the year, and which house keeps a horse for hire. It is less grand than a traveller's tale, and more useful.
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_b.choice_1_resu: You follow the waterman's practical advice and ask him to set it down. He writes the account out for you, and the city's true measures come into your hand.

ev.ev_tauris_consequence_b.title: Tauris: The Road Behind the Answer
ev.ev_tauris_consequence_b_resolution.bo: You have chosen to carry the waterman's account with you — which water lasts the year, and which house keeps a horse. It will not decide the whole journey, but it will keep your purse and your mount in good order.

You tell the next broker before nightfall. The city's measures now travel ahead of you, and where they land, your name follows.
Keep the water-notes in your travel book
You spend a day copying the water-notes into your travel book. The record is yours now, though it cost you a day of the road.
ev.ev_tauris_entry.choice_1_result: You declare your goods at the tamghā-khāna of Tauris, and the tax-master reads the list twice, for the bazaar is full of tricks. As he stamps the page, a broker who holds a bench in the Great Bazaar beckons to you.
ev.ev_tauris_entry.choice_2_result: The men of Tauris answer your questions in a dozen tongues, for half the world's merchants live here. Their answers do not agree, and one of them, a qanat-waterman, promises to bring you the truth before the bazaar closes.
ev.ev_tauris_entry.choice_3_result: You spend a day in the great bāzār of Tauris and carry away a load of goods. The city's trade in pearls, spices, and horses is now written in your book.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_astrodice.choice_1_r: You sit down to learn the star-dice from the reader beside the card table. He teaches the cast for the hour of departure, and at the end he gives you a throw that will wait for you on the road.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_astrodice.choice_2_r: The dice master shows how each house of the sky names a stage of the road. The reading of the houses is now in your book, though the throw stays with him.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_astrodice_followup.b: The dice master who taught you the throwing of the twelve faces calls you back at the city gate. He cups the dice in both hands, blows on them once, and casts them on the curbstone: a final reading for the road. A cast is a cast, he says; you have paid your fee and it is yours to spend. Choose what to take from it.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_astrodice_followup.c: Take the cast as a talisman for the journey
He gives you the dice to carry, their faces worn with years of travel. Whatever they showed, the cast itself is a guard, and you will know how to throw it at any turning.
Ask the dice which road runs best from the city
He casts again and reads the faces: the southern road, the one that ends at Ormus and the sea. The course is drawn on your map and the cast kept in your book.
Stay a day and let the dice settle in your own hand
You sit with the dice through a day, learning their fall, and return them at dusk. The dice master remembers your calm, and the quarter speaks well of you.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_astrodice_followup.t: Tauris: The Dice Master's Last Cast
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_followup.body: The widow who taught you the cards does not let you leave her table empty-handed. She lays out one last spread and reads it for you — a choice-gate cast for the road ahead — then presses a single card into your palm. A parting spread should cost nothing and bind nothing, she says; take from it only what the road will answer for.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_followup.choice_1: Take the parting card she offers you
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_followup.choice_1_re: She gives you the card without naming it, and tells you to read it at the first fork. The reader's gift travels with you now, and the lesson of the spreads with it.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_followup.choice_2: Ask her to read which road will serve you best
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_followup.choice_2_re: She turns the cards and names the southern road, the one that ends at the sea. Ormus is now on your map, and you know the season in which it is best ridden.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_followup.choice_3: Stay a day and watch her cast for the sea road
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_followup.choice_3_re: You stay a day in her house, watching her cast for the sea road and hearing the meaning of each card. It costs time, but the reader's house remembers you, and in Tauris a remembered name opens doors.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_followup.title: Tauris: The Reader's Parting Gift
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_tarot.choice_1_resul: The Frankish widow takes your silver and lays out her cards on the worn table. The teaching weighs gain against cost, and when you rise to go she lays one last spread that she reads only to herself.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_tarot.choice_2_resul: The card-reader nods at your request and points across the room to the other table, where the dice master keeps his leather cup. Two arts, she says, and one parting gift.
ev.ev_tauris_mentor_tarot.choice_3_resul: You watch the reader lay out the gates of choice and show how each road is a reading. The art of the cards is now in your book, though the dealing stays with her.
ev.ev_tenduc_a.choice_1_result: You attend the Nestorian service and listen to the Syriac psalms. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again. You set what you saw into your travel book.
ev.ev_tenduc_a.choice_2_result: You ask the priests what road leads to the Great Kaan's city. The road to Cambaluc opens on your map. The road to Cacanfu opens on your map. Fortune bends a little your way.
ev.ev_tenduc_a.choice_3_result: You leave a coin offering at the church door. You pay 120 coins. Your name carries a little more weight here now.
ev.ev_tenduc_a_followup.body: When the Nestorian service ends, a priest of King George's line draws you aside beside the wooden screen. He says the road east to Cambaluc is not only a yam of horses — it is a chain of churches and post-houses that still remember Prester John's name. He will open one door for you if you choose carefully.
ev.ev_tenduc_a_followup.choice_1: Ask him to mark the yam road toward Cambaluc
ev.ev_tenduc_a_followup.choice_1_result: He marks Cambaluc and the southern post-road on a scrap of parchment. The yam eastward is no longer blind.
ev.ev_tenduc_a_followup.choice_2: Offer a small gift for the church and ask a blessing for the road
ev.ev_tenduc_a_followup.choice_2_result: Your gift is accepted without ceremony. The church remembers your name, and a little favour goes with you on the steppe road.
ev.ev_tenduc_a_followup.choice_3: Wait a day to copy the priests' list of post-houses
ev.ev_tenduc_a_followup.choice_3_result: You wait a day while a scribe copies the post-house list. The waiting costs time, but the next departure is measured.
ev.ev_tenduc_a_followup.title: Tenduc: After the Nestorian Service
ev.ev_tenduc_b.choice_1_result: You walk the market and listen in three tongues. It costs you 1 day on the road. The account is written down before the hour turns.
ev.ev_tenduc_b.choice_2_result: You buy a roll of coloured cotton cloth from a Nestorian weaver. You pay 280 coins. You add 1 item to your stores. A small turn of fortune favours you.
ev.ev_tenduc_b.choice_3_result: You ask the Saracen merchants which road leads north to the steppe. The road to Egrigaia opens on your map. They tell their fellows of the stranger who means to ride the steppe road.
ev.ev_tenduc_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through the gate without delay. You set the way to Tenduc on your map.
ev.ev_tenduc_entry.choice_2_result: You walk through the market. It costs you 1 day on the road. The account is written down before the hour turns. The road to Tenduc opens on your map.
ev.ev_tenduc_entry.choice_3_result: You visit the ovoo (sacred cairn). Your name carries a little more weight here now. You carry away a small sign of the place. You set the way to Tenduc on your map.
ev.ev_tiju_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through without stopping and mark Tiju on your map.
ev.ev_tiju_entry.choice_2_result: You spend a day at Tiju's salt fields, record what the worker says in your travel book, and mark the city on your map.
ev.ev_trapezus_entry.choice_1_result: You thank Tamar and move on. Davit runs up from the boats just in time to catch the cloak Ana tosses him. You mark Trebizond on your map before taking the next street.
ev.ev_trapezus_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day with Tamar and Ana, walking from the houses down to the water. A sailor who has crossed toward Caffa names the places where he has stopped, and Ana asks him to repeat the unfamiliar ones. You mark Trebizond, Caffa, and the sea route between them on your map. At dusk Davit returns to try his cloak; Tamar adjusts the hem while you finish your notes. You leave the next morning.
ev.ev_tripolis_entry.choice_1_result:
Hassan wipes his sticky hand on the sailcloth and points towards the road along the coast. "Leave by that gate. You can reach the next station before dark." His sister adds, "There is a well with a whitewashed rim. Fill your water there."

You make a note of the gate and pass through the carts. Hassan has gone back to folding the cloth.
ev.ev_tripolis_entry.choice_2_result:
You hold up the cloth while Hassan gathers the spilled sugar in its centre. A carpenter replaces the bottom board, then the brother and sister put the sugar back. His sister draws her little moon on the crate again. She watches until the sailors set it safely aboard.

The two give you space to rest in the shed. In the morning Hassan says the southbound caravan has just left through the sea gate. After a night's rest, you feel stronger.
ev.ev_tyrus_entry.choice_1_result: You drink, thank Salma, and continue along the coast. Her brother runs after you to point out the turn past the old stones. You mark Tyre and the shore road on your map.
ev.ev_tyrus_entry.choice_2_result: You stay at the shelter for the day. Salma lets you rest under the cloth while she finishes the sandal. By evening her brother has walked the whole shore in it and returned to show that the seam has held. Salma shares warm food with you, and you sleep there before leaving the next morning. Your strength returns, and you mark Tyre on your map.
ev.ev_unique_cacanfu.body: At Cacanfu’s canal quay, a broker finds damp on a bale of gauze. He needs help separating it from dry rolls. Beside him, a merchant offers a sound bolt of silk at a fixed price.
ev.ev_unique_cacanfu.choice_a_result: You spend a day moving the gauze above the dry rolls. The broker praises your care, and you learn how merchants judge a shipment.
ev.ev_unique_cacanfu.choice_b_result: You pay 9,000 silver and take one bolt of silk. It cannot be sold back at this same quay; its worth lies farther along the road.
ev.ev_unique_cacanfu.title: Dry Silk at the Wharf
ev.ev_unique_cachanfu.body: The Caramoran is too broad for a bridge here. Ginger sacks wait on the bank while a ferryman measures the current. He will take a paying traveller first; the merchants need another hand to load their sacks.
ev.ev_unique_cachanfu.choice_a: Load the ginger sacks before crossing
ev.ev_unique_cachanfu.choice_a_result: You spend a day helping with the ginger and earn 150 silver. The merchants remember your help.
ev.ev_unique_cachanfu.choice_b: Pay for the first ferry across
ev.ev_unique_cachanfu.choice_b_result: You pay 190 silver. The ferryman sets off before the cargo boats and points out the crossing toward Sindafu.
ev.ev_unique_cachanfu.title: Ginger on the Great River
ev.ev_unique_caiju.body: At Caiju, rice and corn for the Kaan’s court pass from river boats into marked storehouses. A tally keeper needs someone to check each mark; a boat master will copy his departure list for a small fee.
ev.ev_unique_caiju.choice_a_result: You spend a day matching sacks to marks. The keeper entrusts you with the final count, and you learn the scale of the grain trade.
ev.ev_unique_caiju.choice_b_result: You pay 150 silver. It names the next waterway toward Chinghianfu and shows how the grain fleet is timed.
ev.ev_unique_caiju.title: The Grain Tally
ev.ev_unique_chinghianfu.body: At Chinghianfu, a silk weaver lays gold thread beside a half-finished bolt. The loom crew needs another hand to wind it evenly. The master will instead teach you how labour and thread set the price.
ev.ev_unique_chinghianfu.choice_a_result: You spend a day at the loom. The weavers remember your careful work, and you learn to work with them.
ev.ev_unique_chinghianfu.choice_b: Pay the silk master for a pricing lesson
ev.ev_unique_chinghianfu.choice_b_result: You pay 180 silver. The master shows how thread and labour change the price of a bolt, improving your judgement in trade.
ev.ev_unique_chinghianfu.title: The Gold Thread Measure
ev.ev_unique_chinginju.body: At Chinginju, carts bring game and silk to a crowded market. A stall keeper asks for help sharing food with newly arrived travellers. A hunter offers a prepared meal for the road.
ev.ev_unique_chinginju.choice_a_result: You spend a day carrying food to the new arrivals. People in the market know your face, and you learn to meet strangers with care.
ev.ev_unique_chinginju.choice_b_result: You pay 240 silver. The hunter packs a hearty meal and shows how to keep it dry, giving you strength for the next stage.
ev.ev_unique_chinginju.title: The Market at First Light
ev.ev_unique_coigangiu.body: The grain fleet has filled the canal at Coigangiu. A boatman needs an oarsman for a hard day against the current; a pilot offers a place on the leading boat for a fee.
ev.ev_unique_coigangiu.choice_a: Row against the current for pay
ev.ev_unique_coigangiu.choice_a_result: You spend a tiring day at the oars and earn 200 silver. Your arms ache, but the boat families remember you.
ev.ev_unique_coigangiu.choice_b: Pay to ride with the pilot
ev.ev_unique_coigangiu.choice_b_result: You pay 180 silver. From the leading boat you see the waterway toward Paukin and learn its turns.
ev.ev_unique_coigangiu.title: One More Boat for the Fleet
ev.ev_unique_coiganju.body: Merchandise arriving by the Caramoran is checked at Coiganju before it is sent onward. A river clerk needs help sorting crate marks. The office also issues a sealed trade note for a fee.
ev.ev_unique_coiganju.choice_a_result: You spend a day matching marks to the river ledger. The clerk pays 150 silver and remembers your careful work.
ev.ev_unique_coiganju.choice_b: Pay for a sealed trade note
ev.ev_unique_coiganju.choice_b_result: You pay 260 silver. The clerk enters your name in the office book; local merchants accept your seal and you understand their accounts better.
ev.ev_unique_coiganju.title: At the River Office
ev.ev_unique_etzina.body: Outside Etzina, camels drink before the road reaches the sandy desert. A herder asks you to mend the straps on his waterskins. A driver offers to show the next known stopping place before he leaves.
ev.ev_unique_etzina.choice_a: Mend the waterskins and fill your own
ev.ev_unique_etzina.choice_a_result: You spend a day checking seams and filling skins. You recover strength for the desert and learn to prepare the journey.
ev.ev_unique_etzina.choice_b: Pay the driver to mark the next stop
ev.ev_unique_etzina.choice_b_result: You pay 160 silver. The driver marks the known road toward Egrigaia and tells you where to keep water close.
ev.ev_unique_etzina.title: The Camel Yard
ev.ev_unique_fuju.body: At Fuju, shipwrights lower a new hull toward the broad river. The ropes strain under its weight. One worker asks for help with the hard launch; another offers to show how ships leave the river for the coast.
ev.ev_unique_fuju.choice_a: Take a rope at the launch
ev.ev_unique_fuju.choice_a_result: You spend a hard day steadying the hull and earn 220 silver. Your strength is spent, but the yard workers respect your help.
ev.ev_unique_fuju.choice_b: Pay to study the river exit
ev.ev_unique_fuju.choice_b_result: You pay 200 silver. A shipwright points out the passage toward Zayton and explains where the deep water begins.
ev.ev_unique_fuju.title: A Hull on the Great River
ev.ev_unique_linju.body: Linju has both busy workshops and men trained for war. A veteran offers to drill you in watching road traffic. A hunter sells a fresh meal for a traveller who needs to regain strength.
ev.ev_unique_linju.choice_a: Spend a day learning the watch
ev.ev_unique_linju.choice_a_result: You spend a day tracing the roads with the veteran. The watchmen accept you, and your sense of travel improves.
ev.ev_unique_linju.choice_b_result: You pay 190 silver and eat well before setting out. You regain strength for the next stage.
ev.ev_unique_linju.title: A Soldier’s Market
ev.ev_unique_mien.body: After the long road into Mien, you find the towers raised for former kings. A keeper will recount how they came to be built. A porter offers to lead you back through the difficult approaches for a fee.
ev.ev_unique_mien.choice_a: Stay and hear the keeper’s account
ev.ev_unique_mien.choice_a_result: You spend a day hearing the story and copying what you can verify. Your care with other people’s accounts grows.
ev.ev_unique_mien.choice_b: Hire the porter for the return approach
ev.ev_unique_mien.choice_b_result: You pay 200 silver. The porter points out the safer way toward Sindafu and saves you from guessing at the mountain forks.
ev.ev_unique_mien.title: The Two Royal Towers
ev.ev_unique_nanghin.body: In Nanghin, silk and gold cloth pass a table where duty is collected. A clerk will teach you to reckon the rolls if you stay. Or you may pay for a sealed passage note.
ev.ev_unique_nanghin.choice_a: Study the duty ledger for a day
ev.ev_unique_nanghin.choice_a_result: You spend a day matching each roll to its mark. You earn no wage, but learn how duties change a merchant’s margin.
ev.ev_unique_nanghin.choice_b: Pay for the sealed passage note
ev.ev_unique_nanghin.choice_b_result: You pay 230 silver. The clerk seals your note, and merchants at the gate treat you as a known traveller.
ev.ev_unique_nanghin.title: The Silk Duty Table
ev.ev_unique_paukin.body: Water spreads on both sides of the stone causeway into Paukin. A cart has stopped where a wheel slips against the stones. Its driver asks for help with the heavy lift; a guide offers to walk the raised road with you.
ev.ev_unique_paukin.choice_a: Help lift the cart from the stones
ev.ev_unique_paukin.choice_a_result: You spend a tiring day freeing the wheel. Your strength falls, but the driver tells the gate workers who helped him.
ev.ev_unique_paukin.choice_b: Pay the guide to walk the causeway
ev.ev_unique_paukin.choice_b_result: You pay 150 silver. The guide shows where the stones hold firm and marks the onward road toward Tiju.
ev.ev_unique_paukin.title: The Stone Causeway
ev.ev_unique_pentam.body: Beside Pentam, a larger vessel waits above the shoal. Its rudder nearly touches the bottom. A pilot says he can sound a passage now, or the crew can wait for the water to rise.
ev.ev_unique_pentam.choice_a: Wait for the tide and mark the shallow passage
ev.ev_unique_pentam.choice_a_result: You spend one day watching the water rise and record where the reef breaks. Your travel sense grows.
ev.ev_unique_pentam.choice_b: Hire the pilot to sound the channel
ev.ev_unique_pentam.choice_b_result: You pay 200 silver. The pilot takes the lead boat across and shows you the passage toward Java Major.
ev.ev_unique_pentam.title: The Rudder at the Shallows
ev.ev_unique_sindafu.body: The river divides Sindafu into its old parts, and bridge traffic is heavy. A boatman asks for help securing his mooring ropes. Another offers a dry boat crossing for a small fee.
ev.ev_unique_sindafu.choice_a_result: You spend a day at the river and earn 150 silver. The boatmen remember your care with their ropes.
ev.ev_unique_sindafu.choice_b_result: You pay 190 silver. The boatman spares you the muddy bridge queue; you recover strength during the quiet crossing.
ev.ev_unique_sindafu.title: Between the River Bridges
ev.ev_unique_sinjumatu.body: At Sinjumatu a southern river is divided for the boats that carry trade onward. A foreman asks you to spend a day settling an argument between crews over the loading order. A pilot sells his channel marks.
ev.ev_unique_sinjumatu.choice_a: Settle the loading order with both crews
ev.ev_unique_sinjumatu.choice_a_result: You spend a day hearing both crews and agree on turns at the quay. The dock workers trust you, and you grow better at dealing with strangers.
ev.ev_unique_sinjumatu.choice_b: Pay for the pilot’s channel marks
ev.ev_unique_sinjumatu.choice_b_result: You pay 200 silver. The pilot shows the branch toward Coigangiu and how the current changes at the split.
ev.ev_unique_sinjumatu.title: Where the River Divides
ev.ev_unique_tiju.body: At Tiju, sacks of salt arrive from the country between the city and the sea. A salt measurer needs help with a long day of lifting and checking weights. A coastal boatman sells his sailing notes.
ev.ev_unique_tiju.choice_a_result: You spend a tiring day at the scales and earn 190 silver. Your strength falls, but the measurers come to know you.
ev.ev_unique_tiju.choice_b_result: You pay 180 silver. His notes mark the way toward Sinju and sharpen your judgement of a salt cargo.
ev.ev_unique_tiju.title: Salt from the Coast
ev.ev_yarcan_entry.choice_1_result: You pass through without stopping. The road to Yarcan opens on your map.
ev.ev_yarcan_entry.choice_2_result: You rest and ask what men say of this place. You set the way to Yarcan on your map. You set what you saw into your travel book. You spend 1 day before the way is clear again.
ev.ev_yarcan_site_gap.choice_1_result: “Take this road northwest to Cascar. Stop at the next oasis; do not pass a water source just to save time.”
ev.ev_yarcan_site_gap.choice_2_result: He puts two cut faces together to show where their bark meets. Bind that ring, but not so tightly that new buds are crushed. In a few days, check the bud before removing the cloth.
ev.ev_yasdi_battuta_a.choice_1_result: You stay the night. Hamid’s daughter finds a clean place for your bedding, and in the morning you help her put out bread for the next travellers. Hamid thanks you and speaks warmly of you to his neighbours.
ev.ev_yasdi_battuta_a.choice_2_result: You join the prayers and remain afterward as the travellers share bread. One of them asks where you have come from; soon the room is full of directions and names of old friends. By the time you leave, people here know you well enough to greet you again.
ev.ev_yasdi_battuta_a.choice_3_result: You spend the day listening as the travellers trace their journey from Isfahan to Yazd. Hamid’s daughter brings out a scrap of paper so you can note the turns and stopping places they remember. You add that stretch of road to your map before you leave.
ev.ev_yasdi_entry.choice_1_result: Roya’s brother points you toward the next street. You mark Yazd on your map and continue.
ev.ev_yasdi_entry.choice_2_result: You spend the day among the weaving rooms and water courtyards. You mark Yazd on your map and write down what you saw in your travel book before leaving.
ev.ev_zayton_battuta_a.choice_1_result: You take your dinars and dirhems to the changers, for no one in China will deal with you until your coin is changed into the king's notes. Each note is a palm-sized sheet stamped with the king's stamp; twenty-five make a nashhat, a dinar of the place. When the paper grows torn or worn you may carry it to the mint, and receive new notes in its place without interest.
ev.ev_zayton_battuta_a.choice_2_result: You sit for the painters, and a day passes under their brushes — none in the world come near to them in painting, and your likeness and the likenesses of your companions go up on the walls and on papers stuck about the streets. It is the custom with every stranger who passes through their towns: should any such a one make flight necessary, his picture is sent out to the other provinces, and wherever he is, he is taken.
ev.ev_zayton_battuta_a.choice_3_result: You spend a day watching the clerks of the harbour take down the names and forms of the men aboard each junk before it sails, and when a vessel returns, the servants of the magistrates board her and compare the men with the descriptions; a missing man costs the commander his ship, and goods not entered in the register forfeit ship and cargo to the king — an oppression seen nowhere else. You learn of the river road, twenty-seven days from Sin Kilan, where earthenware is made as here at Zayton, and that the same river runs on toward Kinsay; here the river called the water of life enters the sea, and the place is called the meeting of two seas.
ev.ev_zayton_entry.choice_1_result: You declare your goods to the Kaan's clerks, and their brushes move without pause, recording your cargo in the sea-trade register. A hundred shiploads wait ahead of yours, and the tally runs two full days before the register closes. When it is struck, one clerk draws a second sheet and asks where your road goes next.
ev.ev_zayton_entry.choice_2_result: You call to the fishermen in their own tongue and slip ashore by their steps, and no brush records your coming. But the tithe clerks will remember the merchant who came ashore undeclared, and the quayside murmurs your name with less welcome. A lamp burns in the watch-house above the quay, and the night watch keeps its own account of every shadow.
ev.ev_zayton_entry.choice_3_result: You ask a boatman what all these ships are, and he answers as only a man who reads the sea can. He can name a hundred ships and a hundred roads, and he offers you the two that matter.
ev.ev_zayton_entry.choice_4_result: A traveller from the West asks leave to handle the king's paper money, and tells of the registry of ships and the painters who draw every stranger's face; he would tell you more of it, if you will listen.
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang.choice_1_result: You ask the Persian traders about the sea road, and they answer in a tongue you are learning to follow. One of them, an old merchant, calls for tea and offers you the bargain that the quarter keeps for strangers of good faith.
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang.choice_2_result: You pay a lad of the foreign quarter to interpret for a season, and spend twenty days in his company. The Arabic tongue now sits in your mouth, and your purse is lighter by three thousand pieces.
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang.choice_3_result: You pay twelve thousand pieces for a bolt of silk from a Manzi weaver and roll it into your cargo. The finest silk of the south now rides with you.
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang_followup.body: In the foreign quarter, the merchant who heard you bargain sends word to your lodging: a bolt of silk has come from the weaver's own loom, and it is offered first to you. He sets it out beside the well where the merchants of three tongues meet. The price is the weaver's price, he says, and the bargain is yours to close — or you may ask instead what the sea-merchants know of the road they do not speak of at the quay.
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang_followup.choice_1: Buy the bolt at the weaver's price
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang_followup.choice_1_r: The bolt is fine Manzi silk, heavier in the hand than it looks, and you carry it out of the quarter wrapped in oiled cloth. At the weaver's price it is a bargain worth the telling; the quarter watches you go, and its judgment is recorded.
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang_followup.choice_2: Ask the sea-merchants of the lane to Chamba
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang_followup.choice_2_r: A merchant of the Indian sea draws the lane in the dust with his finger, mark by mark — the monsoon's turning, the days of open water, the haven at the end. Chamba is now named on your map, and the road that serves it.
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang_followup.choice_3: Let the quarter learn your name
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang_followup.choice_3_r: You bargain plainly and speak plainly, and the quarter marks you for an honest man. Among the merchants of the sea-lands your name will be repeated before you are seen again.
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang_followup.choice_4: Copy the wonder-leaves and road chronicles
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang_followup.choice_4_r: The scholars lend you their stack of papers. By lamplight you copy Prester John beside Wang Dayuan, paradise beside Zhenla, and the mountain crossings of the two pilgrims — a richer book of the road than you carried out.
ev.ev_zayton_fanfang_followup.title: Zayton: The Quarter's Bargain
ev.ev_zayton_harbour.choice_1_result: You buy a sack of pepper at the quayside price, and the merchant slaps the sack as it is weighed. But the price he names is not the whole bargain; he keeps you a moment to speak of the freight ledger.
ev.ev_zayton_harbour.choice_2_result: You stand the pilots a drink and ask about the winds. A day passes in good talk, and the monsoon's law — and the sea-road to Chamba — are now on your map.
ev.ev_zayton_harbour.choice_3_result: You spend the day watching the ships come in — a hundred at a time, they say, when the season is full. The haven of Zayton is now marked in your book.
ev.ev_zayton_harbour_followup.body: The warehouseman who weighed your pepper at the quay finds you again by the customs shed. He has seen how you counted the shipping, and he does what his kind do for a man they trust: he lays open his own reckoning. Freight, he says, is the harbour's second tongue. Small wares pay thirty in the hundred, bulky goods forty, and pepper four and forty — and then the Kaan's tamghā on top. He offers to let you take a sack at the price the merchants pay among themselves. He will not hold it past the turning of the tide.
ev.ev_zayton_harbour_followup.choice_1: Buy the sack at the merchants' own price
ev.ev_zayton_harbour_followup.choice_1_r: The warehouseman weighs out a sack and lets you have it at the price merchants pay among themselves, the tamghā already reckoned in. Pepper in hand, you know the freight reckoning as the merchants know it — and you know the rate that will follow you to every quay of the Indian sea.
ev.ev_zayton_harbour_followup.choice_2: Ask which season the wind turns toward Chamba
ev.ev_zayton_harbour_followup.choice_2_r: The warehouseman points south across the water, where the ships lie waiting. When the monsoon turns, he says, the lane to Chamba opens; a ship that misses it waits a season. The lane is now on your map, and the season that serves it.
ev.ev_zayton_harbour_followup.choice_3: Stand another day among the masts
ev.ev_zayton_harbour_followup.choice_3_r: You spend another day on the quay, among masts that stand like a burnt forest, watching the ships of India come in. The day is gone before the last one is moored; after you leave, whenever you look at the sea, this haven is what you see.
ev.ev_zayton_harbour_followup.title: Zayton: The Freight Reckoning
ev.ev_zayton_jiaobei_ask.choice_1_result: You cast the two cups before the shrine and wait while they settle their answer. The reading is given, and the shrine keeps your name.
ev.ev_zayton_jiaobei_ask.choice_2_result: You pass the temple-shrine without casting the cups. The goddess's answer stays unasked, and the slip stays in the cylinder.
ev.ev_zayton_ledger_consequence.choice_1: You keep the clerk's fair copy of the duty ledger, and your hand rests on the margin where Kinsay and the coastal road are noted. The ledger has given you a road to think about.
ev.ev_zayton_ledger_consequence.choice_2: You let the cargo alone be entered and take no copy. The clerk dips his brush once more and closes the book; a coldness settles on the table that has nothing to do with the ink.
ev.ev_zayton_ledger_consequence_resoluti: By carrying the sealed copy of the duty ledger, you carry Zayton's own mark upon your cargo. It will not decide the whole journey, but wherever the Kaan's clerks keep their tables, the seal will speak before you do.
Present the copy to the harbour-master before nightfall
The harbour-master reads the seal by lamplight and marks your name cleared in his own book. The copy has done its work; Zayton's harbour will not hold you back again.
Keep the copy safe in your travel book
You spend a day setting the copy down fair in your travel book. The seal's work is preserved for the road, though the writing costs you a day.
ev.ev_zayton_mazu.choice_1_result: You make your offering before the sea goddess, and the smoke of the paper rises straight in the still air. The temple keeper watches the reading of your slip, and does not turn away as you rise to leave.
ev.ev_zayton_mazu.choice_2_result: You shake the cylinder and draw a slip before the shrine of the sea-goddess. The answer is read aloud, and the sailors watch to see how you take it.
ev.ev_zayton_mazu.choice_3_result: You stand at the back and watch the sailors at their prayers before the sea-goddess. The way of the sea-folk is now written in your book.
ev.ev_zayton_mazu_followup.body: The slip-reader at the temple door calls you back from the stair. The goddess does not count an offering once, she says; she asks again before every sailing, and a fleet is making ready below. The sailors are already on the hill, burning paper and setting out rice and wine. There is still room at the door for one more who means to ask.
ev.ev_zayton_mazu_followup.choice_1: Make an offering before the fleet sails
ev.ev_zayton_mazu_followup.choice_1_resu: You burn paper at the goddess's feet and set out a dish of rice and a cup of wine, as the shipmasters do. She looks south over the water and does not refuse you; the sea road is kinder to you for the asking.
ev.ev_zayton_mazu_followup.choice_2: Draw a slip for the sailing
ev.ev_zayton_mazu_followup.choice_2_resu: You shake the cylinder until a slip falls, and the reader reads it against the book of verses. It names a day when the wind will serve you — and the lane to Chamba is named with it. You mark the day and go down to the water.
ev.ev_zayton_mazu_followup.choice_3: Stay and watch the sailors ask
ev.ev_zayton_mazu_followup.choice_3_resu: You stay a day on the temple hill while the sailors come and go, each one asking in his own way. The smoke of the sea-temple goes with you when you leave, and you carry the memory of what asking is.
ev.ev_zayton_mazu_followup.title: Zayton: The Temple Asks Again
ev.ev_zayton_mentor.choice_1_result: You sit with the old woman at the temple door and give what you can to the temple. She watches your hands as you take up the cylinder, and she begins to teach you as she has taught forty years of readers.
ev.ev_zayton_mentor.choice_2_result: You sit with the old woman and ask to learn the cups. She looks at you a long moment, then sets the two cups on the threshold and begins, for the three answers have their own order.
ev.ev_zayton_mentor.choice_3_result: The reader of the slips shows how the slips are read by their order and their marks. The art of the lots is now in your book, though the shaking stays with her.
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_followup.body: The old woman who reads the slips will not let you leave with only what you have learned. She reaches for the cylinder and draws one slip for your voyage, but she does not read it aloud. The slips tell a man what he has not considered, she says; you have sat with her long enough to read your own. She holds it out and lets you choose how to carry it.
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_followup.choice_1: Take the slip she draws for your voyage
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_followup.choice_1_re: She reads the slip once, then presses it into your hand: a day to sail, and counsel you now know how to read for yourself. The reading is yours, and the day with it.
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_followup.choice_2: Ask her which road the slips favour
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_followup.choice_2_re: She shakes the cylinder until it answers, and reads what falls: the slips counsel the monsoon lane to Chamba, and the sea-goddess's favour with it. The road is drawn on your map, and the counsel carried in your book.
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_followup.choice_3: Leave silver for the temple lamps
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_followup.choice_3_re: You leave silver for the lamps that burn at the goddess's feet and take your leave of the reader. The blessing of the temple goes with you down the hill, and the smoke of it after you to the water.
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_followup.title: Zayton: The Reader's Parting Counsel
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_jiaobei_followup.bod: The temple attendant who taught you the throwing of the cups waylays you at the gate. He sets a pair of half-moons of wood before you and bids you throw for the voyage you are about to make. The cups fall, and he does not smile or frown: a throw is a throw, he says, and a verdict is a verdict. Choose how to carry it.
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_jiaobei_followup.cho: Keep the verdict as a ward for the journey
He wraps the two cups in a cloth and presses them into your hand. Whatever the throw promised, the carry itself is a protection, and you will know how to read it at any campfire.
Ask the cups which road to take from the port
He throws again and reads the falling cups: the sea road to Java is favoured, the goddess's lane open. The course is drawn on your map and the verdict kept in your book.
Wait a day and let the cups settle in your own hand
You sit with the two cups through an afternoon, learning their weight, and leave them with the temple at dusk. The attendant remembers your patience, and the quarter speaks well of you.
ev.ev_zayton_mentor_jiaobei_followup.tit: Zayton: The Three Cups at Parting
ev.ev_zayton_pilot_consequence.choice_1_: You ask after the monsoon lane, and the pilot draws the southern line again, deeper. He names the days of the season when it runs, and Chamba settles on your map like a ship coming to anchor.
ev.ev_zayton_pilot_consequence.choice_2_: You ask after the inland road, and the pilot sets down his cup and speaks of it as a man speaks of a road he knows in the dark. The way north to Fuju is now written in your book, and your name in his.
ev.ev_zayton_watch_consequence.choice_1_: You pay the late-declaration fee on the watch-table, and the tally is marked paid. The watch leaves your cargo in your keeping, but they have written your name down twice.
ev.ev_zayton_watch_consequence.choice_2_: You leave the cargo for two days' inspection. The watch goes through the bales without haste and marks each one in their book; in the waiting you come to know the rounds of the quay by heart.
ev.ev_zayton_watch_consequence_resolutio: By carrying the watch's tally, you carry the receipt of a debt settled in the dark. It will not decide the whole journey, but at the next quay the tally says you have already paid your reckoning at Zayton.
Enter the tally at the quay office before nightfall
The quay clerk strikes the tally through and writes your name in the paid column. The night's mischance is closed, and the ledger holds no shadow against you.
Keep the tally in your travel book
You spend a day copying the tally and its reason into your travel book. The reckoning is recorded for the road ahead, though it costs you a day.
ev.fuju.entry.body: Now this city of Fuju is the key of the kingdom which is called CHONKA, and which is one of the nine great divisions of Manzi. The city is a seat of great trade and great manufactures. The people are Idolaters and subject to the Great Kaan. And a large garrison is maintained there by that prince to keep the kingdom in peace and subjection. For the city is one which is apt to revolt on very slight provocation. There flows through the middle of this city a great river, which is about a mile in width, and many ships are built at the city which are launched upon this river.
ev.fuju.entry.choice.look: Rest and ask what men say of this place
ev.fuju.entry.title: Concerning the Greatness of the City of Fuju
ev.gap.antiochia.scene.body:
At the bridge, a ferryman reaches into the Orontes with his hook and pulls out a wooden ladle. Three short marks are cut into its handle. He wipes it on his sleeve and holds it up to a child on the bank. "Look, the river gave my ladle back."

The child knocks a heel against the stone step. "You used that to serve me bean soup this morning." The ferryman clears his throat and puts away the hook. Carts move slowly across the bridge. The child is still waiting to hear about those three marks.
ev.gap.antiochia.scene.choice.route: "Is the cart for Berrhoea waiting on the bridge too?"
ev.gap.antiochia.scene.result.route:
The ferryman nods towards the far end of the bridge. "The cart with the blue cover is going to Berrhoea. Wait until it gets across, then ask the driver whether he'll take someone along."

The child returns the ladle. "Did you drop it in again?" The ferryman winks at you. "I pulled it out myself this time. The river hasn't learned to do my work yet."
ev.gap.antiochia.scene.result.talk:
The ferryman gives the ladle to the child. "Your father made them. One mark for each bowl of soup. He says I serve too much, so he keeps count." The child traces the marks and asks why he threw it in the river today.

"Slipped out of my hand." The child laughs and runs up the steps with it. The ferryman calls after him, "Tell your father he still owes me those three bowls!"
ev.gap.antiochia.scene.title: A Ladle Caught at the Bridge
ev.gap.babylonia-cairus.scene.body:
At a bread stall by the canal, a young woman who carries grain holds two loaves and hesitates. Amin, the baker, looks at his board. "I only took payment for one, didn't I?"

She tells him the other is the loaf he promised her little brother this morning. Amin remembers. "He came early. He said you had to cross the river and might miss lunch." She asks whether the second loaf can wait in the oven until the boy returns from school.

Amin puts the loaves back on his board and draws a circle in charcoal at the corner. "I'll know your mark when he comes." Then he turns to you. "Where are you going? Someone passing through here will know the road."
ev.gap.babylonia-cairus.scene.choice.rou: Ask about the road to Alexandria
ev.gap.babylonia-cairus.scene.choice.tal: Help Amin remember the boy's name
ev.gap.babylonia-cairus.scene.result.rou:
Amin points to the wagons by the canal. "They leave for Alexandria tomorrow by the northern road. The drivers buy bread here before each journey. I'll call one over."

The young woman wraps her loaf. She is going to the harbour herself in a few days to see her uncle. She writes down the driver's name and says she will ask Musa if he has a message for him.
ev.gap.babylonia-cairus.scene.result.tal:
The young woman says her brother is named Musa. You write it on the back of Amin's board so he will remember during the rush. She asks if he can give the boy a spoonful of mashed beans with his bread. Amin says yes; he will keep a loaf for himself when the oven closes.

When you pass the canal at dusk, Musa is sitting by the stall with his bread rolled around the beans. His sister has not returned from carrying grain, so he has saved half for her.
ev.gap.babylonia-cairus.scene.title: The Second Loaf at the Canal
ev.gap.basora.scene.body:
Nura’s son, Samir, is sorting soft dates from the ones ready to dry. He keeps one small basket apart. ‘For my aunt,’ he says. ‘Last year I ate half of hers before the boat left. She sent back the empty basket with my name written inside.’

A boatman calls for the next load. Samir picks up the basket, then turns to you: ‘Can you watch this one while I carry the others? If I lose it again, she’ll write my name on every jar.’

You ask what his aunt said when she sent the basket back. Samir says she wrote, ‘Next time count before you taste.’ Nura hears him and adds that the note was kinder than the teasing he got at home. The boatman asks where to set the drying dates; Samir points to a covered tray, then notices the loose seam in the sack beside it. He tells his mother he will mend it after the small basket is safe. Nura tells him to deal with one thing at a time. A second boat noses in, and the crew begins making room along the landing.
ev.gap.basora.scene.choice.route: Ask Samir about the Baghdad road
ev.gap.basora.scene.choice.talk: Keep an eye on the basket
ev.gap.basora.scene.result.route:
Samir has watched the inland caravans leave from this landing. He points northwest toward Baghdad and shows you where they turn away from the canal. You mark that road and the city on your map.

When the road is clear in your book, Samir checks his aunt’s basket once more and sets it on a dry board beside Nura’s jars. She sees the mark and says she will watch it while he carries the next load. The basket is safe for the boat.
ev.gap.basora.scene.result.talk: You wait until Samir returns and place the basket in his hands. He counts it twice, grins, and shares two fresh dates with you. ‘She’ll get the rest this time.’ You mark the landing and its place in Basra on your map.
ev.gap.basora.scene.title: The Date Boat
ev.gap.berrhoea.scene.body:
Rashid's niece Dima is sifting flour at the mill. She has covered the sack but left her own sleeves open, and a puff of white dust rises whenever she moves. Rashid holds out a cloth for her wrists. Dima says she is nearly done; then she sneezes and accepts it.

The flour is for her mother's bread oven. Rashid has promised to bring the first sack over himself, because Dima's mother thinks he spends too much time telling travellers stories beside the mill. He says he does, but only when they listen.

Dima asks if you would like to see how they keep the fine flour separate. Rashid once carried grain west toward Antioch and is happy to describe the road while she finishes the sack.

You ask Dima whether the flour will reach the oven before the first batch of bread goes in. ‘If Uncle Rashid stops telling this story,’ she says. Rashid protests that he is tying the sack while he talks, then asks her to show him which bag has the finer flour. She points to the one she set by the door and says her mother uses it for the thinner flatbreads. He lifts it to test the weight. ‘I will take this one first,’ he says, and Dima finally gets the empty sieve off the table so she can sweep up the flour she spilled.
ev.gap.berrhoea.scene.choice.route: Listen to Rashid describe the Antioch road
ev.gap.berrhoea.scene.choice.talk: Watch Dima finish the first sack
ev.gap.berrhoea.scene.result.route: Rashid names the places where he stopped on the way west to Antioch. Dima interrupts once to ask whether he really delivered the grain before telling stories there. He admits he arrived late that day. You mark Aleppo, Antioch, and the route between them; Dima takes the finished sack from him before he can start another tale.
ev.gap.berrhoea.scene.result.talk: Dima shakes the last flour through the sieve and ties the sack. Rashid shoulders it at once, to prove he has remembered his promise. You walk with them to the bread oven and learn how the mill lane joins the market street. You add this part of Aleppo to your map.
ev.gap.berrhoea.scene.title: The Flour at Rashid’s Mill
ev.gap.bethleem.scene.body:
Salma, who sells lamp oil, is filling a clay lamp. Her grandson Gabriel sits beside her with a small pair of scissors, studying the wick.

“Where do I cut?” he asks.

“Leave a little above the oil,” Salma says, holding the lamp steady. “Too much and the rim will blacken. Too little and the flame will sink.”

Gabriel sets down the scissors. He was looking after the lamp in their yard last night. The wind blew it out, and the people returning home had to find the door latch in the dark. Salma strokes his hair. “Move it inside the wall and try again. I'll be beside you tonight.”

A traveller from the coast stops to buy oil and joins them to look at the lamp. Salma asks whether you will help Gabriel test it. The traveller says he knows the long road to Alexandria.
ev.gap.bethleem.scene.choice.route: Listen to the traveller describe the road to Alexandria
ev.gap.bethleem.scene.choice.talk: Trim the wick and test the lamp with Gabriel
ev.gap.bethleem.scene.result.route:
The traveller tells you the route to Alexandria: first reach the coast, then continue towards Egypt. On his last journey he met a man repairing a cart wheel along the way. The delay cost him half a day, and by the time the wheel was fixed he had companions for the next stretch. You mark Alexandria and the route on your map.

As you talk, Gabriel finishes trimming the wick. Salma lights the lamp and asks him to test it inside the wall. When he comes back, he smiles. “It stayed lit.”
ev.gap.bethleem.scene.result.talk: You hold the lamp while Gabriel trims the wick. Salma lights it and asks him to move it inside the wall. Wind comes through the yard entrance. The flame shifts a little and stays lit. Gabriel picks up the lamp and says he will place it there himself tonight. Salma shows you where to find her oil stall, and you mark this resting place in Bethlehem on your map.
ev.gap.bethleem.scene.title: A Small Pair of Scissors by the Oil Lamp
ev.gap.cobinan.scene.body:
A dyer named Mina lifts a length of blue cloth from her vat. Her sister ordered it for a new room and wants the colour even across the whole wall. Mina hangs the cloth where it will dry, then asks you to look at it from the far end of the lane.

‘From here every patch looks good,’ she says. ‘Tell me what you see from there.’ Her sister will arrive soon. Mina knows a caravan that goes toward Camadi and can tell you where it leaves if you ask.

You take a few steps back and ask where her sister plans to hang it. ‘Across the room from a window,’ Mina says. ‘She wants colour there even when the sun moves.’ An apprentice offers to turn the cloth for you. Mina tells him to leave it still so you can judge the same side she saw. He asks whether one pale strip matters. ‘She will notice it on the first morning,’ Mina answers. ‘She has been waiting for this cloth since the room was finished.’
ev.gap.cobinan.scene.choice.route: Ask Mina about the Camadi caravan
ev.gap.cobinan.scene.choice.talk: Check the cloth from the far end of the lane
ev.gap.cobinan.scene.result.route: Mina tells you which yard the caravan uses and where the road turns toward Camadi. You mark the route and town on your map while the cloth dries.
ev.gap.cobinan.scene.result.talk: From the far end you spot a paler strip. Mina thanks you and dips that section again before her sister arrives. You mark the dye house in Cobinan on your map.
ev.gap.cobinan.scene.title: The Dyer’s Blue Cloth
ev.gap.constantinopolis.scene.body:
At the quay, a fisherman named Petros sorts the morning catch. He puts the bruised fish in one bowl for his family’s soup and sets the sound fish on a wet board for sale. His daughter asks why she cannot sell the whole lot.

‘Because your mother is cooking lunch,’ he says, handing her the bowl. She smiles and carries it away. Petros has heard a captain call for cargo bound for Caffa and can tell you which boat it is.

When the girl returns, she asks whether there is enough for supper as well. Petros counts the remaining fish and says her mother can decide that after lunch. ‘She’ll say to save the best one for Grandfather,’ the girl replies. He puts one aside and asks her to fetch bread from the baker. You ask about the boats waiting beyond the quay. Petros knows which captain is bound for Caffa, but he wants to finish selling this catch before the tide changes.
ev.gap.constantinopolis.scene.choice.rou: Ask about the ship to Caffa
ev.gap.constantinopolis.scene.result.rou: Petros points to the cargo boat at the far end of the quay. Its captain is taking passage to Caffa; you note the boat, the Black Sea route, and its destination on your map.
ev.gap.constantinopolis.scene.result.tal: Petros shows you how he checks the eyes and gills, then lets you arrange the sale fish on the board. You mark this quay on your map of Constantinople before going on.
ev.gap.constantinopolis.scene.title: The Fish Seller’s Lunch
ev.gap.ctesiphon.scene.body:
The girl’s father, Farid, sorts new bricks beside the shelter. One has a crack through its middle. He sets it aside for paving the threshold instead of putting it in the wall.

His daughter complains that her grandmother would have spotted the crack first. ‘Probably,’ Farid says. ‘She also made me carry every brick I chose badly.’ He asks you to hand him a sound brick. The girl is already asking whether you have come from Baghdad.

You ask why he needs the doorway finished today. Farid says a neighbour will bring a woven mat tomorrow, and there must be a level place to set it. His daughter asks whether she can make the threshold brick herself. ‘You may choose its place after it dries,’ he says. She picks up the cracked brick and turns it in her hands. The split would catch a bare foot if he laid it as it is, so Farid shows her which edge to smooth. The neighbour arrives with a sample of the mat and asks them to measure the opening once more.
ev.gap.ctesiphon.scene.result.route: Farid takes you to a rise beyond the fallen wall and points northwest, toward Baghdad. The girl repeats the turns so you will remember them. You mark the road and city on your map.
ev.gap.ctesiphon.scene.result.talk: You hold the brick while Farid settles it into the mortar. His daughter presses a wet thumbprint into an unused scrap and announces that this one is hers. Farid promises to put it by the door once it dries. You mark their shelter beside the old arch on your map.
ev.gap.ctesiphon.scene.title: Bricks for the Shelter
ev.gap.damascus.scene.body:
Amin hangs a water jug on the rack and taps it twice. The first note rings clearly. The second is as dull as a knock on wood. His daughter puts down her polishing cloth. “The base again, Father?”

Amin nods. The jug is for Aziza, who sells water across the street. She has used her old one for more than ten years, and its spout leaks onto her sleeve whenever she serves a customer. His daughter holds the old jug beside the new one. “I'll narrow this part a little more. She likes to hold the jug in one hand and take payment with the other.”

Amin hands her the new jug to narrow the spout and chooses a handle from the rack. Someone calls out apricots for sale outside. Aziza asks across the street if the jug will be ready today. “It will!” Amin calls. “Send your daughter this afternoon. I still have to fit the handle.”
ev.gap.damascus.scene.choice.route: Ask Amin which caravan goes to Acre
ev.gap.damascus.scene.choice.talk: Stay to hear the repaired jug ring
ev.gap.damascus.scene.result.route:
Amin sets down his hammer and points to a covered cart outside. “They take copper goods to Acre. The driver is Hassan. Once I've fitted the handle, I'll come over with you and ask when he leaves.”

His daughter finishes the spout. Amin smooths the base, fits the handle, and pours half a cup of water to test it. Then he takes you to Hassan. Hassan is feeding the mules. He still has several crates to collect for his next journey and tells you to find him beside the shop when they are ready. You mark Acre and its road on your map. Amin carries the new jug over to Aziza.
ev.gap.damascus.scene.result.talk:
His daughter finishes the spout. Amin smooths the base, fits the handle, and taps the jug again. He listens, smiles, and hands it to you. “That's the sound. Give it a gentle tap.”

It rings clearly. Aziza's daughter arrives to collect it, and Amin pours a cup of water so she can see how the new spout works. Every drop lands in the cup. She carries the jug back across the street, and you mark the shop on your map.
ev.gap.damascus.scene.title: The Third Sound at the Coppersmith's
ev.gap.edessa.scene.body:
In a courtyard, Narin combs a bundle of wool while her sister Saba winds the finished strands. They are making a blanket for their mother, who complains that the old one lets the night air through. Saba says their mother also said the last blanket was too heavy. Narin holds up a handful of loose wool. “Then this one has to be just right.”

A boy from the next house has brought back the comb he borrowed. He asks whether the blanket is for their mother's bed or for the road. Saba once carried wool west toward Berrhoea, and he hopes she will tell that story again. Narin offers you a small tuft to try while Saba takes the boy's questions.

You ask whether their mother has seen the wool yet. ‘Only the bundle before we washed it,’ Saba says. Narin wants to keep the finished blanket hidden until the evening meal. The neighbour’s boy asks if their mother will notice it is lighter than the old one. ‘She notices every thread we leave hanging,’ Narin answers, pulling one loose fibre away. Saba puts the finished roll beside the loom and asks the boy to hold the door open while she brings in the next bundle. He does, then returns to the question he really came to ask about the road.
ev.gap.edessa.scene.choice.route: Listen to Saba's journey toward Berrhoea
ev.gap.edessa.scene.choice.talk: Try the comb and hear about the blanket
ev.gap.edessa.scene.result.route: Saba tells the boy how she travelled west with a bundle of wool, stopping where other travellers could find water and shelter. You ask for the names, and she repeats them while Narin goes on combing. The boy arranges pebbles on the floor for each stop. You add Edessa, Berrhoea, and the route between them to your map.
ev.gap.edessa.scene.result.talk: Narin shows you how to draw the comb through a little wool without pulling it apart. Her mother calls from the next room to ask whether the blanket is ready. “We have a traveller helping now,” Narin calls back. The mother asks you to make it light. You remember the courtyard and add this part of Edessa to your map.
ev.gap.edessa.scene.title: The Wool Comb in Narin's Courtyard
ev.gap.ephesus.scene.body:
A mason named Yusuf has laid stones beside a water channel near the houses. His apprentice Arda measures the next block with a worn wooden rule. They are making a low step so Yusuf's mother can reach the water without putting her jar on the ground.

Arda has marked the block too short. Yusuf asks him to measure again against the gap, and Arda sees where the rule slipped. “My grandmother will notice,” he says. Yusuf says she notices everything at the water place, including who has forgotten to eat.

A carrier who once took worked stone north toward Constantinople is waiting for the men to finish. He has time to tell you where he stopped on that journey while Arda makes a new line.

You ask whether Yusuf’s mother has asked for the step herself. ‘She says she can manage,’ Yusuf answers, ‘then leaves her jar halfway up while she catches her breath.’ Arda asks if she will be cross when she sees they changed the stones. Yusuf says she will probably test the step before giving an opinion. The carrier offers to bring a smaller flat stone from his cart. Arda measures it with the worn ruler and finds it fits the gap. He marks the edge again, more slowly, while Yusuf steadies the cord.
ev.gap.ephesus.scene.choice.route: Listen to the carrier's northern journey
ev.gap.ephesus.scene.choice.talk: Help Arda measure the step again
ev.gap.ephesus.scene.result.route: The carrier names the places where he stopped while travelling north toward Constantinople. Arda repeats the names under his breath as he works; he says he wants to see one of those towns someday. You mark Ephesus, Constantinople, and the route between them on your map. When the block is ready, the carrier helps set it in place before leaving.
ev.gap.ephesus.scene.result.talk: You hold the wooden rule against the gap. Arda makes a new mark and cuts the block to fit. Yusuf's mother comes for water and tries the step with her jar. She thanks Arda first, then Yusuf. You add the water place and this part of Ephesus to your map.
ev.gap.ephesus.scene.title: A Mason's Wooden Rule
ev.gap.hierusalem.scene.body:
At the spice stall, a boy grips a few coins and points to two packets of frankincense. "Which one does my grandmother like?" The seller asks who she is.

The boy says she lives in the south of town and always asks him to open the window a little when she burns incense. The seller opens both packets. The boy smells them for a long time, then turns towards the sound of cumin being ground next door.

The seller puts a little resin on charcoal and covers it with a copper hood. "Wait a moment. Does she like a light scent, or one that lingers?" The boy looks at you. "Can you help me remember? She's waiting for me at home."
ev.gap.hierusalem.scene.choice.route: Help him choose, then ask for the road to Acre
ev.gap.hierusalem.scene.choice.talk: Help the boy smell the two kinds of incense
ev.gap.hierusalem.scene.result.route:
The boy chooses the longer-lasting incense. The seller wraps it and turns to you. "Acre is north. Leave by the northern gate and find a caravan going to the coast. They'll know the wells and villages."

The boy says his grandmother went to Acre when she was young. She told him the sea wind filled her clothes, and he has always wanted to see whether it does. The seller laughs and sends him home before she has to wait any longer.
ev.gap.hierusalem.scene.result.talk:
The seller lifts the hood from each sample in turn. The first scent fades quickly; the second stays on the boy's sleeve. "Grandmother asks me to open the window because I make the charcoal too hot," he says. "She likes the second one."

The seller weighs a small packet and adds a grain for the boy to try at home. He holds it carefully on the way out. The seller tells him to let his grandmother tend the fire; the boy says he has learned something this time too.
ev.gap.hierusalem.scene.title: What Kind of Incense Grandmother Likes
ev.gap.ispahan.scene.body:
Parvin lifts a blue cloth from a washing tub. Her sister ordered it for a wedding in another town, and the cloth must be dry before the carriers leave. Her nephew brings a fresh bucket from the channel, careful now to keep the wooden clips tucked into his belt.

‘The colour still comes away on my fingers,’ Parvin says. ‘Another rinse, then we can hang it.’ Her nephew tries to lift the far end alone, and Parvin tells him to wait until someone can take the other side. A caravan master bound for Basra has a courtyard nearby; she has spoken to him this morning.

You ask whether the bride has chosen the darker edge herself. Parvin says her sister asked the girl to come and look at two samples before deciding; she chose this one and wrote her name on the back of the order. The nephew wants to find that paper so they can check the colour again. Parvin tells him to keep his hands dry before he touches it. The neighbour from the channel arrives with her linen and offers to help hold the line when the blue cloth goes up. Parvin thanks her and tests the rinse water one more time.
ev.gap.ispahan.scene.choice.talk: Help rinse and hang the cloth
ev.gap.ispahan.scene.result.route:
Parvin tells you which courtyard the caravan master uses and where the road turns west toward Basra. You mark the route and the city while her nephew repeats the courtyard name so you can find it.

While you ask for the caravan courtyard, Parvin and her nephew finish the last rinse and clip the blue cloth to the line. The neighbour holds the rope steady. The cloth is ready to dry before its later carrier arrives.
ev.gap.ispahan.scene.result.talk: You and her nephew lift the cloth between you. Parvin checks the water and finally says it is clear enough. She clips one end to the line and leaves the other to him, watching as he fastens it securely. You mark her workshop in Isfahan on your map.
ev.gap.ispahan.scene.title: Parvin’s Blue Cloth
ev.gap.moscovia.scene.body:
A fur seller named Pavel turns a pelt over in his hands. His mother wants a warm lining for her coat, and he has kept this one for her. His apprentice nearly hangs it beside the fire to dry.

‘In the shade,’ Pavel reminds him. ‘She complained last time when the edge curled.’ The apprentice carries it away, smiling at the thought of Pavel’s mother inspecting his work. Pavel knows the road south toward Kyiv if you need it.
