You ask what has delayed them. The captain holds up a wet rope. It slipped during loading, and he wants a new knot before anyone carries another bundle aboard. The pilot says the water is still favourable, then kneels to help the sailor tie it. His niece writes the time beside the tide mark.

A porter arrives with the last cargo bundle. He asks whether to put it down or wait. The captain points to dry stones until the rope is secure. The pilot’s niece moves the leather dice cup away from the splash and leaves it beside you while the knot is tested.
ev.ormus.astrodice_tide.choice.cast: Cast the three dice for this departure
ev.ormus.astrodice_tide.choice.sail: Ask the captain and prepare to sail
ev.ormus.astrodice_tide.title: Before the Tide Turns
ev.ormus.b.body:
In a spice warehouse, an Indian trader is trying to read the labels his son tied on the sacks. The boy has written the ship’s name where the buyer’s name should go. ‘Both names matter,’ his father says, and makes room on a clean tag. An older porter brings the sack back from the doorway before it can be loaded onto the wrong caravan.

The trader offers a full pepper lot for 150 silver. At a nearby stall, his wife has a small dish of dried ginger for 3 silver; she warms a piece over the brazier and lets you smell it. You ask how the goods move onward. The porter explains which boats cross toward Calatu and which inland caravans take goods toward Cobinan.

The son copies the two names in the right places. His mother calls from the stall, asking whether the ginger is ready for the traveller. He glances at you, then at his father, waiting to see which tag needs the next knot.
ev.ormus.b.choice.ginger: Buy and eat a small ginger portion for 3 silver
ev.ormus.b.choice.pepper: Buy the full pepper lot for 150 silver
ev.ormus.b.choice.trade_routes: Ask about Calatu and Cobinan trade routes
ev.ormus.b.title: The Spice Warehouse Tags
ev.ormus.c.body:
A hot wind reaches the port lane while a dates seller is tying down his awning. His sister is bringing water jars inside; her little son insists he can carry one alone. She gives him the smallest and asks you to help with the heavy pair. The seller looks up at the dust rising beyond the roofs and calls to a guide who knows when the gusts usually ease.

‘Will it pass before supper?’ the boy asks. The guide says he will watch the sky for a while before promising anything. You ask where the family keeps cool when the shutters are closed. The sister shows you a lower room where the jars stand out of the heat. A neighbour is already there, sewing a torn shade cloth.

The guide offers two days of help reading the weather for 1.5 silver. The family can also give you space to wait out several windy days. The seller pulls the last knot tight and asks his sister whether all the jars are safely inside.
ev.ormus.c.choice.guide: Pay the guide 1.5 silver for two days
ev.ormus.c.choice.observe: Watch how the neighbours prepare for the wind
ev.ormus.c.choice.wait: Wait out the wind for three days
ev.ormus.c.title: When the Hot Wind Reaches the Lane
ev.ormus.entry.body:
At the Hormuz landing, a trader’s daughter is checking the cords on a steel shipment before it goes from a boat to a pack animal. Her father has written the count on a wooden tag, but she finds one bundle with no tag at all. ‘If it goes inland unnamed, someone will count it twice,’ she says. He asks the porter to put it back on dry ground.

A pilot nearby is explaining the tide to a young sailor who wants to leave before his mother arrives with food. ‘She knows this landing better than you,’ the pilot says. The mother appears with a covered bowl and asks whether the boat has water for the crossing. You help the porter keep the steel bundle away from the spray while the trader and his daughter agree on its mark.

The trader offers the full Damascus steel lot for 146 silver. The customs desk will need two days to clear other cargo, and the pilot has time later to talk about the port. His daughter ties the tag firmly, then checks it once more before letting the porter lift the bundle.
ev.ormus.entry.choice.customs: Spend two days clearing cargo at the customs desk
ev.ormus.entry.choice.lore: Spend a day talking with the pilot
ev.ormus.entry.choice.market: Buy the Damascus steel lot for 146 silver
ev.ormus.entry.title: At the Hormuz Landing
ev.ormus.mentor_astrodice.body:
A pilot at the Hormuz landing has three marked dice in a leather cup. His niece is making a tide list for the crews while her father answers a sailor who wants to know whether to cast before departure. ‘First tell me whether the water jars are aboard,’ the pilot says. The sailor admits one is still at the well and goes to fetch it.

The niece shows you the marks on the dice and asks what you would want to know before crossing. You mention wind. She writes it beside the tide, then asks her father whether she has forgotten anything. ‘The boat itself,’ he says, pointing to a frayed rope laid across the table. You ask whether the dice can settle that. He smiles and gives you the rope to inspect.

He teaches the dice over seven days for 70 silver, beginning with the names of their faces. If you only want an explanation now, he will read one example while his niece finishes the tide list. The sailor returns with the last water jar, breathing hard but pleased to have remembered it.
ev.ormus.mentor_astrodice.choice.ask: Ask the pilot to explain one cast
ev.ormus.mentor_astrodice.choice.learn: Pay 70 silver for seven days of star-dice lessons
ev.ormus.mentor_astrodice.title: The Pilot’s Three Dice
ev.ormus.netweight.body:
At a fishing boat, a woman is repairing a net while her brother searches a basket for one missing weight. Their father made the weights from small pieces of fired clay; the last one broke when the net caught on a stone. The brother says they can sail with a gap. She shakes the net and shows him how one corner lifts without the weight.

You ask whether the boat must leave today. ‘When the tide is right,’ she says, ‘after this corner stays down.’ A boy from the neighbouring boat offers a spare weight, but it is too heavy. The brother chooses a smaller clay weight from the basket and asks you to hold the mesh while he ties it on. The woman tests the net in shallow water and calls him back to shorten the cord.

She can pay you 0.5 silver if you stay and help them finish the net, or show you how she sets the weights if you have little time. Her brother passes you the loose corner and waits for your hand.
ev.ormus.netweight.choice.finish: Stay a day and finish the net
ev.ormus.netweight.choice.learn: Ask how the weights are set
ev.ormus.netweight.result.finish: You spend the day helping fit the weights. In shallow water the net settles evenly, and the siblings take it aboard before the tide changes. The woman pays you 0.5 silver; their father will find his work in use again.
ev.ormus.netweight.result.learn: She shows you why the corner rose and how she spaces each weight. You write it down while her brother adjusts the last cord; the boy from the next boat retrieves his heavy spare.
ev.ormus.netweight.title: A Weight for the Fishing Net
ev.paukin.entry.body: When you leave Coiganju you ride south-east for a day along a causeway laid with fine stone, which you find at this entrance to Manzi. On either hand there is a great expanse of water, so that you cannot enter the province except along this causeway. At the end of the day’s journey you reach the fine city of PAUKIN. The people are Idolaters, burn their dead, are subject to the Great Kaan, and use paper-money. They live by trade and manufactures and have great abundance of silk, whereof they weave a great variety of fine stuffs of silk and gold. Of all the necessaries of life there is great store.
ev.paukin.entry.choice.look: Rest and ask what men say of this place
ev.paukin.entry.title: Of the Cities of Paukin and Cayu
ev.pein.entry.body: Pein is a province five days in length, lying between east and north-east. The people are worshippers of Mahommet, and subjects of the Great Kaan. There are a good number of towns and villages, but the most noble is PEIN, the capital of the kingdom. There are rivers in this country, in which quantities of Jasper and Chalcedony are found. The people have plenty of all products, including cotton. They live by manufactures and trade. But they have a custom that I must relate.
ev.pein.entry.choice.look: Rest and ask what men say of this place
ev.pein.entry.title: Of the Province of Pein
ev.pein.site_gap.body: A salt seller shows you two pinches, one grey and one bright. He wets them with a small spoon so you can taste. Good salt tastes clean; a dark colour alone does not make it poor, but sand and damp clumps matter. A camel chews dry grass nearby. He dries a tested pinch in a clay dish to see whether its grains separate again.
ev.pein.site_gap.choice.route: Ask about the road to Yarcan
ev.pein.site_gap.title: The Salt Seller’s Tasting Spoon
ev.pentam.entry.body: When you leave Locac and sail for 500 miles towards the south, you come to an island called PENTAM, a very wild place. All the wood that grows thereon consists of odoriferous trees. There is no more to say about it; so let us sail about sixty miles further between those two Islands. Throughout this distance there is but four paces’ depth of water, so that great ships in passing this channel have to lift their rudders, for they draw nearly as much water as that. And when you have gone these 60 miles, and again about 30 more, you come to an Island which forms a Kingdom, and is called MALAIUR.
ev.pentam.entry.choice.look: Rest and ask what men say of this place
ev.pentam.entry.title: Of the Island Called Pentam, and the City Malaiur
ev.petra.entry.body:
You follow a narrow gorge into Petra. Old water channels are still visible along the rock. Near the opening, Rashida has stretched a cloth shelter and moved the waterskins into its shade. Her grandson Sami counts with pebbles. Each time someone has a bowl of water, he moves one pebble to the other side.

“Why haven't we touched that skin?” Sami asks.

“It's for your father,” Rashida says. “He went to look for the goats beyond the slope. Last time he came back late, everyone had drunk the water. He ate dry bread first and waited.”

Sami says his father had forgotten to take a waterskin with him. Rashida laughs. “This time I'm remembering for him.” She sees you standing nearby and sets out an empty bowl. Sami quickly moves a pebble back. He says a guest should drink before he counts it.
ev.petra.entry.choice.pass: Thank Rashida and continue through the gorge
ev.petra.entry.choice.rest: Spend a day beneath Rashida's shelter
ev.petra.entry.title: Petra
ev.petra.goatbell.body:
Beside a rock face with a carved doorway, Inan is looking for a grey goat. His daughter Maya hears a bell and takes a few steps into the gorge. Then the sound seems to come from the other side, and she stops.

“Which way did it go?” she asks.

Inan looks at the hoofprints. “It went around that big rock and into the shade. The sound moves between the walls. We'll follow the prints.” Maya says this was the first goat she had been trusted to watch alone. She hurried away to help carry water that morning and did not tie its rope tightly enough.

Inan lets her take a moment. He lays the grass he brought beside the stone steps. “It might come out when it smells this. Will you follow the prints with her, or wait here with us?”

You ask Maya what she calls the goat. ‘Cloud,’ she says, because its grey back looks pale in the morning. Inan asks whether Cloud knows the sound of her grain pouch. Maya shakes it gently; the goat bleats from behind the stone. ‘There you are,’ she says, but her father asks her to walk slowly so it will not bolt farther into the shade. She looks back at the loose rope in her hand and asks him to show her the knot once more when they reach it.
ev.petra.goatbell.choice.wait: Wait by the stone steps and rest overnight
ev.petra.goatbell.result.tracks:
You and Maya walk around the large rock and find the grey goat beside a narrow crevice. It is eating a low patch of grass, the bell still around its neck. Maya holds out the cut grass and waits until it approaches before taking the rope. This time she ties the knot twice and asks her father to pull it tight.

Inan pats the goat and thanks you. Back at the resting place he tells the nearby families what happened. When you pass them again, they call you over for water.
ev.petra.goatbell.result.wait:
You wait beside the steps with Inan and Maya until dark. Maya starts towards the gorge several times, but Inan asks her to listen. The bell is drawing closer. The grey goat looks out from behind the rock wall. Maya lures it over with grass and reties the loosened rope.

Inan's family asks you to stay and shares warm bread and soup. You sleep against the rock that night and leave the next morning with your strength restored.
ev.petra.goatbell.title: A Bell in the Gorge
ev.road.00.body: Two camps share a well on the steppe. Rain has cut a fresh rut across the path, and a cart from the southern camp sits with one wheel sunk to the hub. The courier who moved the route stone after the storm kneels beside it. “I thought I was keeping people off the soft ground,” he tells the herder. “The stone sent us straight into it,” she answers, though she helps him lift the wheel. His daughter brings out a sketch she made before the rain. Her pony slipped at the old bend, so she marked the firmer track by the scrub. “Take this to the keeper at the far well,” the herder says. “He knows where both camps come in.” Going there to settle the marker adds two days to your journey. A guide whose family keeps other wells offers a longer circuit for a fee; it adds four days. The daughter holds the paper flat against the wind while the adults study it.
ev.road.00.choice.choice_0: Take the disputed track with the courier's sketch
ev.road.00.choice.choice_1: Pay a fee for the guide's four-day circuit
ev.road.00.title: The Marker Between Two Camps
ev.road.01.body: At a river landing on the road, a ferry keeper has taken up the planks used by heavy wagons. A young clerk arrives with a bag of letters and stops at the gap. “The seals are dry now. How do I get them across?” The keeper points upstream to his mother’s small boat. She is carrying a load of reeds to the bank and calls back, “I can take people and light bags, a few at a time. Wrap the letters before you step in.” The clerk pulls an oilcloth from his sleeve. “Would this do?” She makes him tuck the loose corner under the bag. Her boat charges a fare. The keeper will repair the heavy landing so carts and animals can follow; waiting for both crossings adds two days. The keeper can also arrange guarded landings for a larger travelling party; that route charges a higher fee and adds three days. The clerk holds out the wrapped bag for the woman to inspect.
ev.road.01.choice.choice_0: Pay the boat fare and carry your baggage upstream
ev.road.01.choice.choice_1: Pay a fee for the guarded landings
ev.road.01.title: The Ferry Keeper's Second Landing
ev.road.02.body: Beside an orchard on the road, a cart has pushed through the wrong opening and left an irrigation gate swinging. The owner catches the water running down the wheel track. “My sister comes to pick apricots in the morning,” he tells the driver. “The lower trees need this water tonight.” His nephew wedges the gate shut and points to the public road beside an old boundary wall. “I’ll put a sign there before the next cart arrives.” A traveller remembers an old tale about a ruler who fooled young men with a garden. The nephew gives him an apricot. “My uncle grew these. Help me keep the ditch open.” Walking the proper turn with the nephew and fixing the sign adds two days to your journey. An escort offers the longer public road for a fee; it adds four days but keeps the carts away from the orchard. The owner checks the gate once more while the nephew looks for a board to paint.
ev.road.02.choice.choice_0: Follow the nephew and help mark the orchard turn
ev.road.02.choice.choice_1: Pay a fee for the longer escorted road
ev.road.02.title: The Orchard by the Old Wall
ev.road.03.body: At an island jetty, a boatbuilder is repairing the steering oar of the vessel you have joined. The cook turns a water jar and finds a thin stream running from its base. “That one was for the rowers,” she says. “If we do not refill soon, they will have to share the little one.” A pilot draws two channels in wet sand. The short passage passes a shoal shifted by the last storm; sounding it will add two days to the journey. “Can the oar bear a scrape?” the cook asks. The boatbuilder fits a spare and makes her test the lashings herself. “It can, if you do not force it against the bottom.” The pilot knows a chain of sheltered harbours as well. His fare covers that longer passage, which adds four days. The cook puts the leaking jar where everyone can see it and asks the crew to fill the sound ones first.
ev.road.03.choice.choice_0: Take the short channel and sound the shoals
ev.road.03.choice.choice_1: Pay a fee for the sheltered harbours
ev.road.03.title: The Boat at the Island Jetty
ev.road.04.body: Two groups of riders meet at a steppe waystation, each asking after a horse with a white mark on its foreleg. One rider holds a loose bridle and says the horse carried her younger sister’s bedding. The keeper’s grandson has been tracking prints in the dry streambed. “It went east with a mixed herd,” he says. The second rider frowns. “Our animals went west.” The boy presses his thumb beside a fresh hoofprint. “This one crossed behind the others. Let me follow it before more carts blur the marks.” The streambed is also the way your party meant to travel. Waiting for the search and helping clear the soft bank will add two days. A hired guide offers a loop through watched grazing ground instead; his fee and the circuit add four days. The first rider gives the boy a strip torn from the horse’s blanket so he can recognize it.
ev.road.04.choice.choice_0: Wait for the searchers, then take the streambed
ev.road.04.choice.choice_1: Pay a fee for the grazing-ground loop
ev.road.04.title: The Horse Line at the Waystation
ev.road.05.body: At a steep section of road, a pilgrim and her father are replacing a loose iron handhold beside the steps. A water carrier has stopped at the foot of the climb with two full jars; she cannot use that step until they finish. The pilgrim shows you a drawing of a distant mountain shrine she hopes to visit, where long chains help people climb. “I drew the chains first,” she says, “then I saw how little room the carriers had to put a jar down.” Her father pulls the new fastening. “It holds my weight. Try it with a pack before anyone carries water past it.” Testing the steps and helping people up will add two days to your journey. Porters offer to take baggage by a gentler road for a fee; that trip adds five days. The water carrier sets one jar on a flat stone and waits for the pilgrim to call her forward.
ev.road.05.choice.choice_0: Test the handhold and take the hill steps
ev.road.05.choice.choice_1: Pay a fee for the porters' gentler road
ev.road.05.title: The Chain on the Hill Path
ev.road.06.body: At a road station, a courier is saddling two horses while his sister sorts the mail. She pulls out a sealed bag for an office beside a river. “The clerk wrote twice asking for it,” she says. Her brother puts the bag inside his own satchel. “I have the first horse. The other is for a paying traveller, if they can keep pace at the bends.” She checks the second girth and makes him tighten it again. At the gate a potter is waiting with bowls wrapped in straw. “The cook down the ordinary road asked for these,” he tells you. “She taps every bowl before she pays. Take her receipt, and keep the agreed share from the sale.” The hired relay horse takes a one-day detour beyond your planned route; carrying the bowls to the cook and returning to your route adds two days. The sister holds up the sealed mailbag once more so her brother can check the knot.
ev.road.06.choice.choice_0: Pay a fee and ride with the courier
ev.road.06.choice.choice_1: Carry the potter's bowls for an agreed share
ev.road.06.title: The Courier's Empty Saddle
ev.road.07.body: Beside a road, a sailor from Abash is repairing the tack of two horses brought by ship. One shies when a cart wheel bumps a stone. “They stood on a rolling deck for weeks,” he tells the mounted caravan leader. “Let them find their feet before you ask them to run.” The leader rubs the horse’s neck and offers you a paid place with his party; going with them adds two days to your journey. The sailor has another problem: a stable farther along the ordinary road ordered spare straps, but he must stay until the buyer comes for the horses. He ties a knot the stable keeper will recognize. “She pays the normal price there,” he says. “Keep your agreed share from that money and send the rest back.” Making the delivery adds three days. He shows you where the leather must sit so the keeper can test it on a horse.
ev.road.07.choice.choice_0: Pay a fee for the two-day mounted caravan
ev.road.07.choice.choice_1: Sell the spare tack and keep a commission
ev.road.07.title: The Abash Sailor's Tack
ev.road.08.body: On a road, a cart carrying pottery from Taianfu drops a wheel into a rut. The potter listens to the cups rattle inside their crate. “I packed the corners myself,” she says, “but the last turn was hard.” Her father opens the lid and finds that one handful of straw has slipped. “Hold the box while I push it back,” he asks you. The potter lifts a cup and turns it toward the light to check its rim. A passing caravan can give you and your baggage a paid place; its change of animals will add one day to your planned journey. The potter also has a crate ordered by a tea seller along the ordinary road. “She counts every cup,” she says. “Bring me her marked receipt; take your share from what she pays.” Carrying that crate and returning to your route adds two days. Her father closes the lid only after the cups stop moving.
ev.road.08.choice.choice_0: Pay a fee for the one-day caravan
ev.road.08.choice.choice_1: Deliver the cups and keep a commission
ev.road.08.title: The Potter from Taianfu
ev.road.09.body: At a market, a dyer spreads white cloth for a family gathering. His daughter measures the second bolt and notices it ends a handspan early. The buyer holds the first piece against her arm. “Both must cover the same tables,” she says. “Give me a moment,” the daughter answers. “I can trim the long one and stitch the cut edge neatly.” Her father asks her to save the offcut for patching a canopy, then turns to the cloth still stacked behind him. Another household beyond the next market ordered part of it. A hired merchant train will carry you past the exchange point for a fee, adding two days to your planned journey. Delivering and selling the cloth to that household adds three days; the dyer offers you an agreed share of what the buyer pays. His daughter writes the buyer’s name on a slip and asks you to make sure it travels with the right bolt.
ev.road.09.choice.choice_0: Pay a fee for the two-day merchant train
ev.road.09.choice.choice_1: Sell the dyer's cloth for an agreed share
ev.road.09.title: The White Cloth Order
ev.road.10.body: Beside a road, a pearl seller who trades at coastal markets has overturned a small box by his weighing table. His apprentice kneels in the dust and counts each pearl as he returns it. “Forty-nine,” he says, looking at the empty lid. The seller wets a cloth and wipes under the table legs. “Wait before you blame the road. One may be caught in the mat.” A guarded caravan is leaving for a nearby market; a paid place with it adds one day to your journey. The seller cannot leave his table until the count is right. He hands you a different packet, sealed and already checked: shell beads ordered by a workshop along your road. “Ask the maker to mark my receipt,” he says. “Keep the share we agreed from her payment.” Taking the packet there adds two days. The apprentice lifts the edge of the mat while you choose your road.
ev.road.10.choice.choice_0: Pay a fee for the one-day guarded caravan
ev.road.10.choice.choice_1: Deliver the shell beads for a commission
ev.road.10.title: The Pearl Seller's Count
ev.road.11.body: At a steppe station, a storyteller has gathered listeners around an old account of Chinggis Khan and the ruler it calls Prester John. A boy interrupts when the reader mentions riders bearing a letter. “Would one letter really bring all of them?” His mother, the station keeper, sets today’s sealed packets beside him. “This one goes only to the next station,” she says. “Another rider takes it farther.” The boy turns the packet over, looking for the knot. A harness trader at the same table is tying a label to a bundle for the next camp. “Show him mine,” he tells the keeper. “If the knot comes loose, the buyer will not know whose straps these are.” The keeper offers you a paid place with her relay riders; taking that route adds two days. Selling the trader’s bundle along the ordinary road adds three, and he promises you an agreed share of the sale. The boy holds the loose end of the label while the trader finishes the knot.
ev.road.11.choice.choice_0: Pay a fee for the two-day horse relay
ev.road.11.choice.choice_1: Sell the harness bundle for a commission
ev.road.11.title: The Old Letter and the New Horse
ev.road.12.body: At a roadside district office, a clerk discovers that his copy of a land register has one page twice and another page missing. The assistant spreads the original sheets across the table. “The missing names are here,” she says, putting a weight on the corner before the wind takes it. The clerk points to a line that runs into the margin. “Copy that one fully. The receiving office must be able to find the household.” An official courier waits by the door for the corrected pages. He has a paid place in his party; taking it adds one day to your journey. The assistant also has paper ordered by a school along the ordinary road. “One class has been sharing the same sheet for maps,” she says. “Their teacher asked for another bundle.” Taking it to the school adds two days, and the assistant promises you an agreed share of the sale. She dips her pen and asks the clerk to read the missing name again.
ev.road.12.choice.choice_0: Pay a fee for the one-day courier caravan
ev.road.12.choice.choice_1: Deliver the school paper for a commission
ev.road.12.title: The Clerk's Second Copy
ev.road.13.body: At a coastal landing, a fisherwoman and her son are turning fish on bamboo racks before the afternoon rain. A sailor waiting for the tide points to two islands on his chart and repeats an old tale that men and women lived apart on them. The son asks, “How did they carry water between the islands?” The sailor studies the chart. “The person who told me never said. I saw only one landing when I passed.” His mother moves a rack out of the spray. “Then help me with the fish you can see,” she tells the boy. He asks whether you can hold the mat while he ties the dried bundles for a buyer. The sailor has room on his boat and knows a channel that adds one day to your journey for a fare. Staying to dry and load the catch adds two days. The son presses a corner of the mat under a stone as the first drops fall.
ev.road.13.choice.choice_0: Pay the boat fare and sail with the tidewise crew
ev.road.13.choice.choice_1: Stay two days to dry and load the fish
ev.road.13.title: The Fish Drying Racks
ev.road.14.body: At a road station, a young keeper has pinned up two route lists for the coming season. On her father’s copy, the watering place stands before a sharp bend; on the newer one, it stands beyond. A driver who used the road last month points to the old well mark. “That one dried up. We watered beyond the bend,” he says. “Was there a trough?” the keeper asks. “Under a cover, but I did not see who filled it.” She wants to ask at the next two stations before changing the list, and invites you to help check the answers; that work adds two days to your journey. A caravan whose drivers have already found the new well offers you a paid place. Following them to the trough and back to your road adds one day. The keeper holds the two sheets against the wall and leaves a blank space where the new mark should go.
ev.road.14.choice.choice_0: Check both lists with the keeper over two days
ev.road.14.choice.choice_1: Pay to ride with the caravan that has checked the water
ev.road.14.title: The Two Route Lists
ev.road.15.body: A returning courier is finishing a road report at a station. A local elder glances over his list of halts and taps a blank place between two names. “You missed the bridge my brothers repaired,” she says. The courier looks up. “The wooden span by the old mill?” “Those boards are gone,” she answers. “The stone piers still carry a new deck.” He asks her to repeat the bridge’s name so he can put it in the report. She says the name slowly, then remembers the flood that swept away the old boards. She turns the paper toward you. “The driver also needs to know which bank the road reaches after rain.” You can help them check the wording at the table without delaying your journey. The elder is willing to walk to the bridge and show the bank and wheel marks herself; that visit and return add one day. The courier holds his pen over the empty line, waiting for a direction he can trust.
ev.road.15.choice.choice_0: Help the courier finish his report here
ev.road.15.choice.choice_1: Walk with the elder to check the bridge route
ev.road.15.title: The Bridge Missing from the Report
ev.road.16.body: On the steppe, two herding families bring their animals toward the same well. A stone marker has been moved and now sends one family into a dry hollow. The woman who got there first tips her empty bucket toward her brother. “The lambs followed that stone. They cannot wait while we argue.” An older herder remembers a tale about Chinggis Khan and the ruler called Prester John in which a marker was mentioned, but his grandson shakes his head. “The old people did not stand here after last spring’s flood.” The brother asks you to walk from both approaches and help reset the stone where riders can see it; the work adds a day to your journey. His son has found older stones beside a narrow watercourse and wants company while he checks whether the smaller flock can pass. That search also adds a day. The woman passes a skin of water to her neighbour before either family moves its animals.
ev.road.16.choice.choice_0: Spend a day setting a marker both families can use
ev.road.16.choice.choice_1: Spend a day checking the watercourse with the son
ev.road.16.title: The Marker Near the Old Story
ev.road.17.body: Outside a roadside camp, a saddler is checking repaired tack against the horse keeper’s list. One saddle has no new girth strap. “I tied it to the spare frame so it would not drag in the dust,” the saddler says. The keeper turns the frame over and finds only an old broken strap. A stable boy comes out carrying an empty sack. “I moved a bundle to make space for the feed,” he admits. “Was it the one with the blue knot?” The saddler asks him to show where he put it and invites you to help match the pieces to the list. That can be settled while your party rests. He also has finished tack ordered at the next post and offers a delivery wage if you carry it there; the side trip adds a day. The horse keeper keeps one finger on the missing line until the boy returns from the storeroom.
ev.road.17.choice.choice_0: Help match the saddlery to the keeper’s list
ev.road.17.choice.choice_1: Take the repaired tack to the next post for a wage
ev.road.17.title: The Saddler’s Missing Strap
ev.road.18.body: At a town granary, a mother has come with an old ration token and her youngest child. The new list does not show the family’s full name. “Eight of us still live in the same house,” she tells the clerk. The child adds, “The grain cart went past our door last time.” The mother points to the broken drain on their street and says a loaded cart must come from the other end. The clerk finds a shortened form of their name on another page, but he wants to compare the old token before he alters the ledger. Helping him and carrying the allotment to the family adds one day to your journey. A driver loading the grain cart offers you a place among the sacks. “Ride with me and you will see which streets take a full cart,” she says. Helping her make the deliveries also adds a day, and she can point out the sound roads. The mother keeps hold of the token while the clerk reads the shortened name aloud to her.
ev.road.18.choice.choice_0: Check the register and take the family its grain
ev.road.18.choice.choice_1: Ride with the grain cart and learn the town roads
ev.road.18.title: The Family Missing from the Grain List
ev.road.19.body: At a post station, a merchant receives a letter he sent to his sister weeks ago. The envelope is still sealed, with a note saying that no one found the town. “She lives by the eastern gate,” he tells the clerk. “I have been there. Her children will think I forgot them.” The clerk opens his register to two similar place names and asks which branch of the river runs past the gate. The merchant traces it on the map at your elbow, but his finger stops between the two lines. You can help them check the address and add both names to the envelope while the mail is being sorted; this need not delay your journey. The merchant also offers a delivery wage if you carry the letter to the next post and obtain a receipt; that errand adds a day. He keeps the unopened letter on the table until the clerk reads the two names back.
ev.road.19.choice.choice_0: Help the clerk match the letter’s place name
ev.road.19.choice.choice_1: Carry the letter to the next post for a wage
ev.road.19.title: Two Names for One Place
ev.road.20.body: Beside a road, a falconer has stopped his group under a tree. An apprentice holds a bird on his glove while the falconer examines a leather jess worn thin where it touches the leg. “It came back to me,” the boy says, “but if the strap breaks tomorrow, I may not find it.” The falconer opens his repair pouch and gives the apprentice a fresh strip. “Hold the perch level. I will cut it to the old length first.” The boy asks you to steady the stand while his teacher fits the new leather; the repair can be done during your party’s halt. He also knows a raised path around wet ground, marked with poles that remain visible after rain. Following him round the marsh adds two days to your journey, but he can teach you which marks lead back to the main road. The falconer asks the boy to feel the new leather for any rough edge. The bird shifts its feet, and the boy waits for it to settle before touching the strap.
ev.road.20.choice.choice_0: Help the falconer replace the worn jess
ev.road.20.choice.choice_1: Follow the apprentice around the marsh for two days
ev.road.20.title: The Falconer’s Worn Jess
ev.road.21.body: At a steppe waystation, a caravan driver is being held until a missing load tag is found. The station steward says one sealed bale cannot be released without it. The driver's daughter has the tally her father wrote at the last camp. She asks the steward to let her father water the horses while the papers are checked. He nods, but keeps the sealed bale beside his desk. “This mark is the same as the one on the bale,” she says, but the steward wants a second witness. An older porter offers to walk back with you and check the previous station; that will add two days to your journey. A guide with a place in a departing party can take you on a one-day detour if you pay his fee. The daughter folds her father's tally so the mark remains visible and asks whether you will help her find the tag before the cart loses another day.
ev.road.21.choice.choice_0: Spend two days checking the driver's tally and tag
ev.road.21.choice.choice_1: Pay the guide and continue with the departing party
ev.road.21.title: The Missing Load Tag
ev.road.22.body: At a roadside lodging house in western Asia, two merchants are loading their pack animals for another stage. Their niece is making her first long journey with them. She finds a letter for home under a folded cloth and calls after her uncle. “If this stays here, Mother will think we left without a word.” He asks you to check the names on their parcels while they still have the table, and the niece writes the letter's destination on the list. The lodging keeper offers wax for the letter's seal. The niece asks her uncle to read the destination back, and he does it twice until she is satisfied. The merchants also need one packet carried to the next stop, a day's detour from your route, and offer a delivery wage if you go with them.
ev.road.22.choice.choice_0: Help the family check the letter and parcel list
ev.road.22.choice.choice_1: Carry their packet for a day and take the agreed wage
ev.road.22.title: The Niece’s First Journey
ev.road.23.body: Two travelling camps on the steppe intend to water their horses at the same shallow pool. A boy sent ahead returns with dry mud on his boots. “There is only enough for the first animals,” he says. His aunt has heard of a channel behind the grass but cannot leave the young horses alone. The boy points to a bent willow: 'The grass parts there after rain.' His aunt asks him to mark the safe return path before he goes. She asks whether you will spend an extra day checking it with the boy. The camp's water carrier unfolds her own well list for a caravan leader. He asks you to check its markings with her and make him a legible copy. He offers to pay for that work while your party rests. The water carrier asks him how many horses he has, then checks the last well on her list before you copy it.
ev.road.23.choice.choice_0: Spend a day finding the channel with the boy
ev.road.23.choice.choice_1: Check and copy the camp's well list for a wage
ev.road.23.title: The Water Below the Dry Grass
ev.road.24.body: Two brothers arrive at a steppe camp from different directions, each with a herd of horses. Their ropes have become tangled around the same row of posts. “Mine need the windy side,” the elder says. The younger points to a mare that strayed during the confusion. Their aunt has brought spare rope and asks both to move their animals before dusk. 'The mare knows the sheltered hollow,' she tells the younger brother. 'Take a lead rope, but first let me clear these posts.' He gives her the loose end of his line. You can help her divide the tether places now, or spend an extra day with the younger brother following the mare's hoofprints toward the next hollow. The elder brother holds his herd still while his aunt makes room between the two lines.
ev.road.24.choice.choice_0: Help the aunt divide the tether places
ev.road.24.choice.choice_1: Follow the younger brother for a day to find the mare
ev.road.24.title: Two Herds at One Camp
ev.road.25.body: At a steppe stopping place, a messenger brings a sharply worded letter from the next camp. A family there lent out its well bucket and has heard it was broken. The borrower holds up the repaired handle. “I meant to bring it back at the next watering,” she says. The messenger reads the letter aloud, then waits for an answer. The borrower shows him the new pin holding the handle. 'Tell him I fitted this myself,' she says. 'I will,' the messenger answers, 'but give me a day I can write down.' You can help both families agree on the return and write it down here. Or you can carry the reply to the next camp on a one-day detour; the borrower offers a delivery wage because she must stay with her animals. She touches the repaired handle once more before handing the messenger a clean scrap for her reply.
ev.road.25.choice.choice_0: Help the families agree on when to return the bucket
ev.road.25.choice.choice_1: Carry their reply for a day and take the wage
ev.road.25.title: A Letter About a Borrowed Bucket
ev.road.26.body: Before a steppe caravan sets out, its leader and horse keeper disagree over how many filled skins each cart should carry. A tired driver braces his hand against a wheel. “Another full skin will put this axle in the mud.” The keeper points to the animals waiting behind him. “Then count them with the people. They will drink before the next well.” The leader opens the tally and discovers one skin marked full has not been checked since yesterday. She asks you to stay and inspect the loads with them; dividing the water will add a day to your journey. A young scout has seen a gap in the bank of a dry channel beyond the first bend. “If the carts can cross there, we can spread the load,” he says. Going to test that crossing and returning to the road will add two days. The tired driver loosens a strap while the others wait for the count.
ev.road.26.choice.choice_0: Spend a day counting and dividing the water skins
ev.road.26.choice.choice_1: Spend two days checking the scout’s crossing
ev.road.26.title: The Water Skins Before Departure
ev.road.27.body: After rain, a narrow steppe track can take only one family’s carts at a time. The elders gather beside a fence to decide the order. A young scribe reads the first names back, then stops. “I missed the last one.” An older woman points to three carts at the south fence. “They are mine. My son is waiting with the oxen.” The scribe asks her to say the family name slowly while the others listen. You can help finish the list now and hang it where arriving carts will see it. Nearby, the camp’s water carrier has a rough list of working wells. A caravan head asks you to check it with her and make a clean copy; that work adds a day, and he offers a wage. The water carrier puts a wet finger beside the well she filled from yesterday and waits for you to read its name.
ev.road.27.choice.choice_0: Help the scribe complete the order of carts
ev.road.27.choice.choice_1: Check the camp's wells and copy the list for a wage
ev.road.27.title: The Last Name on the Council List
ev.road.28.body: Two caravans meet at a shallow steppe ford after rain. The leading cart turns sharply, and several marked bundles slip into the current. A woman driving the next cart calls for help, then asks the others to leave a clear place for the animals to stand. “The first horse is still shaking,” she says. A merchant wades to the edge, sees his mark on one wet bundle and asks who can carry the rescued goods on. He has spare pack animals for that job and offers a wage if you take his load to the next station; the delivery adds two days to your journey. Staying to pull the bundles ashore and mark the firm crossing adds one day. The woman asks the merchant to read the marks aloud before anyone lifts a bundle; he names two that belong to another caravan. She tests the shallows with a pole while he spreads a dry cloth for the goods.
ev.road.28.choice.choice_0: Spend a day recovering loads and marking the ford
ev.road.28.choice.choice_1: Carry the merchant’s rescued loads for two days
ev.road.28.title: The Loads in the Shallow Ford
ev.road.29.body: At a western Asian resting place, a small Christian congregation is preparing an evening meal. An elder tells the children an old tale of a caliph who threatened their community and of the people who met to choose an answer. One child asks whether they argued. “Some spoke for a long time,” the elder says, turning the bread. “The others waited until they finished.” The cook lifts the lid from the last pot and finds less grain than expected. “Four more travellers came after sunset,” she tells the elder. “They will need a place at the table.” A small offering would buy food for them and let you join the group’s prayer for the road. The elder is also willing to tell you the rest of the old account while she works; the child drags a stool close enough to hear. She asks which part of the tale was a prayer and which part happened at the council, then asks you to write down the answer.
ev.road.29.choice.choice_0: Contribute to the meal and join the prayer
ev.road.29.choice.choice_1: Listen to the elder’s old tale and record it
ev.road.29.title: The Meal Beside the Old Tale
ev.road.30.body: At a western Asian stopping place, a cobbler is mending children’s shoes outside a small prayer house. A boy asks about an old tale in which a one-eyed cobbler prayed for a frightened community. “Did he mend shoes first?” the boy asks. The cobbler holds up the sole he is sewing. “Your sister needs this pair to walk home. Hand me the thread, and I will tell you while I work.” The boy does, then checks the repaired heel with his thumb. Several households have left shoes at the bench. Taking the finished pairs to their doors will add a day to your journey, and the cobbler has written each family’s name on a scrap. He also knows a footpath above a washed-out turn and can show it to you if you stay for the rest of the old tale. The boy asks whether the footpath begins behind the prayer house; the cobbler points there with his awl. Then the boy lines up the finished shoes so none is sent to the wrong house.
ev.road.30.choice.choice_0: Spend a day helping deliver the mended shoes
ev.road.30.choice.choice_1: Hear the cobbler’s old tale and ask about the footpath
ev.road.30.title: The Cobbler’s Story
ev.road.32.body: At a roadside shelter, a cart driver shows a bridge drawn on his father’s old route list. The planks have been lifted for repairs, but a second driver has already sent his loaded cart toward them. A carpenter comes back from the river with wet sleeves. “The stone piers are sound,” she says. “I need two days to fit the new deck, and someone to keep the waiting carts out of the mud.” The first driver points at the list. “My father marked a ford as well. Does it still hold?” A hired guide says he knows a passable way around; his fee covers the guide and the ferry on that route, and the detour adds one day. You can stay two extra days to help the carpenter and show arriving drivers where to wait, or pay the guide and continue around the bridge.
ev.road.32.choice.choice_0: Stay two extra days to help reopen the bridge
ev.road.32.choice.choice_1: Pay the guide and take the one-day detour
ev.road.32.title: The Bridge on the Old Route List
ev.road.33.body: On a road used by people leaving Mien, two strings of pack animals meet at a narrow cut between trees. One group is moving a young elephant with its mother. The animal stops when a cart bell sounds behind it, and its keeper loosens the rope instead of pulling. “She will follow her mother if the carts give us room,” he says. The other group’s driver asks his helper to wrap the cart bell in cloth. Then he points to sacks tied high on his mule. “I can wait, but the track has to stay open when she starts moving.” The young elephant reaches for its mother's flank, and the keeper waits for its breathing to slow. He asks for help shifting the sacks and taking the animals through in small groups; the work adds a day. A guide knows a higher track around the cut. It takes two extra days, and he offers to show you how to find its dry ground if you go with him.
ev.road.33.choice.choice_0: Stay an extra day and help both groups through the cut
ev.road.33.choice.choice_1: Take two extra days to learn the higher track
ev.road.33.title: Room for the Young Elephant
ev.road.34.body: At a roadside shelter, an old guard is reading the escort list for a caravan that has just arrived. His former apprentice has delivered a small chest safely, but the clerk has put another guard’s name beside it. “The pay will go to the wrong house,” the old man says. The apprentice rubs a mark on the chest. Her younger sister is waiting by the pay table and asks whether they can take the money home tonight. “I tied this knot before we left. Ask the merchant who received it.” The clerk agrees to hear the merchant and tells the sister to keep their place in line. She needs someone to bring both the receipt and the apprentice back to the table. You can help check the chest and settle the list here. A second merchant is leaving for another stop and offers a delivery wage if you carry a copy of the corrected list to his partner; that errand adds a day to your journey.
ev.road.34.choice.choice_0: Help the clerk check the escort’s work
ev.road.34.choice.choice_1: Carry the corrected list for an agreed wage
ev.road.34.title: The Escort’s Name on the List
ev.road.35.body: On the steppe, a herder has brought her sheep to a stretch of grass her family used last winter. The stone she remembers is gone. A neighbour has already pitched his felt shelter nearby and thinks her flock should turn away. “My mother set the marker beside a crooked shrub,” she says. The neighbour looks at the bare ground. He has already watered his sheep here and asks whether her lambs need the nearer bank. “The shrub died in the dry year. Show me where it stood.” Her younger cousin offers to search for the old base with you; that will add a day to your journey, and you can learn how the herders read this ground. Or you can stay two extra days to help both households measure enough grass and agree where each flock will feed. The sheep keep moving toward the same patch while they talk, and her cousin turns them back with a whistle.
ev.road.35.choice.choice_0: Spend an extra day locating the old marker's site
ev.road.35.choice.choice_1: Spend two extra days helping both households divide the grass
ev.road.35.title: The Winter Grass Marker
ev.road.36.body: At a roadside lodging house, a courier has brought two bundles addressed to a family returning after several years away. Three travellers with the same family name are waiting by the door, but the youngest says the blue cloth belongs to her aunt, who went on to a village off the main road. “She packed my brother’s winter coat in that cloth,” she tells the courier. He checks the knot and finds a second name under the string. “I cannot hand it to the wrong cousin,” he says. The innkeeper offers her table so you can compare the names with the family’s letters. The youngest unfolds one of those letters and asks her brother to check the village spelling before anyone unties the parcels. You can help settle it here and give the right parcel to the people waiting. The courier also offers a delivery wage if you take the remaining parcel to the aunt’s village; that errand adds a day to your journey.
ev.road.36.choice.choice_0: Help the family sort the parcels here
ev.road.36.choice.choice_1: Deliver the aunt’s parcel for a wage
ev.road.36.title: The Bundle for the Returning Family
ev.road.37.body: Two guards at a roadside storehouse disagree over a cart of grain. One has an old order bearing a seal; the other says the grain was set aside for the households now waiting beyond the gate. The cart driver lifts a corner of the cover. Two households waiting at the gate ask whether their sacks are among the load. “My receipt has the same seal, but the number of sacks was changed,” she says. The clerk thinks a second delivery arrived yesterday and knows where that earlier account is kept. Checking it will add a day to your journey. “Come with me and count the sacks before anyone unloads them,” he asks. A guide has found places on another cart leaving by a road around the storehouse queue. His fare includes the cart ride and the crossing; the detour also adds a day, and he can show you a reliable crossing used when this gate is crowded.
ev.road.37.choice.choice_0: Spend an extra day checking the grain account
ev.road.37.choice.choice_1: Pay the guide and learn the alternate crossing
ev.road.37.title: The Grain Cart and the Old Order
ev.road.38.body: At a roadside shelter on the Indian routes, a Christian family has stopped with a feverish child. The father tells an old story he heard about St Thomas and a place where travellers went to pray, while the mother asks the keeper for clean water. “The story can wait,” she tells the father. “Find out where the healer is lodging.” The child wakes and asks for a drink. His mother lifts him enough to sip, then asks the keeper whether any of the water has been kept clean in a covered vessel. The keeper has water, but the family is short of food for the road. A small gift will buy a meal and fresh water for them, and the father offers to share a road prayer with you. The mother has learned that a healer is visiting a nearby settlement. She asks whether you can help find the house and bring her the directions; the errand adds a day to your journey.
ev.road.38.choice.choice_0: Contribute food and water for the family
ev.road.38.choice.choice_1: Spend an extra day finding the healer
ev.road.38.title: Water for the Travellers
ev.road.39.body: At a roadside trading shed, a merchant is checking his delivery account against the bales on a cart. The account lists one more bale than the driver unloaded. “I counted twelve when I took them from the weaver,” the driver says. The merchant runs a finger down the line of names. “Then why does the tax tally say thirteen?” His niece notices that one number has been copied twice, but the clerk who wrote it has gone to the next market. The first buyer is already at the door, so she asks him to wait until they can read the seals aloud. You can stay here and compare the seals, marks and receipts with them; the shed will then release the goods to the right buyers. The merchant also has cloth due at the next market and offers a delivery wage if you take it with his party. That side trip adds a day to your journey.
ev.road.39.choice.choice_0: Help compare the bales with the account
ev.road.39.choice.choice_1: Deliver the cloth for an agreed wage
ev.road.39.title: The Missing Bale on the Account
ev.road.astrodice_counsel.body: The road offers a moment to cast astrodice. Great fortune and great ill omen are both spoken here without shame.
ev.road.astrodice_counsel.title: Counsel of astrodice
ev.road.bazi_counsel.body: The road offers a moment to cast the four pillars. Great fortune and great ill omen may both be named.
ev.road.bazi_counsel.title: Counsel of the pillars
ev.road.desert_voices.body: At a night camp on the road out of Lop or Sachiu, the cook calls the last traveller in for hot water. A voice beyond the low dunes answers with the same words, though everyone in the camp is already beside the fire. The camel keeper puts down a cup. “I heard my brother there last year,” he says. “He was asleep beside me. I walked toward the voice and lost the lantern.” A younger guard lifts his own lamp and asks, “Was it a person calling, or did the wind carry our words back?” The keeper cannot say. Another call comes from the dark and sounds like a companion asking for help. You may follow it, stay by the fire and mark the place on your route notes, or use the I Ching if you have learned it. The guard offers to hold the rope while you decide; no one has yet gone beyond the line of lamps.
ev.road.desert_voices.choice.divine: Cast the I Ching and steady your party for the road
ev.road.desert_voices.choice.follow: Follow the voice beyond the lamps
ev.road.desert_voices.choice.ignore: Keep watch and mark where the sound came from
ev.road.desert_voices.title: A Voice Beyond the Camp
ev.road.fadlan_01.body:
The caravan reaches a frozen river on the steppe. An oil merchant lifts the flap of his cart and checks the jars packed in straw. His sister is waiting for the load across the river. An older traveller recalls a passage from Ibn Fadlan's account: at the Jayhun, the ice was said to be seventeen spans thick, and laden carts could cross it. Here, a cart is already halfway over, its wheels pressing two tracks through the snow.

The merchant asks the keeper of the waystation whether he should follow it. The keeper crouches by the bank and knocks the ice with the butt of his staff. “I sent two men to look at the upper crossing,” he says. “They'll be back before supper. If you're going now, keep to the cart tracks.” The merchant calls his hired driver over and prepares to go with the next group. He asks whether you want to join them. You can also wait for the scouts at the waystation.
ev.road.fadlan_01.choice.cross_on_ice: Take the marked ice crossing with the caravan
ev.road.fadlan_01.choice.wait_at_ribat: Stay at the waystation for the scouts' report
ev.road.fadlan_01.title: The Steppe Ice Crossing
ev.road.fadlan_02.body:
Beyond the last houses, the wind has covered the caravan road. A young driver walks ahead of the animals, searching for a marker his father described: three stones with a piece of red cord between them. He finds two stones, then begins scraping at the snow with his boot. “The old road turns here,” he says, though he cannot tell which way.

A local guide arrives with a bundle of firewood across his back. He brushes snow from the third stone and points toward a low ridge. “The cord blew away in autumn. I put the stone back after the first storm.” He knows a shelter beyond that ridge and a place where the animals can feed. He asks for a guiding fee for the next march. The caravan master says he has already paid for the animals' fodder and asks whether you would cover the guide's fee. The young driver watches the guide's hand on the stones, eager to learn the route.
ev.road.fadlan_02.choice.hire_guide: Pay the guide and take him over the ridge
ev.road.fadlan_02.choice.press_on_alone: Follow the old road markers with the caravan
ev.road.fadlan_02.title: The Guide and the Snow Markers
ev.road.fadlan_03.body: The camp is nearly settled when the low sun reddens a bank of cloud. A herder is closing the sheep pen while his younger brother sits with an old copy of Ibn Fadlan’s account. The boy points at the sky. “Is this the red mist he saw?” His brother asks him to read the next line aloud. In the distant northern story, the light remained after dark and seemed to hold shapes of armed riders. “Will ours stay?” the boy asks. The herder ties the gate and comes over. “We can watch it while the sheep eat. Tell me what colour it is when I come back with the pail.” A companion offers to keep the passage open beside the fire and compare the boy’s account of this sunset with the older traveller’s words. Inside the tent, someone has saved a warm bowl for you. The boy shifts his seat so both the page and the clouds stay in view.
ev.road.fadlan_03.choice.seek_shelter: Join the others inside the tent
ev.road.fadlan_03.choice.watch_the_sky: Read the old account with the brothers by the fire
ev.road.fadlan_03.title: The Red Mist in the Old Journey
ev.road.fadlan_04.body:
At a roadside fire, a merchant unfolds a page he copied from an old travel account. It tells of a Bulghar king who went down to the Itil after traders reported a huge man by the flooded river. The account says he stood twelve cubits tall and had a head as large as a cooking pot. The king took him in and wrote to the people of Wīsū, three months away. The reply, according to the account, called the stranger one of Gog and Magog.

The merchant's niece has been turning a loaf over the coals. She asks who brought the reply from Wīsū, and her uncle checks the page. “It doesn't say. A traveller named Ibn Fadlan asked the king about the man and wrote down what he heard.” She breaks the loaf, gives him the larger piece, and asks him to read the part about the river again. Others edge closer to the fire. You can stay to ask about the old account, or take the road at first light.
ev.road.fadlan_04.choice.ask_the_kingdom: Ask how the king's story reached the written account
ev.road.fadlan_04.choice.press_on: Set out with the caravan at first light
ev.road.fadlan_04.title: The King's Story at the Fire
ev.road.fadlan_05.body: At a roadside camp, a young man has found a worn page inside his grandfather’s boatbuilding ledger. It carries Ibn Fadlan’s account of a Rus chieftain’s funeral long ago: a boat drawn ashore, new clothes sewn for the dead man, and an older woman the mourners called the Angel of Death. The grandfather used to build small river boats. “He folded this among the measurements for a keel,” the young man says. “I wish I had asked what he made of it.” His sister is coming to collect their grandfather’s cloak. She has sent word that the ledger ought to stay with the tools, but he wants her to see the page first. “Can you help me read the difficult names before she arrives?” he asks. A water carrier calls that she saw the sister waiting by the well; the young man also wants someone to walk with him there. He places the cloak beside the ledger so he will not leave either behind.
ev.road.fadlan_05.choice.record_rite: Spend the day reading Ibn Fadlan's account with him
ev.road.fadlan_05.choice.withdraw: Walk with him to meet his sister and give her the cloak
ev.road.fadlan_05.title: The Page About a Boat Funeral
ev.road.fadlan_06.body: At a caravan halt, a sailor opens a chart on a crate and puts a pebble on each corner. His daughter has inked the coastal harbours from their last voyage. Along the edge, her father has copied older stories from Abū Hāmid’s account of the Caspian: a black mound said to rise from the water, birds nesting among snakes, and an island where travellers heard voices. Another traveller wrote of an island crowded with wild sheep. “Did you see any of that?” a driver asks the daughter. “I saw these harbours,” she says, touching the fresh ink. “The rest is what Father kept from the books.” Her father points to a blank inlet. “If you ever reach it, ask its name for us.” He offers the chart for a price. An inland merchant leaving at dawn calls that his pack animals have room beside them. The daughter waits for the ink to dry before she rolls the map, whether it will travel with you or stay in her hands.
ev.road.fadlan_06.choice.stay_inland: Take the inland road with the merchant
ev.road.fadlan_06.title: The Sailor's Chart
ev.road.fadlan_07.body: A broker from Bulghar is repacking three bundles before the caravan leaves. His apprentice has tied beaver and ermine skins together. “The buyer asked for them separately,” the broker says, loosening the knot. From the third bundle he lifts a pale tusk so heavy that the apprentice catches its other end. “What animal carried a tooth like this?” the boy asks. The broker says people in the north dig such things out of the ground and send them south for carving. “One trader called them bones of ancient people,” he adds. “He had not seen the animal either.” The boy studies a small crack in the ivory and asks whether the buyer will mind. “Tell him about it before he pays,” the broker says. He asks you to hold the cord while they wrap the tusk and to help keep the two kinds of skins apart. A caller at the gate announces that the caravan is about to leave; the apprentice is still waiting to hear where the tusk will go.
ev.road.fadlan_07.choice.listen_trade: Stay and hear how the broker sorts his goods
ev.road.fadlan_07.title: The Broker's Three Bundles
ev.road.fadlan_08.body: At the forest edge, a trader lays bare blades and cow bones on the snow. He places a twig beside each pile and leads his companions behind the fir trees. The youngest has brought one bone his father polished for him. “He asked me to see whether anyone wanted it,” he says, looking back at its twig. “What if they leave it?” “Then you carry it home,” the older trader answers. When the group returns, sable skins lie beside several piles. The polished bone has not moved. The young man turns it in his hands and sets it down again, this time with a blade. Long wooden-board tracks cross the clearing; whoever left the skins has already gone. The trader says he will wait and look once more. Your caravan has room for a two-day pause here, while another party is preparing to leave along the forest edge. The young man keeps the polished bone in sight until everyone withdraws again.
ev.road.fadlan_08.choice.observe_barter: Wait for another exchange and record what happens
ev.road.fadlan_08.title: The Goods Left in the Snow
ev.road.fadlan_09.body: At a steppe halt, a pilgrim has opened an old travel book on the bench. His daughter is copying a tiny drawing in its margin. The page tells of a pool near Khwarazm, a mound with a gold-tiled dome, and travellers who said a boat lowered into the water vanished. Another page has a tale of the giants of Iram and a tomb far away. “Which part did the person who wrote this see?” the girl asks. Her father goes back through the lines and admits that some came from other travellers. She rubs out the shape of a boat she had drawn too large. Beyond the halt, a low mound rises from the grass. “Come and draw those stones with me,” her father says. “I will carry paper and water for the walk.” Visiting the mound and returning to the road adds two days to your journey. The girl folds her unfinished sketch and asks whether you can help her name the parts she sees for herself.
ev.road.fadlan_09.choice.press_on: Continue with the caravan and carry the old tale
ev.road.fadlan_09.choice.seek_the_mound: Spend two days sketching the nearby mound
ev.road.fadlan_09.title: The Mound in the Travel Book
ev.road.fadlan_10.body: At a small market beside the steppe road, a seed seller from the west opens two cloth packets for a local gardener. In his sleeve is an older page from Abū Hāmid’s account of Khwarazm: it says melons there were kept into winter, and grapes could grow as large as dates. The seller has brought seeds from that region wrapped in dry paper. The gardener rolls one between his fingers. “The well is low this year. How much water will these need here?” “I have never grown them on this ground,” the seller says. A woman buying onions points to her shaded plot and offers to tell them when she waters. The seller asks you to stay while he speaks to the other growers and to put each person’s name beside their advice; that work adds two days to your journey. The gardener puts the seed back on the paper and asks to see the seller’s own packet of winter stores.
ev.road.fadlan_10.choice.enter_khwarazm: Spend two days at the market with the growers
ev.road.fadlan_10.choice.press_on: Buy provisions and continue the journey
ev.road.fadlan_10.title: Seeds from Khwarazm
ev.road.fadlan_11.body: At a roadside station, a courier is stitching the torn seam of his leather letter bag. A younger clerk holds an old account of Sallām the Interpreter open so the courier can listen while he works. Long before your journey, Sallām left Samarra in felt coats and fur boots to seek the barrier said to have been raised by Dhū al-Qarnayn. Letters introduced the travellers to rulers in Armenia, the land of the Alans, and among the Khazars. “Did all those letters fit in one bag?” the clerk asks. The courier pulls his new thread tight. “They needed only the letter for the next person. A wet seam would lose even that.” He asks the clerk to hold the bag to the light and check for gaps. The account also mentions a stretch of foul-smelling black earth. The courier offers to point out the old sequence of places before he closes the book; his own mail for the next station is drying on the table. The clerk keeps a finger on the page while you look at the repaired seam.
ev.road.fadlan_11.choice.ask_the_route: Ask how Sallām's letters carried him onward
ev.road.fadlan_11.choice.press_on: Leave the old account and follow your own road
ev.road.fadlan_11.title: The Courier's Old Account
ev.road.fadlan_12.body:
At a steppe crossroads, a map seller spreads two lists beside his cooking fire. One is copied from Ibn Khurradādhbih's old book: it describes the Radhaniya merchants, who knew Arabic, Persian, and Frankish, and the Rus traders who carried furs and swords from the Slavic lands. The other list was made this season. It names the wells and shelters along the road you are travelling now.

A customer points to the older page. “That route sounds grand. Why is this one shorter?” The seller taps a well on the newer list. “Because this one was dug after the old book was written.” He has heard that a shelter farther on has closed for repairs, and asks whether you passed it. You can share what you know and compare the lists, or pay for his current notes and set out with them.
ev.road.fadlan_12.choice.share_road_news: Share recent road news and compare the lists
ev.road.fadlan_12.title: Two Lists of Roads
ev.road.fadlan_13.body: At a roadside camp, a copyist is reading Masʿudi’s older account to his apprentice while the ink dries on a fresh page. The account says that the Khazars had a ruling king who handled armies and public affairs, and a khaqan kept in the palace whose presence mattered to the kingship. When famine or defeat came, people sometimes demanded the khaqan’s death. The apprentice sets his pen down. “Did he decide any of this?” The copyist turns the book back a page. “The writer tells us what people did around him. Listen to the part where the king defended him.” The boy reads that line and looks at the clean margin. “Should I put his name here?” “We do not have it,” the copyist says. He asks you to hold the page flat while he makes a careful note of which part came from the old book. Outside, a carter calls that the animals are nearly ready; the apprentice waits for you to finish reading before he closes the cover.
ev.road.fadlan_13.choice.press_on: Leave the copyist to his work and travel on
ev.road.fadlan_13.choice.record_court: Read the passage and record Mas'udi's account
ev.road.fadlan_13.title: The Two Rulers in an Old Book
ev.road.fadlan_14.body: A travelling teacher’s geography book has come loose in his pack. He lays it open on a cloth and asks you to hold the pages while he threads them back together. The pupil sitting across from him reads Masʿudi’s account of summer nights around Bulghar, so short that a cooking pot might scarcely boil between dusk and dawn. “How long is our night?” she asks. The teacher hands her a marked stick. “Set this by the bowl at sunset. In the morning, we will see what you wrote.” She squints at the sky above the present camp. “I should write the place too.” “Yes, and the day,” he says, nudging his pen toward her. Watching and measuring here will add a day to your journey; travelling on with your party also uses another day along the road. The pupil presses the stick into level earth and waits for its shadow to lengthen.
ev.road.fadlan_14.choice.observe_night: Stay for a full day and help measure the light
ev.road.fadlan_14.choice.press_on: Take a day's march with your own company
ev.road.fadlan_14.title: The Measure of a Short Night
ev.road.fadlan_15.body: Where the road narrows, a fur trader has stopped his carts to check the labels on three bundles. Rain loosened the cords, and his nephew tied them again before anyone saw which tag belonged where. “The tailor asked for the dark pelts,” the trader says. “He will turn each one over before he pays.” The nephew points to ink marks on the wrapping. “I kept the maker’s marks outside. Can we match them to the order sheet?” The trader remembers reading Masʿudi’s older account of black fox fur carried from Burtas lands through Itil and sold far away. His present goods arrived by a different road, each marked with the household that prepared it. “Hold this corner while I open it,” he asks you. “If I mix them again, my sister will spend the evening sorting what I should have checked here.” The nephew sets a clean strip of cloth beside the open bundle, ready to tie the right tag onto it.
ev.road.fadlan_15.choice.inspect_loads: Help check the pelts and their owners' marks
ev.road.fadlan_15.choice.press_on: Take the other track around the stopped carts
ev.road.fadlan_15.title: The Mark on a Fur Bundle
ev.road.fadlan_16.body: At a seasonal steppe market, a broker has torn the corner from his stock list while pulling it out of his coat. One seller waits with honey and wax, another with furs and carved wood. “I wrote down the goods,” the broker says, “but this corner held the names.” His daughter brings the honey seller back from the water stand. “Ask her before you guess,” she says, putting a clean sheet on the crate. He shows you an older list copied from Muqaddasi, naming goods once carried from Bulghar: furs, birch wood, amber, arrows and honey. “I copied the old one to learn the words,” he tells his daughter. “Today I have to pay the people who brought these things.” She asks you to go from seller to seller with her and read each name back before the market closes. The honey seller sets a wax cake by the paper so the wind will not lift it.
ev.road.fadlan_16.choice.catalogue_goods: Spend the day helping the broker catalogue his goods
ev.road.fadlan_16.choice.press_on: Buy provisions and continue after the market closes
ev.road.fadlan_16.title: The Broker's Missing Page
ev.road.fadlan_17.body: Snow has filled the cart ruts beside a frozen lake. At a post, the keeper is fitting a small sled with food, firewood and the bags his passengers cannot carry. His lead dog tugs toward the path before the traces are fastened. “He knows the next post,” the keeper says, rubbing the dog’s neck. His daughter lifts a bag off the front runner. “Not there. It will drag when we turn.” The keeper moves it low behind the seat. He has heard an older description by Biruni of northern people using wooden sleds, dogs and bone skates. When you ask about the skates, he shows you the polished runners beneath his own sled and says he has never worn the bone ones. The paid sled crossing adds a day to your journey; walking the marked ice road adds two. His daughter hands you a strip of food for the lead dog and asks you to save it until the first halt.
ev.road.fadlan_17.choice.hire_sled: Pay for a sled ride to the next post
ev.road.fadlan_17.choice.walk_the_ice: Follow the marked ice road on foot
ev.road.fadlan_17.title: The Post Keeper's Dogs
ev.road.fadlan_18.body: A travelling reader has gathered people at a roadside halt with a chronicle copied in Novgorod. In it, a merchant’s servant repeats what people among the Iughra told him: cries from a mountain near the sea, voices through a narrow opening, and hands that exchanged furs for iron. The reader’s son looks up. “Were they really the people Alexander enclosed?” His father runs a finger down the line. “Some of the tellers thought so. The servant says he never saw their faces.” A carter waiting to leave asks the boy to read the part about the iron again. “My brother would trade a whole bundle of nails to hear where that was,” he says. The boy turns to you: “How do I write down a story that came through so many people?” The reader offers the page for you to examine. Outside the shelter, rain has made the direct road soft; the party leaving now will take a longer firm track, adding a day to its journey.
ev.road.fadlan_18.choice.press_on: Let the readers keep the page and travel on
ev.road.fadlan_18.choice.record_tale: Record who told each part of the chronicle's tale
ev.road.fadlan_18.title: The Mountain Tale in a Chronicle
ev.road.fadlan_19.body: A fur merchant is preparing to cross a low stretch where fog hides the road markers. He lays a rope beside the packs and has his companions practise walking with a little slack between them. One woman ties it hard around her wrist. “That will hurt before the first halt,” he says, kneeling to loosen the knot. His father used to tell him of the far northern “Land of Darkness,” where traders took experienced dogs, food and firewood onto frozen ground. “I never went there,” he tells you. “Here I can still hear my people if we keep close.” He asks the woman to call the next person’s name; an answer comes back through the line. Learning their marks and rope signals with him adds two days to your journey. A clear road around the low ground adds one day instead. The merchant shows you a dry rise he means to mark before the fog thickens.
ev.road.fadlan_19.choice.learn_the_rite: Stay two days to learn their route and rope signals
ev.road.fadlan_19.choice.turn_back: Take the longer clear road around the fog
ev.road.fadlan_19.title: The Rope for the Fog Road
ev.road.fadlan_20.body: A winter night has frozen the water in every jar at a steppe camp. A carter chips ice into a pot while his sister holds the horses’ reins. One horse noses the empty trough and stamps. “It will drink as soon as this melts,” she says, moving the pot closer to the fire. Her brother tries to pull on his mitten, but his fingers have gone stiff. She wraps them in a dry strip of cloth. “Can you still hold the reins?” she asks. “Once they warm,” he answers, and asks for another piece of wood. A slow march after the horses drink will add two days to your planned journey. Resting here longer and building up the fire adds three days, giving the animals and his hands more time. An older driver drags the trough closer to the fire and asks whether the first pot is ready. The sister counts the remaining wood aloud, then asks you to pass her the next jar of ice.
ev.road.fadlan_20.choice.endure_march: Water the horses and make the slower winter march
ev.road.fadlan_20.choice.halt_and_fire: Help tend the fire and leave after a longer rest
ev.road.fadlan_20.title: Water for the Winter Road
ev.road.fadlan_21.body: A map seller has left the far northern edge of his sheet uninked. A young courier reaches for the pen. “My uncle traded with men who spoke of Sibir and Julman. I can put the names here.” The seller holds the paper down. “Did he go to either town?” “No,” the courier admits. “He heard about long winters, and someone told him Alexander built a tower beyond them.” The seller draws a small question mark beside the pencilled tower. He has an older route list that gives stages north from Bulghar, and asks the courier to tell him who passed on each part of the tale. The boy remembers one trader’s name only after looking at a note in his uncle’s hand. You may help copy the traceable stages while they compare the stories. A departing party calls that it will take the road before the ink dries; going with it adds a day to your journey. The seller leaves a blank space for a northern name he has yet to hear from anyone who went there.
ev.road.fadlan_21.choice.ask_distances: Ask which distances were measured and which were heard
ev.road.fadlan_21.choice.press_on: Let the courier take his map and continue your journey
ev.road.fadlan_21.title: The Far Edge of a Map
ev.road.fadlan_22.body: At a river crossing, a boatman has turned a small hide boat upside down. He points to a split seam while his daughter brings their baggage down to the water. “Wait until the patch dries,” he tells her. She sets the bags on a dry stone and asks which bundle should go first. “The sealed one,” he says. “It can sit low in the boat. The animals will cross separately when the main ferry is ready.” The crossing costs a fare and adds a day to your journey. Upstream, another caravan is preparing ropes for a shallower reach. Its driver tests the current with a staff and says, “We can take your animals with ours, but every rope must be tied before we start.” That route adds two days and may wet the baggage. The daughter asks whether your baggage has anything that must stay dry; she sets that bundle on the highest stone. Then she brings a new needle to the seam and asks you to hold the hide taut.
ev.road.fadlan_22.choice.pay_boatmen: Pay the boatman for the crossing
ev.road.fadlan_22.choice.swim_with_carav: Join the caravan's slower crossing upstream
ev.road.fadlan_22.title: The Boatman's Worn Skin
ev.road.fadlan_23.body: Before dawn, a family at a roadside camp finds its tether cut and three horses gone.
