ev.zayton.harbour.choice.watch: Spend the day watching the ships come in
ev.zayton.harbour.title: The Quay
ev.zayton.jiaobei_ask.body: At the temple threshold the cups wait. A bright answer is called great fortune; a dark one, great ill omen — and still you must choose a road.
ev.zayton.jiaobei_ask.title: Ask the Cups
ev.zayton.ledger_consequence.body: On the second day a clerk brings a fair copy of the duty ledger. It records not only your cargo but where goods came from and where they may go next. The coastal road between Kinsay and Zayton is noted in the margin. He asks whether you want a sealed copy.
ev.zayton.ledger_consequence.choice.copy: Keep the copy and note Kinsay and the coastal road
ev.zayton.ledger_consequence.choice.refu: Keep no copy; let the cargo alone be entered
ev.zayton.ledger_consequence.title: The Road in the Ledger
ev.zayton.mazu.body: Above the anchorage stands a temple to a goddess of the sea, and no shipmaster of this coast puts out without going up to it first. They burn paper there, and set out a dish of rice and a cup of wine, and shake a bamboo cylinder of numbered slips until one falls; the slip is carried to an old woman by the door, who reads what is written against that number. The sailors do not call this fortune-telling. They call it asking.
ev.zayton.mazu.choice.lots: Shake the cylinder and draw a slip
ev.zayton.mazu.choice.offer: Make an offering before you sail
ev.zayton.mazu.choice.watch: Stand at the back and watch
ev.zayton.mazu.title: The Temple of the Sea
ev.zayton.mentor.body: The old woman at the temple door has read slips for forty years and can tell you the name of every shipmaster who ignored one. She will teach the reading to anyone who sits with her long enough and gives what he can to the temple; but she says plainly that the slips do not tell a man what will happen. They tell him what he has not yet considered.
ev.zayton.mentor.choice.ask: Ask only how the reading is done
ev.zayton.mentor.choice.learn: Sit with her, and learn to read the slips
ev.zayton.mentor.choice.learn_jiaobei: Sit with her, and learn the temple cups
ev.zayton.mentor.title: The Woman Who Reads the Slips
ev.zayton.pilot_consequence.body: When the boatman has finished his wine, a pilot dips one finger in water and draws two lines on the table. One runs south with the monsoon to Chamba; the other goes inland and north to Fuju. There is time to ask one road clearly.
ev.zayton.pilot_consequence.choice.chamb: Ask about the monsoon lane south to Chamba
ev.zayton.pilot_consequence.choice.local: Ask about the land road north to Fuju
ev.zayton.pilot_consequence.title: Two Roads from a Pilot
ev.zayton.watch_consequence.body: After dark the watch lanterns stop at your lodging. They cannot find your mark in the quay ledger. Their leader draws no weapon; he places a late-declaration tally on the table. Pay now, or leave the cargo in bond for inspection.
ev.zayton.watch_consequence.choice.submi: Leave the cargo for two days' inspection
ev.zayton.watch_consequence.title: Lanterns of the Night Watch
good.aloeswood.desc: The dark, resinous heartwood of the Aquilaria tree, formed when the tree is infected with a particular mould. Burns with a fragrance worth its weight in gold; the Kaan's temples use it.
good.aloeswood.name: Aloeswood
good.arabian-horse.desc: The horses of the Nejd — small, fine-boned, and astonishingly swift. A bloodline traceable to the Prophet's own stables; the foundation of every cavalry in Islam.
good.arabian-horse.name: Arabian Horse
good.asbestos-cloth.desc: Cloth woven from a mineral fiber mined in the mountains of Cathay — it does not burn, but is cleaned by throwing it into a fire. The Kaan's napkins are made of this.
good.asbestos-cloth.name: Salamander Cloth
good.baghdad-brocade.desc: Silk cloth woven with gold and silver thread in the workshops of Baghdad, patterned with arabesques and Kufic inscriptions.
good.baghdad-brocade.name: Baghdad Brocade
good.balas-ruby.desc: The balas ruby from the mountains near Balc — a vivid red spinel, often mistaken for true ruby. Set in crowns, sword-hilts, and the Kaan's own seal-ring.
good.balas-ruby.name: Balas Ruby
good.birds-nest.desc: The nests of the swiftlet, woven from its own saliva on the ceilings of sea-caves in Java and Borneo. Boiled in broth, it becomes a gelatinous soup believed to prolong life.
good.birds-nest.name: Birds' Nest
good.brazilwood.desc: The red dyewood of Sumatra and the Malay coast, chipped and boiled to extract a crimson dye. So valuable that a country on the other side of the world will one day be named after it.
good.brazilwood.name: Brazilwood
good.camel-felt.desc: Heavy felt pressed from the wool of Bactrian camels, used for tents, saddle-blankets, and winter coats on the Silk Road. Waterproof and nearly indestructible.
good.camel-felt.name: Camel Felt
good.camlet.desc: A fine fabric woven from the hair of the Angora goat, native to the mountains of Anatolia. Water-resistant and soft as cashmere.
good.camlet.name: Camlet
good.camphor.desc: The white crystal distilled from the wood of the camphor laurel of Borneo and Sumatra. Clears the head, repels moths, and burns with a bright, smokeless flame.
good.camphor.name: Camphor
good.cinnabar.desc: The red ore of mercury, mined in the mountains of southern China. Carved into seals, ground into the vermilion ink of the Emperor's edicts.
good.cinnabar.name: Cinnabar
good.cloves.desc: The dried flower buds of the clove tree, native to the Moluccas — the Spice Islands. A handful of cloves in a ship's hold smells sweeter than any garden.
good.cloves.name: Cloves
good.coral.desc: Red coral from the reefs of Sardinia and the Barbary coast, carved into beads and amulets. Believed to ward off the evil eye; prized in India and Cathay.
good.coral.name: Coral
good.cotton-cloth.desc: Cotton from the fields of India, spun and woven into cloth lighter than wool and cooler than silk. The everyday dress of half the world.
good.cotton-cloth.name: Cotton Cloth
good.damascus-steel.desc: Blades forged in Damascus from Indian wootz steel, watered with a pattern like running water or damask cloth. A sword of Damascus steel can cut a silk scarf dropped onto its edge.
good.damascus-steel.name: Damascus Steel
good.dates.desc: The fruit of the date palm, harvested in Basra, Medina, and the oases of Arabia. Dried dates can cross any desert; a handful sustains a man for a day.
good.dates.name: Dates
good.dehua-porcelain.desc: The blanc de Chine from the kilns of Dehua — pure white, unglazed on the surface, with a warm ivory glow. The Europeans call it 'marco-polo ware'.
good.dehua-porcelain.name: Dehua White Porcelain
good.diamonds.desc: The diamonds of Golconda and Borneo — the hardest stone in creation. Cleaved and polished in the workshops of India; a single flawless stone buys a kingdom.
good.diamonds.name: Diamonds
good.ebony.desc: The black heartwood of the Diospyros tree, so dense that it sinks in water. Carved into furniture, chess pieces, and the hilts of ceremonial swords.
good.ebony.name: Ebony
good.frankincense.desc: The dried resin of the Boswellia tree, harvested in Dhofar and Somalia. Burns with a white smoke sacred to every temple from Rome to Cambaluc.
good.frankincense.name: Frankincense
good.furs.desc: Sable, ermine, fox, and squirrel from the forests of Rus and Siberia, trapped in winter when the fur is thickest. The sable alone is worth its weight in silver.
good.furs.name: Furs
good.ginger.desc: The knobby root of the ginger plant, dried and candied or ground into powder. Warms the stomach and preserves food on long sea voyages.
good.ginger.name: Ginger
good.glass-bead.name: Glass bead
good.glass-lamps.desc: Enamelled glass mosque lamps from the furnaces of Aleppo and Damascus, painted with verses from the Quran in gold and blue.
good.glass-lamps.name: Glass Lamps
good.hangzhou-fan.desc: Folding fans from the workshops of Kinsay, painted with mountain landscapes, plum blossoms, and calligraphy. A gentleman's accessory in the south.
good.hangzhou-fan.name: Kinsay Folding Fan
good.hunting-falcon.desc: Trained falcons from the cliffs of the Caucasus, the Altai, and the Hindu Kush. A gerfalcon that has taken a crane in flight is worth more than three horses.
good.hunting-falcon.name: Hunting Falcon
good.indigo.desc: The blue dye extracted from the leaves of the Indigofera plant, grown in Gujarat and the Nile valley. A vat of indigo dyes a thousand bolts of cloth the colour of the evening sky.
good.indigo.name: Indigo
good.jade.desc: River jade from the streams of Khotan — white like mutton fat, green like spring leaves. The stone the Kaan values above all others; carved into cups, belts, and ritual objects.
good.jade.name: River Jade
good.koumiss.desc: Fermented mare's milk, the drink of the Mongol steppe. Sour, slightly alcoholic, and rich in the vitamins that keep a man alive on a diet of meat and milk.
good.koumiss.name: Koumiss
good.lacquerware.desc: Wood coated in layer upon layer of the sap of the lac tree, each layer dried and polished before the next is applied. The finished piece gleams like dark water.
good.lacquerware.name: Lacquerware
good.lapis.desc: Lapis lazuli from the mines of Badakhshan — a blue so deep it seems to hold the night sky. Ground into pigment for the painters of kings; the ultramarine of the ages.
good.lapis.name: Lapis Lazuli
good.leather.desc: Tanned leather from the hides of steppe cattle, worked in the towns of the Silk Road into saddles, boots, water-skins, and book-bindings.
good.leather.name: Leather
good.melons.desc: The melons of Khorasan and Tangut — larger than a man's head, green-rinded and golden-fleshed. Dried into spirals that can travel a thousand miles without spoiling.
good.melons.name: Melons
good.murano-glass.desc: Glass from the furnaces of Murano, near Venice — the clearest and most brilliant in Christendom. Coloured with cobalt, gold, and manganese, shaped into cups, beads, and mirrors.
good.murano-glass.name: Murano Glass
good.musk.desc: The dried secretion from the gland of the musk deer of the Tibetan highlands. The most powerful perfume known to man; a grain scents a room for a week.
good.musk.name: Musk
good.muslin.desc: Cotton cloth from Mosul and Dhaka, woven so fine that a length of forty yards can be drawn through a finger-ring. The dress of the Mughal court and the Kaan's summer robes.
good.muslin.name: Muslin
good.myrrh.desc: Dark, bitter resin from the Commiphora tree of southern Arabia. Used in embalming, medicine, and incense; the gift of the Magi.
good.myrrh.name: Myrrh
good.nutmeg.desc: The kernel of the nutmeg fruit, wrapped in a red lace of mace. Grown only on the Banda Islands; a sack of nutmeg bought for a few coins in Java sells for a fortune in Venice.
good.nutmeg.name: Nutmeg
good.olive-oil.desc: Golden oil pressed from the olives of Apulia and the Levant. Used for lamps, cooking, and anointing; a staple of every Latin merchant's cargo.
good.olive-oil.name: Olive Oil
good.paper-money.desc: The Kaan's paper currency — mulberry-bark sheets stamped with the imperial seal. Accepted as legal tender in every market of the empire; refusal is punishable by death.
good.paper-money.name: Paper Money
good.paper.desc: Paper from Samarcand, beaten from linen rags and polished smooth with stone. The finest writing surface in the world; a single sheet costs a day's wages but lasts three hundred years.
good.paper.name: Paper
good.pearls.desc: Pearls from the fisheries of the Gulf of Manaar, between India and Ceylon. The divers descend without aid, holding their breath longer than any man in Christendom.
good.pearls.name: Pearls
good.pepper.desc: The black gold of Malabar — the dried berries of the Piper vine. More valuable than silver by weight; the spice that built Venice and filled the holds of a thousand ships.
good.pepper.name: Pepper
good.persian-carpet.desc: Hand-knotted carpets from the looms of Isfahan, Tabriz, and Kerman. The finest have a thousand knots to the square inch; their colours deepen with age.
good.persian-carpet.name: Persian Carpet
good.porcelain.desc: The white clay of Jingdezhen, fired at a heat that would melt iron, glazed with cobalt blue from Persia. So thin that light passes through; so hard that steel cannot scratch it.
good.porcelain.name: Porcelain
good.rhubarb.desc: The root of the medicinal rhubarb plant, grown in the mountains of Tangut and Cathay. More valuable than many spices; cures fevers and purges the body.
good.rhubarb.name: Rhubarb
good.rosewater.desc: Water distilled from the petals of Damask roses, grown in the gardens of Persia. Used in cooking, perfume, and the washing of honoured guests' hands.
good.rosewater.name: Rosewater
good.sable.desc: The sable of the Siberian forest — the most valuable fur in the world. The Kaan's winter robes are lined with it; a single pelt buys a horse.
good.sable.name: Sable
good.salt.desc: Salt from the mines of the Punjab, the pans of the Sahara, and the shores of the Black Sea. Salt is money on the steppe — a cake of salt buys a sheep.
good.salt.name: Salt
good.sandalwood.desc: The fragrant heartwood of the sandal tree, grown in the hills of southern India and the islands of Indonesia. Carved into boxes, burned as incense, or distilled into oil.
good.sandalwood.name: Sandalwood
good.silk.desc: The queen of fabrics — thread spun by the silkworm from the leaves of the mulberry, dyed with saffron, indigo, madder, and cochineal. A bolt of the finest silk sells for its weight in silver.
good.silk.name: Silk
good.silverware.desc: Silver plates, cups, and candlesticks from the workshops of Nuremberg and Limoges. The Latins' finest export to the East.
good.silverware.name: Silverware
good.steppe-horse.desc: The horses of the Mongol steppe — small, shaggy, and tireless. They can survive on grass buried under snow and carry a rider two hundred miles in a day.
good.steppe-horse.name: Steppe Horse
good.sugar.desc: Cane sugar from the plantations of the Levant and the islands of the Indian Ocean. Once a medicine, now the sweetener of kings and merchants.
good.sugar.name: Sugar
good.tabriz-pearls.desc: Pearls from the oyster beds of the Persian Gulf, sorted and drilled in the bazaars of Tabriz. A matched string of fifty pearls is worth a ship.
good.tabriz-pearls.name: Tabriz Pearls
good.tea.desc: The leaf of the Camellia bush, picked in spring, dried in the sun, pressed into bricks for the caravan trade. The Kaan's court drinks tea with milk and salt; the south drinks it clear.
good.tea.name: Tea
good.tin.desc: Tin from the mines of the Malay Peninsula, smelted into ingots and shipped to China and India. Mixed with copper, it makes bronze — the metal of bells, cannon, and Buddhas.
good.tin.name: Tin
good.tortoiseshell.desc: The mottled brown shell of the hawksbill turtle, harvested in the islands of the Indian Ocean. Heated and pressed into combs, boxes, and the inlay of fine furniture.
good.tortoiseshell.name: Tortoiseshell
good.turmeric.desc: The golden root of the turmeric plant, dried and ground into a powder that dyes cloth, flavours food, and heals wounds. The colour of a monk's robe.
good.turmeric.name: Turmeric
good.turquoise.desc: Sky-blue turquoise from the mines of Nishapur in Persia. Set in silver and worn as protection against the evil eye and falls from horseback.
good.turquoise.name: Turquoise
good.woolen-cloth.desc: Heavy woolen cloth from the Flemish looms, dyed with madder, woad, and weld. The best is as smooth as silk and as warm as a camel's coat.
good.woolen-cloth.name: Woollen Cloth

lesson.mentor.beatrice.action: Taking this one means leaving another. Good. Keep weighing the choice.
lesson.mentor.beatrice.chat: I teach choices, returns and costs. Deciding for you would cost extra, and I do not take that commission.
lesson.mentor.beatrice.hint: Each card brings two contributions. Watch both, not just the one you like.
lesson.mentor.beatrice.inspect: The back keeps a secret; the face offers clues. Our symbol counts turn choosing into a puzzle.
lesson.mentor.beatrice.intro: Choosing cards is like bargaining: you cannot take everything. Decide what your three places are worth.
lesson.mentor.beatrice.name: Beatrice
lesson.mentor.beatrice.retry: A fresh hand. I have survived worse bargains and recovered.
lesson.mentor.beatrice.round: That hand balances. I will be watching the next one closely.
lesson.mentor.beatrice.support: No need to replace the whole hand. Find what you have too much of and what is missing.
lesson.mentor.beatrice.tease: A lively hand! Unfortunately, liveliness will not settle the bill. Check the totals.
lesson.mentor.beatrice.trait: A merchant widow with a quick wit
lesson.mentor.beatrice.win: Lovely. If this were a negotiation, I would sit on your side.
lesson.mentor.bjorn.chat: I kept the first stave I ruined. It levels my table nicely.
lesson.mentor.bjorn.hint: Remember the shape and its place. A name alone will not find the stave.
lesson.mentor.bjorn.inspect: These practice pieces borrow the shapes of carvings. The matching game is not an ancient ritual.
lesson.mentor.bjorn.intro: Look past the wood grain to the cuts. Remember the pairs. No need to rush.
lesson.mentor.bjorn.name: Bjorn
lesson.mentor.bjorn.retry: The wood can take it. Try again.
lesson.mentor.bjorn.round: A pair. Keep it in mind.
lesson.mentor.bjorn.support: Pause. Remember one pair. That is enough. Then the next.
lesson.mentor.bjorn.tease: Those pieces may be cousins. They are not twins.
lesson.mentor.bjorn.win: Good. Steady hands, steady eyes. You could teach the next learner.
lesson.mentor.jin.action: There. You do listen after all.
lesson.mentor.jin.chat: I remember every captain who dismissed the sticks. They rarely remembered an umbrella either.
lesson.mentor.jin.hint: Do not wrestle with it. Notice the shapes in front of you before choosing an answer.
lesson.mentor.jin.inspect: This tube has been with me for decades. It decides nothing for you; it invites an overlooked thought.
lesson.mentor.jin.intro: Loosen your grip. Are you here to read the sticks or shake my tube to pieces?
lesson.mentor.jin.name: Granny Jin
lesson.mentor.jin.retry: Good to see you back. The tube survived, and I am not raising the fee.
lesson.mentor.jin.round: Steady at last. Do not let a little praise send the next one flying.
lesson.mentor.jin.support: No hurry. I can wait. Take a breath and watch just the part that matters.
lesson.mentor.jin.tease: Oh dear. Even the temple cat closed its eyes for that one. Try again.
lesson.mentor.jin.win: Now that looks right. If someone rushes you, tell them Granny taught you to take your time.
lesson.mentor.lin.action: Note what changed, not merely where you touched.
lesson.mentor.lin.chat: They call me difficult. Keep the figures clear and I will even forgive cold tea.
lesson.mentor.lin.hint: Separate the target from the current state. Then check exactly what this move changes.
lesson.mentor.lin.inspect: Each diagram and instrument has its own reading convention. Ornament cannot check your work.
lesson.mentor.lin.intro: Look at the connections before moving. My desk has room for mistakes, but not for vague reasoning.
lesson.mentor.lin.name: Master Lin
lesson.mentor.lin.retry: We have enough paper. Start again and keep what you discovered.
lesson.mentor.lin.round: The reasoning holds. Take that patience into the next round.
lesson.mentor.lin.support: Pause. Follow one connection at a time. You are trying to watch too many things at once.
lesson.mentor.lin.tease: Are you trying to change the desk along with the answer? Check what that move affected.
lesson.mentor.lin.win: Acceptable. Remember the reasoning; it is worth more than my praise.
lesson.mentor.mira.action: That detail is noted. Do not overlook the other one.
lesson.mentor.mira.chat: I once argued over half a division all evening. It turned out my lamp was casting a crooked shadow.
lesson.mentor.mira.hint: Compare the target and current values, then check what a single move changes.
lesson.mentor.mira.inspect: Keep scales, symbols and positions distinct. These combination puzzles were designed for practice.
lesson.mentor.mira.intro: I brought exercises from several chart traditions. Use the scale on this page; keep their conventions distinct.
lesson.mentor.mira.name: Mira
lesson.mentor.mira.retry: The chart is still here. Refill your patience and try again.
lesson.mentor.mira.round: Beautifully aligned. On to the next chart.
lesson.mentor.mira.support: Follow one change at a time. After each move, check what happened elsewhere.
lesson.mentor.mira.tease: A stylish move, but the target is still elsewhere. Check it once more?
lesson.mentor.mira.trait: Patient with people, exact with scales
lesson.mentor.mira.win: Aligned! That patience is more dependable than my brass ruler.
lesson.mentor.nadir.action: Keep that small light. Now the next.
lesson.mentor.nadir.chat: Someone asked for the correct answer to a dream. I gave them blank paper to record what they had seen.
lesson.mentor.nadir.hint: Give neighboring shapes a short story. Include their positions in it.
lesson.mentor.nadir.inspect: Lamplight and reflections invite wandering thoughts. We are practicing observation, not writing verdicts on the future.
lesson.mentor.nadir.intro: Tonight, do not rush to explain. Hold what you see as gently as a lamp.
lesson.mentor.nadir.name: Nadir
lesson.mentor.nadir.retry: Turn the page again. A second reading often reveals a different detail.
lesson.mentor.nadir.round: The fragments connect. Let us read another page.
lesson.mentor.nadir.support: Remember one outline first. A long story can be told one sentence at a time.
lesson.mentor.nadir.tease: Your memory took a side street. The lamp is still over here. Come back and look.
lesson.mentor.nadir.win: You brought the scattered pieces home. Tonight the lamp stays lit a little longer for you.
lesson.mentor.sahl.action: I saw that mark. Keep checking.
lesson.mentor.sahl.chat: A student asked for my costliest tool. I said: the patience to count again.
lesson.mentor.sahl.hint: Compare one part at a time. A finished row need not distract you from the next.
lesson.mentor.sahl.inspect: A sand tray can be smoothed and redrawn. Practice should allow revision too.
lesson.mentor.sahl.intro: There are many grains of sand and few rules. Let us keep it that way.
lesson.mentor.sahl.name: Sahl
lesson.mentor.sahl.retry: Smooth it out and begin again. Keep the method; leave the mistake.
lesson.mentor.sahl.round: This arrangement works. Test your method on the next.
lesson.mentor.sahl.support: Forget the whole tray for a moment. Work through one row. The rest can wait.
lesson.mentor.sahl.tease: The sand has not secretly moved. I can vouch for it. Count again.
lesson.mentor.sahl.win: Clear and economical. The tray appreciates that answer. So do I.
lesson.mentor.selma.action: Got that one? Good. I will try not to interrupt.
lesson.mentor.selma.chat: Guests always see a bird in the grounds. I sometimes see the bill they forgot to pay.
lesson.mentor.selma.hint: Turn the cup and the relationships remain. Hold on to one small cluster of neighboring marks.
lesson.mentor.selma.inspect: Coffee leaves the grounds; our eyes connect the shapes. Looking again is more fun than rushing to a conclusion.
lesson.mentor.selma.intro: Do not drink yet. That little landscape in the cup could keep us talking all afternoon.
lesson.mentor.selma.name: Selma
lesson.mentor.selma.retry: Another look. We have plenty of time to talk.
lesson.mentor.selma.round: You read this cup clearly. A different angle for the next.
lesson.mentor.selma.support: Take your time. Start with the marks near the rim. No need to swallow the whole picture at once.
lesson.mentor.selma.tease: You remembered the little path outside the cup. It has not grown legs, you know.
lesson.mentor.selma.win: Such careful eyes! Now I can safely step away to refill the coffee.
lesson.mentor.zhou.action: Yes. Your eyes are catching up with your hands. Continue.
lesson.mentor.zhou.chat: Once I copied the lines upside down. My teacher said nothing; he handed me the book upside down.
lesson.mentor.zhou.hint: A good question. Admitting you missed a detail beats pretending you understood.
lesson.mentor.zhou.inspect: The tools remind you to pause. You still do the thinking.
lesson.mentor.zhou.intro: No need to race to an answer. Settle in and study the clues; they will not complain if you take your time.
lesson.mentor.zhou.name: Master Zhou
lesson.mentor.zhou.retry: Lay it out again. An old puzzle can still reveal something new.
lesson.mentor.zhou.round: This layer is sound. Do not race ahead on the next.
lesson.mentor.zhou.support: Leave the ending aside. Read this one detail clearly; the next step will be easier.
lesson.mentor.zhou.tease: An impressively confident move. Confidence earns no points, though. Look once more.
lesson.mentor.zhou.win: That was more than luck. You have learned to pause and observe. Good.
lesson.numerology.prompt: Use counting tokens to reach the exact number.
lesson.numerology.title: Turn Name to Number
lesson.observed_fmt: Recorded %d observations. Now make a bounded judgement.
lesson.operation_invalid: This action cannot be performed now: %s
lesson.oracle.clue.0: Whether he asks another to decide
lesson.oracle.clue.1: Whether he would keep the unknown hidden
lesson.oracle.option.0: Decide for me whether I should wed
lesson.oracle.option.1: Tell me what I have overlooked
lesson.oracle.option.2: Name the day of my death
lesson.oracle.prompt: Study the boundary of the question, then choose a suitable way to ask.
lesson.oracle.title: The Boundary of Asking
lesson.order_pass: The order is correct. You remember the method.
lesson.orient_fail: The direction does not answer the season and terrain in the prompt.
lesson.orient_pass: You matched direction to the present circumstances.
lesson.palmistry.option.0: Fix the years of life by one line
lesson.palmistry.option.1: Record the layers and speak your doubt
lesson.palmistry.prompt: Record the dominant hand and the lines, then state your uncertainty.
lesson.palmistry.title: The Layers of the Palm
lesson.qimen.prompt: Fix the chart when the gate comes into the time window.
lesson.qimen.title: Fix the Gate and Chart
lesson.runes.option.0: Throw out the stones you dislike
lesson.runes.option.1: Keep every stone, marking each place
lesson.runes.option.2: Cast again until a good omen falls
lesson.runes.prompt: Cast the stones and keep every one where it falls.
lesson.runes.title: Cast the Runes
lesson.scrying.option.0: Take it for prophecy at once
lesson.scrying.option.1: First record the shape and your own thoughts
lesson.scrying.option.2: Stare until the vision grows plain
lesson.scrying.prompt: Record the vague shapes and your own associations.
lesson.scrying.title: Gaze and Record
lesson.stage.direct: Touch the instruments or use the controls
lesson.stage.draft_touch: Tap a symbol to inspect its balance; choose cards at right
lesson.stage.rings_touch: Tap a ring clockwise; right-click reverses it
lesson.stage.tip_cast: Read each face before combining the result.
lesson.stage.tip_cycle: One move affects two places. Follow the link first.
lesson.stage.tip_draft: Compare all four totals to find the excess and the shortage.
lesson.stage.tip_memory: Remember the positions of one pair before the next.
lesson.stage.tip_numbers: Add the selected values, then find the gap to the target.
lesson.stage.tip_parity: One row first: odd leaves one dot; even leaves two.
lesson.stage.tip_rings: Each ring turns its neighbor too. Check both.
lesson.stage.tip_route: Find an adjacent open cell, then check the route to both markers.
lesson.stage.tip_timing: Slow down. The hint button can remove the timing requirement.
lesson.stage.tip_trace: Remember two or three neighboring dots as a group.
lesson.tarot.prompt: Lay the cards in the correct sequence and hold the spread.
lesson.tarot.step.0: Set the question in the mind
lesson.tarot.step.4: Read the cards one by one
lesson.tarot.title: Hold the Spread
lesson.timing_stop: Fix the Image in the Window
lesson.vedic.clue.0: The lunar lodge of the hour
lesson.vedic.clue.1: The hour that may be exchanged
lesson.vedic.option.0: Swear the road is barred forever
lesson.vedic.option.1: Name the risk and offer another hour
lesson.vedic.option.2: Decide the traveller's fate for him
lesson.vedic.prompt: Observe the clues, then choose a bounded answer.
lesson.vedic.title: The Lunar Lodge and the Road
lesson.western.prompt: Generate the foundation chart in the correct order.
lesson.western.title: Turn the Star Wheel
lesson.xiangmian.option.2: Fix the years of his life by it
lesson.xiangmian.prompt: Observe first, then choose a statement that does not judge.
lesson.xiangmian.title: Observe Without Judgment
lesson.ziwei.prompt: Build the palace chart step by step, one position at a time.
lesson.ziwei.step.0: Set the palace of the life
lesson.ziwei.title: Place the Twelve Palaces

log.lesson_failed: Lesson failed — %s not learned yet. You may seek the mentor again.
market.alexandria.item.arabian-horse: A horse belongs to the merchant’s trade stock. Buying this cargo does not select a transport mode for the next road.
market.alexandria.item.baghdad-brocade: Folded brocade takes more room than a bead. Picture it in your pack before paying.
market.alexandria.item.damascus-steel: A blade catches the light. The stall calls it Damascus steel; the name on a stall is not proof of a blade’s origin.
market.alexandria.item.dates: These dates are sold as a cargo parcel. The market price is for trade goods, not the meal shared at a host’s table.
market.alexandria.item.frankincense: The seller opens a pouch of pale resin. Ask where the cargo came from before mistaking an imported scent for a local harvest.
market.alexandria.item.glass-bead: A single glass bead with a hole for a cord: a modest keepsake, sold individually and carried in one cargo slot.
market.alexandria.item.glass-lamps: Light passes through the glass walls. The parcel is bulkier than the single bead on the next tray.
market.alexandria.item.myrrh: Dark resin lies beside the lighter incense. The merchant offers a trade parcel, not a single pinch.
market.alexandria.item.paper: Sheets are stacked into a travel parcel. A blank page could become a letter, a copied route or a merchant’s account.
market.alexandria.item.persian-carpet: The seller unrolls a corner to show the weave. A carpet is cargo for a planned journey, not a light souvenir.
market.alexandria.item.rosewater: A stoppered bottle is offered for inspection. Keep it apart from paper and cloth in your imagination of the pack.
market.alexandria.item.tabriz-pearls: The trader calls these pearls a Tabriz consignment. The trading name tells you a claimed route, not where a pearl grew.
market.zayton.item.cinnabar: Cinnabar from the mountain mines of the south, sold in both the raw stone and the ground powder — the latter in small stoppered bottles because the wind off the haven will carry it away by the grain.
market.zayton.item.dehua-porcelain: Blanc de Chine out of the Dehua kilns — unglazed on the surface, warm as ivory. The Arab merchants call it 'the fat of the earth' and pay the forty-four in the hundred freight without complaint.
market.zayton.item.ginger: Preserved ginger in clay jars sealed with wax, bound for the galleys of Hormuz and Aden. The spice merchants say a ship without ginger is a ship that will lose half its crew to the flux.
market.zayton.item.hangzhou-fan: Folding fans from Kinsay, their ribs of sandalwood, their leaves painted with calligraphy. A merchant who buys a crate of these at Zayton can sell them in Damascus for ten times the price.
market.zayton.item.lacquerware: Black and cinnabar-red lacquer from the workshops of Fuju, cured in the damp heat of the coastal summer. The Indian merchants prize it for the way candlelight moves across the surface like oil on dark water.
market.zayton.item.musk: The musk-pod from the deer of the Tibetan marches, brought down to Zayton by caravan through the passes. A single pod, no bigger than a walnut, will scent a cargo of silk for a month.
market.zayton.item.paper-money: The Kaan's own currency, printed on mulberry-bark sheets with the imperial seal in vermilion. The quay-side money-changers will swap silver for paper at a rate that changes with the tide.
market.zayton.item.porcelain: The white ware of Jingdezhen, packed in straw and sawdust, carried down the rivers on flat-bottomed boats. A percentage of every crate is broken in transit, and the merchants have already figured that cost into the price you pay.
market.zayton.item.rhubarb: The dried root of the Tangut rhubarb — worth more pound for pound than cinnamon in the apothecaries of Venice. The warehousemen weigh it on the same brass scales they use for pearls.
market.zayton.item.silk: Bales of raw Manzi silk, stacked eight-high in the customs shed, waiting to be weighed and taxed. The Kaan's clerks nick a corner of every bale to check the grade; finer than any the Persians spin.
market.zayton.item.sugar: Cane sugar from the plantations of Fuju, shipped up the coast in cone-shaped loaves wrapped in palm-leaf. A cone of sugar is the universal gift at the quay; no deal is closed without one.
market.zayton.item.tea: Tea pressed into bricks and stamped with the producer's chop. The quayside merchants will trade a brick for a sack of pepper straight across, and both sides consider it a bargain.
npc.npc-kiovia-mentor.name: The Rune-Carver of Kiovia
npc.npc-kiovia-mentor.omen: He cuts marks into birch before every ford.
npc.npc-zayton-guide.name: Guide of Zayton
npc.npc-zayton-interpreter.name: Interpreter of Zayton
npc.npc-zayton-mentor.name: The Woman Who Reads the Slips
npc.npc-zayton-mentor.omen: She has read slips for forty years, and remembers every master who ignored one.
npc.npc-zayton-porter.name: Porter of Zayton
npc.npc-zayton-sailor.name: Sailor of Zayton
retainer.cambaluc-mentor.fate_0: This year, a former student now high in the Kaan's service will offer him a pardon. Accepting means returning to Cambaluc — the one city he has sworn never to enter again.
retainer.cambaluc-mentor.fate_1: The scholar's eyes are failing. By the end of the year, he will need a scribe to read him the oracle books.
retainer.cambaluc-mentor.name: Scholar Wang of the Hanlin
retainer.cambaluc-mentor.origin: A Hanlin academician who fell from favour at the Kaan's court after disputing the interpretation of an oracle. He now teaches the I Ching to anyone who will listen.
retainer.cambaluc-mentor.quest: Wang believes that the true text of the I Ching was lost when the Qin emperor burned the books, and that a fragment survives in a monastery in the Tangut mountains. He seeks a travelling companion to help him find it.
retainer.cambaluc-mentor.sign: His fingernails are stained black from years of grinding ink. He has not written a single character since the day he left the court.
retainer.camel-driver.fate_0: This year, Bekter will attempt his forty-first crossing. The desert is a jealous wife, he says; she does not like to let a man go.
retainer.camel-driver.fate_1: One of Bekter's camels has developed a strange white patch on its flank. The old man believes it is a mark of blessing, but the other drivers call it a curse.
retainer.camel-driver.name: Old Bekter
retainer.camel-driver.origin: A Bactrian camel-driver who has crossed the Great Desert forty times. He has more miles on his knees than most men have in their whole bodies. He speaks to his camels in a language only they understand.
retainer.camel-driver.quest: Bekter once buried a hoard of silver at a place in the desert whose location he can only find by the stars. He wants to retrieve it before he dies. He will need help carrying it out.
retainer.camel-driver.sign: He can taste the water in the air. When he says a well is dry, every man in the caravan believes him — he has never been wrong.
retainer.cotanese-weaver.fate_0: A carpet Gulbibi wove ten years ago has been recognised by a merchant in Cambaluc as the work of a 'master of Khotan.' Buyers are searching for her. Fame will find her this year — whether she wants it or not.
retainer.cotanese-weaver.fate_1: The indigo crop failed this year. Her blue thread is running out, and without it, her carpets cannot be sold as the finest grade.
retainer.cotanese-weaver.name: Gulbibi the Weaver
retainer.cotanese-weaver.origin: A master carpet-weaver from Khotan, who can draw from memory the pattern of any carpet she has seen for more than five minutes. Her hands are stained with madder, indigo, and walnut.
retainer.cotanese-weaver.quest: Gulbibi's mother taught her a pattern that no other weaver in Khotan knows — a prayer for safe journey encoded in knot-counts and colour sequences. She wants to weave one last copy of it before her eyes fail.
retainer.cotanese-weaver.sign: She ties one knot in every carpet wrong, deliberately. 'Only God makes things perfect,' she says.
retainer.guard-aleppo.fate_0: A scar on his shoulder aches before storms. This year, it will ache for three weeks straight — and the storm that follows will change everything.
retainer.guard-aleppo.fate_1: An old comrade from the Mamluk corps has become a bandit chief in the mountains of Anatolia. Yusuf will have to choose: join him, turn him in, or pretend he never heard the name.
retainer.guard-aleppo.name: Yusuf the Circassian
retainer.guard-aleppo.origin: A former Mamluk slave-soldier who bought his freedom in the markets of Aleppo. He fought in the Sultan's cavalry against the Franks and the Mongols.
retainer.guard-aleppo.quest: Yusuf seeks the man who taught him to fight — an old weapons-master who retired to a monastery in the Caucasus. He wants to return the broken sword and receive a new one.
retainer.guard-aleppo.sign: He carries a sword with a broken tip. The break, he says, was a mercy; the man it broke against lived.
retainer.kinsay-mentor.fate_0: This year, a client whose fortune she once read will return — not for another reading, but for her. He has been looking for twenty years.
retainer.kinsay-mentor.fate_1: Lin's chart shows a clash between her fire and the year's water. The southern sea roads are dangerous for her this year; the northern roads, however, will bring an unexpected inheritance.
retainer.kinsay-mentor.name: Lin Sanniang
retainer.kinsay-mentor.origin: A fortune-teller from the pleasure quarters of Kinsay, who read a hundred faces a day and never forgot one. She learned the Four Pillars from an old astrologer who took her in as a girl.
retainer.kinsay-mentor.quest: Lin's mentor died leaving a sealed box that can only be opened on the day her chart predicts. She carries it everywhere but has never opened it. The predicted day falls this year — somewhere on the road.
retainer.kinsay-mentor.sign: She never reads her own chart. 'The gods do not need to know I am watching back,' she says.
retainer.mazu-priestess.fate_0: A ship blessed by A-Mei three years ago has been sighted off the coast of Champa. Everyone aboard was given up for dead. Their return will be either a miracle or a scandal.
retainer.mazu-priestess.fate_1: The temple of Mazu needs a new roof. A-Mei must raise the funds this year, or the spring rains will ruin the goddess's image.
retainer.mazu-priestess.name: A-Mei of the Sea
retainer.mazu-priestess.origin: A priestess of Mazu at the great temple in Zayton. She has blessed a thousand ships and watched a hundred of them fail to return. Her eyes are old with the sea.
retainer.mazu-priestess.quest: A-Mei believes that Mazu's power is fading because the source of her blessing — a sacred spring on the island of Meizhou — has been polluted by a shipwreck. She seeks travellers to help her cleanse it.
retainer.mazu-priestess.sign: The incense she burns in the temple always drifts toward the sea, never toward the land. She says Mazu is calling.
retainer.nestorian-priest.fate_0: This year, Father Simeon will find what he has been looking for — but it will not be what he expected. The Prester John of legend is dead; only his descendants remain, ruling a small tribe in the Ordos.
retainer.nestorian-priest.fate_1: A Nestorian bishop in Cambaluc has accused Simeon of heresy. The road east may be closed to him this year.
retainer.nestorian-priest.name: Father Simeon
retainer.nestorian-priest.origin: A Nestorian priest from Mosul, travelling east in search of the Christian kingdom of Prester John. He has crossed the steppe twice and been turned back twice.
retainer.nestorian-priest.quest: Simeon believes that the Nestorian church in Cambaluc holds a Gospel written in the hand of St. Thomas himself. He wants to see it, touch it, and copy it before he dies.
retainer.nestorian-priest.sign: He carries a reliquary that contains, he says, a fragment of the True Cross. No one has ever seen him open it.
retainer.steppe-guide.fate_0: This year, a blizzard will test him as no blizzard has before. If he survives it, his confidence will carry the whole party.
retainer.steppe-guide.fate_1: Temur's clan will call him home this year for a marriage he cannot refuse. He may return — or he may not.
retainer.steppe-guide.name: Temur the Herder
retainer.steppe-guide.origin: A Mongol of the Keraite clan, raised on the steppe north of the Gobi. He can navigate by the stars, read the weather in the taste of the wind, and find water where no man sees any.
retainer.steppe-guide.quest: Temur's elder brother was taken by a rival clan in a raid ten years ago. He has heard a rumour that the man is alive, a slave in the markets of Samarcand. He will not ask for help, but his eyes search every face in every crowd.
retainer.steppe-guide.sign: He cannot enter a walled city without first circling its walls three times. An old steppe custom, he says.
retainer.tartar-messenger.fate_0: A message Altan is carrying this year contains news that will start a war. He does not know it yet — but if he reads it, he will have to decide whether to deliver it.
retainer.tartar-messenger.fate_1: The Kaan's post is expanding this year. A new station will open in a place where no messenger has gone before. Altan will be the first — or someone else will.
retainer.tartar-messenger.name: Altan the Arrow
retainer.tartar-messenger.origin: A Tartar courier of the Kaan's yam, the imperial post. He can ride two hundred miles in a day, changing horses at every station. He knows every post-house between Cambaluc and Samarcand.
retainer.tartar-messenger.quest: Altan's father was a courier who died carrying a message from the Kaan to the Ilkhan. The message was never delivered. Altan wants to find out what it said and whether it changed the course of a war.
retainer.tartar-messenger.sign: He never dismounts on the left side of a horse. The one time he did, the horse threw him and he broke three ribs.
retainer.tauris-merchant.fate_0: This year, a debt from his past will find him. Pay it or flee — either way, the road changes.
retainer.tauris-merchant.fate_1: Mirza's network of informants will bring word of a caravan that doubles its value by the time it reaches the sea.
retainer.tauris-merchant.name: Mirza of Tabriz
retainer.tauris-merchant.origin: A Persian merchant who once ran the Genoese fondaco in Tauris. He knows every language between Venice and Cambaluc, and the price of every goods.
retainer.tauris-merchant.quest: Mirza owes a sum of silver to a merchant-house in Hormuz. He will not speak of it, but he watches every ship that docks in every port. Help him settle the debt, and he will share his knowledge of the southern sea roads.
retainer.tauris-merchant.sign: He never sleeps with his back to a door. When asked why, he changes the subject.
retainer.venetian-clerk.fate_0: Pietro's gambling debt will catch up with him this year. A Venetian agent in Tauris has a warrant — or says he does.
retainer.venetian-clerk.fate_1: A merchant in Kinsay has noticed Pietro's handwriting and offered him a position keeping the books of a pepper fleet. The salary is a fortune; the temptation to embezzle is greater.
retainer.venetian-clerk.name: Pietro the Clerk
retainer.venetian-clerk.origin: A Venetian notary's apprentice who stowed away on a galley to escape a gambling debt. He has a beautiful hand for writing, a head for figures, and a complete inability to keep his mouth shut.
retainer.venetian-clerk.quest: Pietro wants to compose a book of his travels — a Merchants' Guide to the East, with prices, routes, and notes on every city. He needs to visit twelve more cities before he has enough material.
retainer.venetian-clerk.sign: He writes a letter to Venice every month and posts none of them. The stack in his saddlebag is a year thick.
retainer.zayton-mentor.fate_0: This year, the monsoon will arrive a week early. If he is at sea when it comes, his ship will outrun the storm. If he is in port, the harbour will be blocked for a month.
retainer.zayton-mentor.fate_1: A rival captain has challenged his monopoly on the Zayton-Hormuz route. Majid will need to prove his worth this year — or lose his ship.
retainer.zayton-mentor.name: Captain Majid of Zayton
retainer.zayton-mentor.origin: An Arab sea-captain who has made the voyage from Zayton to Hormuz thirty times. He knows every reef, every current, and every monsoon between the China Sea and the Persian Gulf.
retainer.zayton-mentor.quest: Twenty years ago, Majid lost a chest of pearls overboard in a storm off the coast of Champa. A diver recently claimed to have found it. Majid will detour a thousand miles on the rumour alone.
retainer.zayton-mentor.sign: He always consults the temple lots before setting sail. He has never ignored a lot in his life — and he has never been shipwrecked.
